An honest note on how that was found: the first transcription of those 172 bytes from the IDB was wrong
in the 106..125 region, and the first draft of this section claimed the two sets differed on six slots.
`audit_tables.py` caught it -- it compares the port's table against the image byte for byte -- and the
IDB re-read agrees with the image. The claim above is the corrected one.

### The four panels (0x6EA7C..0x6EE5C)

All four are `operator new(0x1BB4)` + `UiPanel_ctor(nRows)`, all nStyle 13 (+0xBE0), nFont 16 (+0x1B9C),
nPosY 70, +0x1B8C 70, style bytes 0..2 = 0xB4,0xB4,0xB4 and 6..11 = 0xF0,0xF0,0xF0,0x14,0x14,0x14.

| | global | x | +0x1B88 | viewW | extras |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | pManufProductPanel 0x15EE44 | 10 | 5 | 230 | click ManufScreen_SelectListed, bytes 3..5 = 0x32,0x32,0xFA, +0x1BA1 1, +0x1BB0 0x96 |
| B | pManufPanelB 0x15EE48 | 150 | 155 | 30 | +0x1BA4 2 |
| C | pManufPanelC 0x15EE40 | 187 | 185 | 30 | +0x1BA4 2 |
| D | pManufPanelD 0x15EE38 | 233 | 5 | 230 | click ManufScreen_SyncSelection, +0x1BA4 2, +0x1BA1 1, +0x1BB0 0x96 |

Only A gets `UiPanel_SetBytes3to5`. `bFlag7073` is 1 on all four because `UiPanel_ctor` sets it; only A
and D write it again. B and C keep the constructor's 0xFF at +0x1BB0.

### The four columns of a row

One row index is shared by all four panels.

  A line: the item's own name, copied out of `apObjects[id]` (the record's szName at +0, reached through
     the Map-block pointer array at 0x113AC0), cut to 17 characters when strlen is above 0x11 (0x6EF18
     `CMP R0,#0x11` / `STRBHI R3,[SP,#var_53]`, var_64+17). A's aux is the **slot id** (0x6EF64).
  C aux: the **topic index**, not the slot id -- 0x6EF70 stores R8, the outer loop counter.
  B line: `auManufCol[200*base + id]` as decimal (0x6EF9C `LDRH` at anchor + 400*base + 2*id + 17156),
     or the empty string at 0x10DA38 when it is zero.
  C line and D line both hang off `apProductB[200*base + id]` (0x6F038 `LDR [R0,#4]` at anchor +
     4*(200*base+id) + 4). Zero means both get the empty string (0x6F1C4). Otherwise:
       C = `100 * apProductA / (uManufWorkPerUnit * apProductB)` with "%" appended. The ARM composes
           _rt_sdiv with the DIVISOR in R0 (`MUL R0, R3, R1` at 0x6F068, work-per-unit times the asked-for
           count) and the DIVIDEND in R1 (`MUL R1, R2, #0x64` at 0x6F070) -- the argument order proved at
           0x65BD0/0x65BDC, and the same reading of the four columns CommitProduction established.
       D = `itoa(apProductB) + "/" + itoa(apProductA / uManufWorkPerUnit)` -- what was asked for, then the
           units the accumulated work has paid for (0x6F174 `LDRH [R2,#0xBA]`, _rt_sdiv at 0x6F178).

There is **no sort pass** here, unlike BuySellScreen_BuildPanels @ 0x76de0 and
TransferScreen_BuildPanels @ 0x96b30: the rows stay in topic order.

### IDB: aFacTypeTable was the research table under the wrong name

0x15EF08 was named `aFacTypeTable` and a second label `aResearchTopics` sat at 0x15EF0C with no
cross-references at all. The ARM settles it: `Research_TopicNeedsItem` does `MUL R3, R0, R3` (topic *
34) then `ADD R3, R3, =0x15EF08` (0x72CC0..0x72CC8), and this function does `ADD R2, R0, #0x22` for
topic 1 -- so the base is 0x15EF08 and the stride is 34, and 0x15EF0C is four bytes off a record
boundary. 0x15EF08 is now `aResearchTopics`, typed as 144 x a new local struct `ResearchTopicLive`:

    +0x00 abUnk0[4]   +0x04 wGate4   +0x06 wUnk6   +0x08 wTotal   +0x0A wProgress
    +0x0C bActive     +0x0D bUnlocked +0x0E nItemId
    +0x0F abUnkF[9]   +0x18 abItemIds[5]   +0x1D abUnk1D[5]

`bUnlocked` (+0xD) is the byte this function gates on, the byte `Unit_SelectBestFireMode` tests at
0x47A10 / 0x47B3C through `byte_AA968[ObjectRec.uSortKey]`, and the byte the tactical action-menu gate
reads at 0x17078..0x17094 -- the earlier notes called that one `aFacTypeTable[13 + 34 * ...]`, which is
this same table. `abItemIds` (+0x18..+0x1C) is named here for the first time: five object slot ids a
topic unlocks, used both as the abManufRowFlag index and as the apObjects index for the name. The
on-disk `ResearchTopic` order (pufo_save.h) and this in-memory order are still not mapped onto each
other; LoadGame is the function that would show it and it is not ported.

The port's `ResearchTopicLive.bGate13` was renamed to `bUnlocked` and its `abUnkF[19]` split into
`abUnkF[9]`, `abItemIds[5]`, `abUnk1D[5]`.

### Deviations

The original allocates the four panels with `operator new` and dereferences every allocation, every
panel pointer and every apObjects slot with no test; the port tests the object slots and bounds the row
index against the 500-line panel capacity. It indexes abManufRowFlag with the raw byte (LDRSB at
0x6EA50) and so reads past its 172 bytes for a slot id of 172 or more; the port refuses those. Both
divisions can be by zero and the original calls _rt_sdiv either way; the port answers zero --
unreachable in the shipped data, because every flagged slot has a non-zero work cost and only a flagged
slot gets a row. The teardown deletes the six click controls in the original and only frees their pads
in the port, because the port's controls are caller-owned.

IDB: `byte_AA548` -> `abManufRowFlag` with a data comment; `aFacTypeTable` @ 0x15EF08 ->
`aResearchTopics` typed `ResearchTopicLive[144]` with a data comment; the stale zero-xref
`aResearchTopics` label at 0x15EF0C cleared; function comment at 0x6e9e8.
## ManufScreen_Draw (0x6e3e0, 1332 B)

Ported as `ManufScreen_Draw` in `src/pufo/game/pufo_baseui.c` behind a `ManufDrawEnv`.

Installed as the click handler of the shared draw control `unk_186BB4` by `ManufScreen_Init` (`LDR R3,=ManufScreen_Draw` / `STR R3,[R0,#0xC]` at 0x71228), and called again from `Geoscape_CloseUI` case 8 at 0x8BD78 whenever `bManufProductSelected` is set. Both call sites discard the return value -- the original returns `Base_UpdateLabNeeded`'s loop-counter residue of 6 -- so the port returns void.

Where BuildPanels refreshes the whole product list, this refreshes the ONE row the cached cursor points at: the product id is `pManufProductPanel->anLineAux[nManufProductRowCache]` (0x6E40C).

- 0x6E410 / 0x6E424 / 0x6E430: `bManufProductSelected = 0`, panel A's `+0x1BA1` = 1, `Sound_Play(17)`. `Sound_Play` @ 0x9e0c0 reads only R0 -- its body is the sound-enabled byte, a `Game_RandU16(200)` and `FSOUND_PlaySound(-1, ...)` -- so the `MOV R1,#4` at 0x6E428 is register residue, not a second argument.
- 0x6E478: `aManufProductB[200*base + product] == 0` calls `ManufScreen_ClearProductSlot(&unk_159E98, base, product & 0xFF)`. The mask is `AND R2,R3,#0xFF` at 0x6E484 while the index itself uses the unmasked product.
- 0x6E4E4..0x6E51C: the seed. `apProductA[idx] == 0` AND `apProductB[idx] != 0` AND `auManufCol[idx] != 0` together store 1 into `apProductA[idx]` (`MOVNE R11,#1` / `STRNE R11,[R4,LR]` with R4 = anchor + 4*idx and LR = anchor + 4). A product that has a quantity and allocated engineers but no accumulated work starts with one unit of it. 0x6E6D4 reloads `apProductA` from memory afterwards, so a seeded row goes down the percent path with that unit in it rather than the empty-string one.
- 0x6E52C..0x6E5A8: the hangar branch, and it is DEAD. `LDR R11,[SP,#var_4C]` / `LDR R11,[R11]` reads the dword at panel A offset 0 (var_4C is the panel pointer, stored at 0x6E4A8), and 0x6E530 / 0x6E538 test it for `> 118 && < 122` -- the three hangar products 119..121. Nothing in the binary writes a product id there: BuildPanels leaves panel A's style bytes at B4 B4 B4 32 32 FA, so the dword reads as 0x32B4B4B4, and `UiPanel_ClickRow` and `UiScrollList_TrackHold` store the clicked row into the dword at panel offset 12. The branch therefore never runs, and the selected base's byte in the eight-byte table at 0x159DBC is never raised by the craft count the player asked for. Recorded in bugs.tsv. What it would do: `apBases[base]->bUnk4` (0x6E5A4) -> `BaseGrid_GetByte0x654` (0x6E558) -> write back that byte plus the LOW BYTE of `apProductB[idx]` (`LDRB [R3,#0x1904]` at 0x6E58C, `ADD R2,R3,R0` at 0x6E590) through `BaseGrid_SetByteAtFound` (0x6E5A8).
- 0x6E5EC..0x6E6A0: panel B's line for the row = `auManufCol[idx]` (`LDRH [anchor + 2*idx + 17156]`), or the empty string at 0x10DA38 when it is zero.
- 0x6E6D4..0x6E8E0: when `apProductA[idx] != 0`, panel C = `100 * apProductA / (uManufWorkPerUnit * apProductB)` with `%` appended -- divisor `MUL R0,R3,R2` at 0x6E708, dividend `MUL R1,R3,R2` with R2 = 0x64 at 0x6E714, `_rt_sdiv` at 0x6E718, the same divisor-in-R0 reading BuildPanels and CommitProduction gave -- and panel D = `itoa(apProductB)` (0x6E7A0) then `/` (0x6E7E8) then `itoa(apProductA / uManufWorkPerUnit)` (0x6E83C..0x6E848). Otherwise both get the empty string. The guard here is `apProductA != 0` where BuildPanels guards on `apProductB != 0`; the clear at 0x6E48C has already zeroed the slot when the quantity is zero, so the empty-string path is reached through `apProductA` being zero.
- 0x6E8F4 / 0x6E908: `Base_UpdateWorkshopNeeded` then a tail `Base_UpdateLabNeeded` on the selected base -- the same pair `ResearchScreen_ConfirmAndCache` ends with. The originals call `Base_CountActiveManuf` and `Base_CountActiveResearch` inside themselves; the port passes the counts in, taken from `auManufCol[200*base..]` and `auResearchCol[144*base..]` with the shared entry-count byte at 0x160C4C.

Deviations. The original bounds nothing: an out-of-panel row, an out-of-range base index or a product past 199 indexes the 1600-entry columns and `apBases` blindly. The port reads the aux cell only for a row inside the panel, skips the table work when the composed index is outside 0..1599, and dereferences `apBases` only for a base inside the array; the two tail passes still run either way, which the test asserts. Both divisions can be by zero in the original and the port answers zero, the same policy BuildPanels and CommitProduction record. The port returns void where the original returns 6.

Test: `tests/test_baseui.c:TestManufDraw`, 42 checks, on panels built by the real `ManufScreen_BuildPanels` so the aux column and panel A's style bytes are the ones the screen itself leaves. It asserts the sample, the two flag stores, the clear path (accumulated work, committed units and allocated work all go to zero while the neighbouring row is untouched), the seed, the percent and unit lines for a normal row and for the zero-work row, that the offset-0 dword is 0x32B4B4B4 and leaves the 0x159DBC byte alone, that forcing it to 118/122 still leaves it alone while 120 and 121 take the branch and store the byte-wrapped sum, the two tail passes with the real budget (110 allocated work buys exactly three of five workshops, and the lab pass with no active research clears the lab cell), that an out-of-panel row does no table work but still runs the tail passes, and that a null environment or null panel does nothing at all.

## ManufScreen_DrawFrame (0x6f9a4, 5400 B)

Ported as `ManufFrameEnv` + `ManufScreen_DrawFrame` in `src/pufo/game/pufo_baseui.c`. It returns
void in the port; the original returns the shortfall value, which `Geoscape_Draw` at 0x941A0 drops.

Rails, 0x6F9C4..0x6FB54. Twenty-four steps of 7 at x 5 and x 234, at y 7k+1 and 7k+151, with the
climbing colour `5*(k+20)` (100..215) and the falling one `0xE6-5k` (230..115); then twenty-four
steps of 5 at y 5 and y 315, at x 5k+1 and 5k+119, climbing `5*(k+20)` and falling `0xFA-5k`
(250..135). The two halves of a side rail overlap at y 151..168 and the climbing half is issued
later, so at (5,151) the climbing colour (index 205) is what survives -- reproduced, and checked.

Band and panels. The band is `16 * min(nLineCount, nStyle)` (0x6FC78). With the panels built the
four `UiPanel_DrawText` calls come first, then colour (250,250,250/0,0,0), TEXTS[1173] at (10,52),
the base name from `BaseSiteRec[base] + 26` centred at (120 - w/2, 13), then the map-cursor row's
object name at (10,300) in (150,150,250/0,0,0). That name is gated on `!bManufProductSelected`,
`bBaseFacPreviewOk` and `70 < nSmapCursorY < 70 + band`, and its row comes from PANEL D's row
cursor at +0xBD8 indexing panel A's aux column at +0x13B4 -- not from panel A's own cursor. Three
separators 1 x (band+2) at x 130, 152 and 187, index 0xB4.

No product selected (0x70D84): blit the reset control, colour (68,244,252/4,70,75), shortfall block.

Selected: `Ui_AnimExpandBlit(0, 30, 236, 284, 4, 0x28, 0x2D, 0xC8, 3)`. On false the frame sets
(220,80,80/50,30,30), then (68,244,252/4,70,75), runs the shortfall block and stops. On true: the
name centred at (120 - w/2, 45); `itoa(uManufWorkPerUnit)` + TEXTS[1349] at (10,69); TEXTS[1174] at
(10,83); TEXTS[1175] + `itoa(dtoi(price * 0.7))` + "$" at (10,97). The 0.7 is the double the ARM
builds at 0x6FFBC/0x6FFC4 from 0x66666666 / 0x3FE66666; `ManufScreen_CommitProduction` uses 1.4 for
the same `anObjectPriceInit`, so the screen quotes half of what committing costs.

Components, 0x7002C..0x7073C: `for (nCase = 0; nCase < 4; ++nCase)`, and a zero
`abManufComponents[nCase]` skips WITHOUT advancing the row counter -- the rows stack only where
something is asked for. The headers TEXTS[1176]/TEXTS[1177] are drawn inside the loop, centred at
(140 - w/2, 114) and (200 - w/2, 114). Row y = 130 + 14 * rows_drawn. The component name is
TEXTS[439]/[505]/[497]/[498] and the stock is `apObjects[105]/[106]/[107]/[109]->auPerBaseVal[base]`
-- the four component slots `ManufScreen_CommitProduction` already gates on, so the pairing is
confirmed from two independent places. When required > available the colour becomes
(20*(nMapPhase+5), 10, 10 / 50, 0, 0) and `bManufQtyGate` is raised.

Crew and capacity, 0x70740..0x709F4: TEXTS[1178] + `Base_GetEngineerCount(apObjects[112],
auManufCol + 200*base, base, nEntryCount)` at (10,185); TEXTS[1179] + `(Base_CalcWorkshopCap -
Base_CountActiveManuf)` at (10,199); colour (150,150,255/20,20,120); TEXTS[1180] at (10,216);
TEXTS[1182] at (140,216); TEXTS[1181] + `auManufCol[idx]` at (10,230); TEXTS[1183] +
`aManufProductB[idx]` at (140,230).

Buttons, 0x709F8..0x70D08: TEXTS[1142] at (38,251) and (170,251), TEXTS[1143] at (38,271) and
(170,271); the last four of the six arrow controls blit; then `unk_186B94` is MOVED to (94,251) and
its `pfnClick` re-pointed to `ManufScreen_UpdateProgress`, and `unk_186B90` to (94,271) with
`ManufScreen_ReduceSelectedQtyToOne`, every frame. TEXTS[1604] centred at (114 - w/2, 252);
TEXTS[1711] centred at (113 - w/2, 272) -- record 1711 is past the 1650 records lang.dat loads, so
that button's label draws empty in the shipped build. Then the draw control with TEXTS[1127] ("OK")
centred at (73 - w/2, 295) and the confirm control with TEXTS[1144] ("Cancel") at (164 - w/2, 295).

Shortfall, 0x70DB8..0x70EB4, reached from all three exits: only when `byte_1870C8 == 1`. Reason 0
draws `Ui_AnimExpandBlit_IfEnabled(20, 130, 200, 70, 1)` plus TEXTS[1184] centred at
(120 - w/2, 158); reason 1 the same panel with TEXTS[1185]; any other value nothing.

Every one of the 22 label addresses is a TEXTS.DAT record: the ARM builds each as
`LDR R0, =(<addr> - 0xB38D0)` against R8 = 0xB38D0, so `addr - 0xB38D0 = 205 * n`. The texts of all
22 were read out of lang.dat and are what the `PUFO_MANUF_TEXT_*` names record; the four component
captions decode to "Elerium-115", "Alien alloys", "UFO power source", "UFO navigation", which is
independent confirmation of the component-to-slot pairing.

Deviations: none of behaviour. The port guards the panel, object, grid and site arrays the original
indexes blindly, and it keeps the two quantity controls' handlers as environment inputs rather than
naming the callees at the call site.

Test: `TestManufDrawFrame` in `tests/test_baseui.c`, 69 checks, all on a real 240 x 320 16 bpp
surface with the real FONT.SPR and the real TEXTS.DAT layout. The rails are checked as exact 565
values at exact coordinates, including the rise/fall overlap at (5,151) and the bottom rail winning
over the side rail at (5,315). The separators are checked at (130,118) and (130,119), which is what
pins the band to `16 * min(nLineCount, nStyle)` rather than `16 * nLineCount`. The cursor-row gate
is checked by drawing the name and then removing one condition at a time. The price is checked by
rebuilding the band from a reference (the same detail-panel frame, then the label) and comparing it
pixel-for-pixel against "700$", and against "701$", "699$" and "700" to show it is not those; then
1428 -> "999$" and 1429 -> "1000$", which pins the factor to 0.7 within 1/1428. The component rows
are compared between a three-component and a four-component product: the fourth row appears only in
the second, and the first two rows are identical in both. The short-component colour is compared
between nMapPhase 0 and 5. The controls are checked through the injected blit seam: eight blits in
slot order, and the two quantity controls found at (94,251) and (94,271) afterwards.

## ResearchScreen_Init (0x749a8, 592 B)

Ported as `ResearchInitEnv` + `ResearchScreen_Init` in `src/pufo/game/pufo_baseui.c`. It is the
research screen's bring-up and the twin of `ManufScreen_Init`, with three differences that matter.

Four controls, not six. Research has no engineers pair: the four slots at `ppScreen + 0x1D48 + 4*i`
(array indices 1874..1877) take PanelPrev, PanelNext, IncSelectedQty, DecSelectedQty, and the four
descriptors at `g_aResearchCtlDesc` (0xABB10, renamed from `stru_ABB10`) are the topic-list scroll
pair at (205, 18) / (205, 38) -- the same offsets the manufacturing tab pair uses -- and the quantity
pair at (10, 163) / (10, 183).

The two shared bottom controls are re-pointed, not re-allocated, and the research screen points them
the other way round from the manufacturing one: `unk_186BB4` gets `ResearchScreen_CancelSelectedAndClose`
and `unk_186BB0` gets `ResearchScreen_StartSelected`, where `ManufScreen_Init` gives BB4 its OK button
and BB0 its cancel. They are generic geoscape controls and each screen re-points them.

Handlers first, positions last. `unk_186BB4` and `unk_186BB0` get their `pfnClick` at 0x74AC4 / 0x74AD0
but their coordinates only at 0x74B98..0x74BB4, after the rebuild call and the topic walk: BB4 to
(165, 188) and BB0 to (165, 166), one above the other in the same column. The test proves the order by
having the rebuild hook record the cancel control's position -- it is still the value the test preset.

The topic walk, 0x74B08..0x74B8C: for `i` in `0..nResearchEntryCount-1`, if
`aResearchTopics[i].bActive` is zero then `auResearchCol[144*nSelectedBaseIdx + i] = 0`. The base index
is `LDRSB` of `abFacilityGrid + 0x619` sign-extended through the usual `LSL #24 / ASR #24` pair, and
the count byte is re-read from memory on every iteration. Deviation: the original bounds only by the
count byte (a byte, so up to 255 of the 144 entries) and passes the base index through untested; the
port stops at the table size and refuses a base index outside the eight columns.

The tail call. `ResearchScreen_Init` is the only one of the four research entry points that refreshes
the three panels itself (0x74BC4 -> `ResearchScreen_RefreshPanels` over unk_160C68 / unk_15EEFC /
unk_15EF00) rather than leaving it to a handler; `ResearchScreen_StartSelected` does the same thing
mid-screen. The test proves the refresh runs after the panel build by having the build hook record
panel 1's `nLineCount` -- it is still the preset 99.

`Research.pad` loads in mode 6 (0x749DC), is the 240 x 320 member of main.dat, and its two origins are
zeroed at 0x749EC / 0x74A00 -- PadImage +0 and +4, which Hex-Rays renders as `->x` and `->uWidth`
because it types the slot as `UiControl *`.

Deviations: the original allocates the pad and the four controls with `operator new` and derefs every
allocation with no test; the port takes caller-owned controls into `ppRoot[1..4]` as the manufacturing,
buy/sell and transfer inits do. `ResearchScreen_RebuildTopicList` (0x74270) and
`ResearchScreen_BuildPanels` (0x733f4) are not ported yet and arrive as hooks.

Test: `TestResearchInit` in `tests/test_baseui.c`, 54 checks. The pad is loaded from the real main.dat
and checked for its size and mode; the four controls are checked in their slots, their handlers and
their descriptor positions (205/18, 205/38, 10/163, 10/183); the walk is checked against eight topics
with four active -- the inactive allocations are cleared, the active ones survive, entry 8 past the
count byte survives, and base 0's column is untouched; the two bottom controls are checked for handler
and position; and three hooks record the state when they ran, which is what pins the order.

## ResearchScreen_BuildPanels (0x733f4, 1600 B)

Ported as `ResearchBuildEnv` + `ResearchScreen_BuildPanels` in `src/pufo/game/pufo_baseui.c`. Build or
teardown of the research screen's three panels, chosen by `byte_160C7C`. The twin of
`ManufScreen_BuildPanels`, with three differences.

**The filter is `bActive`, not `bUnlocked` plus `abManufRowFlag`.** Manufacturing lists the items an
unlocked topic can produce; research lists the topics themselves, and `bActive` is already the
"this topic is on the screen list" flag that `ResearchScreen_RebuildTopicList` maintains. There is no
object array here at all.

**The topic's name is `TEXTS[topic + 4]`.** 0x7373C `LDRH R3,[R10,#4]`, 0x73744 `MOV R2,#0xCD` /
`MUL R2,R3,R2`, 0x73748 `ADD R1,R2,R0` with R0 = 0xB38D0. The u16 at record +0x4 therefore carries two
meanings: the weapon fire gate reads it as a value, this reads it as a TEXTS.DAT record index. Neither
use is a mistake, and the port's `wGate4` name now documents both.

**The percentage is computed the other way round from `ResearchScreen_RefreshPanels`.** Here it is
`100 * (wProgress / wTotal)`: 0x73834 `LDRH R1,[R10,#0xA]` as the dividend, 0x73850 `LDRH R0,[R10,#8]`
as the divisor, `_rt_sdiv`, then 0x73870 `MUL R0,R3,#0x64` on the **quotient**. RefreshPanels at 0x73168
multiplies **first** (`MUL R1,R2,#0x64`) and divides after. A topic one quarter done reads "0%" from
this function and "25%" from that one. Recorded in `docs/parity/bugs.tsv` and reproduced; the test shows
both numbers from the same topic and the same data.

**The screen block is the topic table.** `ResearchScreen_Init`'s `ppScreen` is 0x15EF08, so the screen's
pad lives in `aResearchTopics[0]`'s first four bytes, the four controls at 0x15EF08 + 0x1D48 =
0x160C50..0x160C5C, and `pResearchTopicPanel` @ 0x160C68 is exactly one 34-byte record past the end of
the 144-record table. That is why the teardown reaches them as `*(void **)aResearchTopics[0].abUnk0` and
as `&aResearchTopics[220].abUnkF[1] + 4*i` (220 * 34 + 0x10 = 0x1D48).

Build path: flag set; `aResearchTopics[0].bActive = 1` (topic 0 is always on the list); three
`UiPanel_ctor(144)` -- constructed with the full 144 rows, not the row count, which is only written into
`nLineCount` at the end. All three share nStyle 15 (not the manufacturing 13), nFont 16, nPosY 70,
nUnk7056 70, bytes 0..2 = B4 B4 B4 and bytes 6..11 = F0 F0 F0 14 14 14. Panel A is x 10 width 230 with
nUnk7052 5, bytes 3..5 = 32 32 FA, bFlag7073, bUnk7088 = 0x94 (the manufacturing panels use 0x96) and the
click handler `PlaySample7_SetFlags_Cache0xBD8`, which is what caches the row cursor into 0x160C74 that
the two quantity buttons read. Panel B is x 197 width 30 with nUnk7052 175 and nUnk7076 = 2; panel C is
x 233 width 30 with nUnk7052 205 and nUnk7076 = 2 -- the two narrow right-aligned numeric columns.

Fill pass: topics 1..count-1 with `bActive == 1`. Panel A gets the name and `anLineAux[row]` = the topic
number; panel B gets `itoa(auResearchCol[144*base + topic])` or the empty string at 0x10DA38; panel C
gets the percentage plus "%" or the empty string. The row counter advances only for an active topic, and
all three panels end with `nLineCount` = that counter.

Teardown: flag cleared; the three `nLineCount = 144` stores come **first**, before anything is released;
the pad's data freed and the pad deleted; the three panels freed in A, B, C order; then the four
controls' pads freed and the controls deleted.

Deviations: the original bounds the walk only by the count byte (a byte, so up to 255 of the 144 topics)
and writes `apLines[row]` with no test; the port stops at the table. It also skips the progress store when
`wTotal` is zero, where the original would divide by zero -- the same policy as `RefreshPanels`.

Test: `TestResearchBuildPanels` in `tests/test_baseui.c`, 48 checks. Every panel coordinate, width, style
byte group and the 0x94/0x96 difference is asserted; the four rows, their names, their aux topic numbers
and their quantity strings are asserted; the percentage is asserted as "0%" for a quarter-done topic and
then the same panels are refreshed and the same row asserted as "25%", which is the divergence itself;
and the teardown is asserted through the panel slots, the root pad slot and the four controls' pad
pointers going to null, followed by a rebuild that proves the flag drives both directions.

## ResearchScreen_RebuildTopicList (0x74270, 1700 B)

Ported as `ResearchScreen_RebuildTopicList` in `src/pufo/game/pufo_baseui.c`; the argument block is
`ResearchRebuildEnv` in `pufo_baseui.h`; `TestResearchRebuild` in `tests/test_baseui.c` adds 160
checks.

**The argument is the topic table.** 0x742E4 writes `*(_BYTE *)(result + 4875) = 1`, and
4875 = 143 * 34 + 13 is `aResearchTopics[143].bUnlocked`. All three callers (ResearchScreen_Init
0x74B00, ResearchScreen_StartSelected 0x73310, ResearchScreen_AccumulateAllocated 0x749A0) pass
0x15EF08.

**Block 1 (0x74294).** When record 143 is locked, the bUnlocked of the five prerequisite topics
listed at record 143 +0x13..0x17 is ANDed into a byte product (AND R2,R2,#0xFF after each MUL) and
the record unlocks only when the product is exactly 1. A prerequisite holding 2 gives 2 and the test
fails; both cases are asserted.

**The walk (0x74314)** is `for (n = 1; n < nResearchEntryCount; ++n)`: topic 0 is the screen block,
not a topic. main.dat really loads 144 (test_geoiinit asserts the same byte), so the last iteration
is topic 143.

**The gate at 0x74364** runs unless `bUnlocked == 0 && wTotal > 0`, and a failure skips the whole
iteration (0x74388 BEQ loc_748EC). Because `Research_TopicNeedsItem` answers 0 for every topic
outside 55..65 and 118..142 (and for 135, 140 and >= 143), most topics are skipped outright. With
object 7 stocked with 3 units, exactly topics 55, 56 and 57 get through: each spends a unit at
0x743E8 and topic 58 finds the stock at zero. One dataset pins the bands, the gate, the spend and the
skip in a single run.

**Split at 0x74394** on `wTotal > wProgress`.

*In progress* (0x747A0): the gate is the AND of the five prerequisites' bUnlocked, and the same five
bytes are also ADDED into an accumulator -- the original adds the topic NUMBERS, not any count. The
accumulator only feeds the `!= 0` test at 0x748E0, so the oddity cannot change an outcome, but it is
reproduced. The five needed-item bytes at +0x0E..0x12 (0x747E4) clear the gate when they are 254 or
255, and a real id `<= Map_nObjectCount` whose `apObjects[id]->auPerBaseVal[base]` is zero clears the
gate AND writes bActive = 0 (0x74854); an id above the object count is skipped without derefing. Then
the second range pair, `aTopics[n+1]` +0x24/+0x25: lo2 + hi2 + accumulator must be non-zero, and when
lo2 != hi2 some topic in [lo2, hi2] must already be unlocked or already marked in abResearchZero
(0x74894..0x748C8). bActive = 1 only when the gate survived and that sum is non-zero -- the four
variants (all good, one item empty, nothing unlocked in the range, sum zero) are each asserted.

*Finished* (0x743A4): the item spend and `wProgress = 0` are a pair, both skipped when the topic needs
no item, so a topic that needs nothing keeps its wProgress (asserted: 10 stays 10). Then bUnlocked = 1,
nResearchFinishedTopic = n (byte, 0x74414), nResearchTopicShown = n (dword, 0x74424), the eight
per-base allocation entries cleared, the shortfall dword set to 1, the facility flag, one message line
appended with flag 37 and colours n / 0xFF / 0xFF / 0xFF, bActive dropped when the item is missing,
abResearchZero[n] = 1, and the five topics at +0x1D..0x21 switched to bActive = 1.

**The topic -> facility-kind permutation.** Both switches (0x74460, 0x74668) switch on the topic
number with cases 37..53 and write 1 into `aBaseFacFlags[kind].bFlag20` (0x186E48 + 28*kind + 0x14):
37->0, 38->1, 39->2, 40->3, 41->4, 42->5, 43->13, 44->6, 45->7, 46->14, 47->none, 48->15, 49->16,
50->12, 51->10, 52->8, 53->9. Case 10's jumptable entry is the default label, which is also where the
other sixteen land -- so the Append and the SetLine run for every walked topic, not only the mapped
ones. FAC_HANGAR (11, record 0x186F90) is the kind no topic ever writes. LoadGame @ 0x4539C carries
the same seventeen-entry table over the same base with the same -37 offset and the same unmapped case
10, which is what pins the mapping down. The test asserts three specific kinds, the hangar's absence,
and that exactly three of the seventeen flags are set.

**The range pairs live in the NEXT record.** The roll's (lo,hi) is `aTopics[n+1].abUnk0[0..1]`
(0x745AC LDRB [R9,#0x22], 0x745C0 LDRB [R9,#0x23]) and the availability pair is
`aTopics[n+1].abUnk0[2..3]` (0x74868). The record being tested is `aTopics[n]`, so the ranges sit one
record later; for n == 143 they are 0x160228, the four-byte gap between the 144-record table and
auResearchCol @ 0x16022C, which has no cross-reference anywhere in the IDB. No other function reads
these four bytes of a record, so the pairing is visible only here. The port reads zeros there, which
makes lo == hi and skips the roll for the last topic -- asserted by showing that a full 144-entry walk
in which topic 143 finishes unlocks nothing.

**The roll (0x745AC).** Game_RandU16(hi - lo + 1), retried while the landing topic is already active
or already unlocked, up to 50 tries; at 50 the original accepts whatever it landed on (0x7460C). With
every candidate in [10,13] pre-unlocked, the test seeds the RNG so the first and the fiftieth draws
differ and asserts that the accepted topic is the fiftieth -- which fails if the cap is 49 or 51.

**Deviation found (0x74648).** The column clear after the roll is `MOV R0,R7`, and R7 still holds
`&auResearchCol[nTopic]` from 0x74428; the rolled index was used only for the bUnlocked store and for
nResearchTopicShown. So the finished topic's eight entries are cleared twice and the newly unlocked
topic's never. ResearchScreen_AccumulateAllocated (0x74914) books auResearchCol[i] into wProgress for
every i below the entry count, locked topics included, so a locked topic really can arrive at its
unlock carrying a non-zero allocation. Recorded in bugs.tsv and reproduced.

**The line rewrite (0x7474C).** When abResearchZero[lo + roll] is zero, the line the finished branch
just appended is overwritten in place at index (nLineCount - 1) with flag 37 and colours
n / roll / 0xE8 / 0; abResearchZero[lo + roll] = 1 follows unconditionally. The test pins the roll to
a seeded value and asserts slots 1..3 become roll / 0xE8 / 0 while the later lines keep 0xFF, and a
second run where the picked topic was already marked shows the rewrite skipped.

**Deviations.** The original derefs the topic table, the object pointers, the count byte and the line
list with no test. The port returns the entry count where the original returns its own argument (the
0x15EF08 anchor) when the count is 0 or 1 -- the callers expect an i32 and the port cannot carry a
pointer in it. The port reads the 0x160228 gap as zero.

**IDB.** `unk_15EEF8` renamed `nResearchFinishedTopic`, `unk_160C60` renamed `nResearchTopicShown`.
`ResearchTopicLive` fields renamed: `nItemId` plus `abUnkF[9]` became `abNeedItems[5]` (+0x0E..0x12)
and `abPreTopics[5]` (+0x13..0x17), and `abUnk1D[5]` became `abActivateTopics[5]`. Comments at 0x74270,
0x74460 and 0x4539C.

## ResearchScreen_Draw (0x73a34, 2108 B)

Ported as src/pufo/game/pufo_baseui.c:ResearchScreen_Draw, declared over a ResearchDrawEnv in
pufo_baseui.h. Its only caller is Geoscape_Draw's screen-id-8 case (0x94114 loads R0 with 0x15EF08, the
topic table itself, and 0x94124 overwrites the result with 0), so the port returns void. Tested by
tests/test_baseui.c section "the research screen's frame" (69 checks) on the real 240x320 surface with
the real font and the real research.pad.

Order, from the ARM. 0x73A3C `LDR R0,[R0]` + PadImage_Blit: the screen pad pointer lives in the first
four bytes of aResearchTopics[0], because the screen block IS the topic table. This is the one frame of
the three research/manuf/transfer frames that blits its pad -- ManufScreen_DrawFrame opens straight into
the rails. 0x73A44..0x73BE0: the rails, 24 side steps of 7 (CMP #0xA8) and 24 top/bottom steps of 5
(CMP #0x78), with the climbing index 5*(k+20) and the falling ones 0xE6-5k and 0xFA-5k stored through
STRB, so each of the three index arguments is the low byte. The three originals carry the same 96 blits
with the same constants, so the port draws them from one BaseUi_DrawFrameRails helper shared with
TransferScreen_Draw and ManufScreen_DrawFrame.

0x73BE8: bResearchPanelsBuilt (was byte_160C7C) == 0 ends the function -- no panels, no labels, not even
the close control. 0x73BFC..0x73C14: the three panels' text, topic / B / C. 0x73C34: the white pair,
TEXTS[1138] at (10, 52), then the selected site's 64-byte name from 0x186C5A + 64 * nSelectedBaseIdx
centred at (120 - w/2, 13). 0x73D00..0x73D60: two 1-pixel column separators at x 170 and x 200, y 69,
index 0xB4, height 16 * min(nLineCount, nStyle) + 2 of the TOPIC panel -- note it is nStyle that caps
the band, not the row cursor.

0x73D64: bUiRowSelected (was unk_160C80) == 0 blits the shared close control g_pUiCloseCtl and returns.
That is the only path in the function that blits the close control: with a topic row selected the close
pad is never redrawn here. The flag is set by panel A's click handler PlaySample7_SetFlags_Cache0xBD8
(0x73328) and cleared by ResearchScreen_StartSelected (0x73244). 0x73DA0: Ui_AnimExpandBlit over the
anim root 0x1864F8 at (0, 110) 236x100, index 0x32, source (0x96, 0x32), key 0x96, mode 4; only the low
byte of the result is tested (0x73DA8) and a false result leaves through the same tail.

0x73DBC..0x73E64: TEXTS[1139] at (10, 118), TEXTS[1140] at (10, 132), TEXTS[1141] at (10, 146).
0x73E8C: the teal pair 68,244,252 / 4,70,75, then TEXTS[1142] at (40, 164) and TEXTS[1143] at (40, 184).
0x73F24..0x74068: white pair, then three j_itoa numbers at x 195 -- Base_GetScientistCount at y 118,
Base_CalcLabCap - Base_CountActiveResearch at y 132, and auResearchCol[anLineAux[0x160C74] + 144*base]
at y 146, the row index being the cursor 0x160C74 that panel A's click handler caches.

0x7406C..0x7408C: two UiControl_BlitActivePad calls whose pointers come from `&aResearchTopics[0].wTotal
+ 1874` advanced by two u16 slots, i.e. screen-block control slots 1876 and 1877 at 0x160C58 and
0x160C5C -- the IncSelectedQty and DecSelectedQty controls ResearchScreen_Init installed. 0x7409C:
unk_186BB4 (cancel, parked at (165, 188)), the teal pair, TEXTS[1144] centred at (198 - w/2, 189).
0x74120: unk_186BB0 (start, (165, 166)), TEXTS[1127] centred at (198 - w/2, 167) -- the caption pair is
swapped against the controls' own order, "OK" under the upper control and the cancel caption under the
lower one. 0x74184..0x741A4: unk_186B94 is re-pointed at ResearchScreen_UpdateProgress and moved to
(100, 164) every frame, then blitted; TEXTS[1604] centred at (119 - w/2, 165) is the return value.

The nine labels are direct pointers into aTextRecs (stride 205): 0xEC81A, 0xEC8E7, 0xEC9B4, 0xECA81,
0xECB4E, 0xECC1B, 0xECCE8, 0xEBF4B and 0x103D44 are records 1138, 1139, 1140, 1141, 1142, 1143, 1144,
1127 and 1604. 1127/1142/1143/1144/1604 are the same records the manufacturing frame uses for its own
buttons; only the positions differ. research.pad loads 240x320 in mode 6, the MOV R2,#6 at 0x749DC.

Deviation: the original copies every label into a 104-byte stack buffer with an unbounded
byte-at-a-time loop, builds the three numbers through a second 52-byte buffer, derefs the three panels,
the four screen-block controls, the three shared controls and the colour root with no test, and indexes
anLineAux with the cached row cursor without bounds. The port bounds the label buffer, null-guards the
panels and controls, and clamps the row read the way ResearchScreen_IncSelectedQty does. The test also
shows the pen Text_DrawString paints with is the SECOND triple of the packed pair: the white pair
250,250,250 / 0,0,0 draws black text, and the teal captions come out as 4,70,75.

## BuySellScreen_Draw (0x77e6c, 3524 B)

Ported as src/pufo/game/pufo_baseui.c:BuySellScreen_Draw over a BuySellDrawEnv in pufo_baseui.h, and
tested by tests/test_baseui.c section "the buy/sell screen's frame" (100 checks) on the real 240x320
surface with the real font. Called from Geoscape_Draw's buy/sell screen-id case (0x93E10); the result is
register residue and the caller discards it, so the port returns void.

**The frame splits on bBuySellPanelsBuilt @ 0x161A28 and the two halves are not the same drawing.** They
share the rails, the close control, the funds line, the site name, the five panel draws, the four column
separators and the "no row under the cursor" tail, but they differ in four places: the total line is
TEXTS[157] "Èòîãî" in the 255,120,120 pair on the not-built half and TEXTS[411] "Âûðó÷êà " in
120,120,255 on the built half; the two column captions swap sides (TEXTS[92] "ÍÎÊ-âî" centred on 210 and
TEXTS[158] "Öåíà" on 155, against 145 and 212); the separators move from x 130/176/191/206 to
130/160/175/190; and the shortfall panel exists only on the not-built half.

Common head, 0x77E80..0x78150: the shared rails, then UiControl_BlitActivePad(g_pUiCloseCtl)
unconditionally -- the opposite of ResearchScreen_Draw, which blits the close control only when no row
is selected. Then TEXTS[156] "Äåíüãè: " + itoa(nFunds) + " $" at (10, 28), where Text_MeasureWidth runs
at 0x780B4 and its result is thrown away, and the selected site's name centred at (120 - w/2, 10).

Not-built half, 0x786BC..0x78B94: bBuySellControlsBuilt @ 0x161A24 == 0 ends it. Otherwise the total
line, the two captions, then the only bFlag7073 writes in the function -- panels B and C get
(dword at byte_1870C8 != 1) -- and both get bUnk7080 = bPanelFlagScratch (was unk_161F0C), which is
zeroed after the copy. Five UiPanelMsg_Draw in the order A, E, C, B, D. Band = 16 *
min(panelB->nLineCount, panelB->nStyle); separators 1 pixel wide at y 69, height band + 2, index 0xB4.
Then 220,80,80 / 50,30,30 and, if the shortfall dword is 1, a switch on dword_1870B4[0]: reasons 0..3
run Ui_AnimExpandBlit_IfEnabled(20, 130, 200, 70, 1) and draw TEXTS[405 + reason] centred at
(120 - w/2, 158) and return; the default breaks into the cursor block, so reason 4 gets no panel at all.

Built half, 0x78180..0x78420: the scratch byte only, no bFlag7073 write; the blue total line; the
captions on the other sides; the same five panels; separators at 130/160/175/190; no shortfall panel
even with the shortfall dword at 1.

Cursor block, both halves. Gate: bBaseFacPreviewOk != 0 and 75 < nSmapCursorY < band + 75, strict on
both ends. The row marker is panelA->anLineAux[unk_186BE8] and decodes three ways. == 1000

+0xBA -- with TEXTS[412] "Óâîëèòü" at (10, 297); the not-built half draws only TEXTS[159] "Ñîëäàò".
> 2000: an alien row carries its slot plus PUFO_ROW_ALIEN_OFFSET, so 0x784E8 reads
apObjects[marker - 2000] (the ARM's `LDR R2,=0xFFFFE1C8` is -7736 dwords off the 0x1139B8 root, i.e.
2000 slots), named at (10, 281) with TEXTS[1605] "Óñûïëåí" under it. Anything else:

## RadarScreen_BlitMapBackdrop (0x5eb10, 508 B)

Ported in src/pufo/game/pufo_geoscape.{c,h} as RadarScreen_BlitMapBackdrop behind RadarBackdropEnv;
tested by TestRadarBackdrop in tests/test_geoscape.c on a real 240x320 16 bpp surface, with a real
8x3 glyph record for the world bitmap, a real alpha plane for the layer pad and a real 6x5 glyph for
the map pad.

It is installed as a callback, not called directly: RadarScreen_Init stores it at +0x0C of the radar
screen's corner controls (0x5FCEC, 0x5FCF4).

Phase first, draw second. bRadarBlinkPhase @ 0x159730 zero means set it and return without touching
anything; set means clear it and draw. Radar frames therefore show the backdrop on alternate calls.
RadarScreen_Init clears the byte (0x5F4CC); RadarScreen_Update reads it to pick 50 against 0
(0x60584) and to gate the flashing message colour block (0x61144).

The half-extents are the map's half size minus the screen's half size: nHalfW = gSmapCam.nMapW / 2 -
120 (0x5EB44..0x5EB54, held in R7) and nHalfH = nMapH / 2 - 160 (0x5EB58..0x5EB68, R6). The ARM's
MOVS / ADDMI R3,R3,#1 / ASR #1 triple is C division by two, not an arithmetic shift: -5 becomes -2.

Two PadImage_Blit calls of pSmapPadCur @ 0x186E40: nOriginX = -(nScrollX + nHalfW) and
nOriginY = -(nScrollY + nHalfH) (0x5EB6C..0x5EB94), then nOriginX = -(nScrollX + nMapW + nHalfW) with
nOriginY rewritten to the identical value (0x5EBBC..0x5EBC4). The redundant y store is reproduced as
written rather than corrected.

Then three masked blits of the whole world bitmap through pSmapLayerPad @ 0x186BE0, at
nSmapOverlayOriginX - nScrollX - nHalfW, then minus nMapW, then plus nMapW (0x5EBD0, 0x5EC50,
0x5ECA8), all at the layer pad's y, which is copied from the map pad's nOriginY instead of being
recomputed. Each is skipped when nGeoscapeScreen @ 0x186BC4 is 2 (Cydonia). The three x offsets are
one map width apart: the same bitmap is painted left of, on, and right of the viewport, which is how
the original wraps the world horizontally.

SoftSurf_BlitFlip's third argument is the glyph record itself and its fourth the palette base, so the
IDB's own parameter names (nW, nH) mislead: SoftSurf_BlitFlipEx @ 0x9FB80 forwards nW as
SoftSurf_BlitFlip_Inner's pSrc and nH as its palette table, and SoftSurf_BlitFlip_Inner @ 0xA49A0
reads u16 w and u16 h out of the first and indexes through the fourth. pSrc is pSmapWorldBits
@ 0x186BC0 -- a {u16 w, u16 h, u8 indexed[w*h]} record Geoscape_InitUI allocates as 0x4E204 =
800*400+4 bytes (0x85A18..0x85A50) and the zoom steps only resize through the same pointer (600x300
at 0x81E9C, then 472x236). The palette is aPalette slot 29 (0x14E6D0, built as aPalette + 0x7400 at
0x5EC28). The mask is pSmapLayerPad->pData, the layer pad's own byte plane used as per-pixel alpha,
offset by (pIdx - pGlyph) exactly as the blend offsets it.

IDB corrections made here: pSmapViewSize -> pSmapWorldBits (it is a pointer to the record, not the
u16 pair the earlier reading assumed), unk_159730 -> bRadarBlinkPhase typed u8, nSmapModeXBias ->
nSmapOverlayOriginX (its only writer is Geoscape_Draw at 0x8C3D4), unk_14E6D0 -> aPaletteSlot29, and
pSmapPadCur / pSmapLayerPad typed as PadImage *.

Deviation: the original returns 1 on the phase-setting call and otherwise whatever the last blit or
the screen id left in R0, and no caller uses it -- the function is reached through the +0x0C control
slot. The port returns whether it drew. The port also refuses a null environment or a null member,
which the original cannot reach because all five live in globals.

## RadarScreen_DrawFuelGauge (0x5d918, 524 B) and RadarScreen_DrawRangeBar (0x5d6e4, 564 B)

Ported in src/pufo/game/pufo_geoscape.{c,h} behind RadarFuelEnv and RadarRangeBarEnv; tested by
TestRadarFuelGauge and TestRadarRangeBar in tests/test_geoscape.c on a real 240x320 16 bpp surface, with
eleven real 2x1 digit pads whose second column carries the colour key so the keyed blit is verified to
skip it.

The gauge reads the CONSUMED fuel percentage, not the remaining one: n = (int)(100.0 - 100.0 *
(double)Ship.nFuel(+0x18) / (double)Ship.uFuelMax(+0x16)), built as two _itod, _divd, _muld by 100.0,
_subd FROM 100.0 and _dtoi (0x5D950..0x5D9D8). Both halves are read with LDRSH, so uFuelMax is read
signed -- pinned by a check that a 0x8000 uFuelMax with 100 fuel clamps to 100 where an unsigned read
would give 99. When n reaches 100 it clamps there and sets bRadarCraftOutOfFuel @ 0x1596DC, which is the
only thing the original keeps of the number and what RadarScreen_Update reads nine times.

Three _rt_sdiv calls split it into digits -- the divisor travels in R0 and the dividend in R1, the
quotient comes back in R0 and the remainder in R1, the same convention the port already uses elsewhere
and re-confirmed here against Inv_HandlePointer's (nX - 23) / 38 at 0x11B0C. hundreds = n / 100,
tens = (n - 100*hundreds) / 10, units = n % 10. Each digit picks a pad out of aRadarDigitPads
@ 0x1596A0 -- eleven PadImage pointers RadarScreen_Init allocates and loads as i0..i9 through palette
slot 0x19, the eleventh at 0x1596C8 -- moves it to a fixed origin and blits it keyed with 1: hundreds
to (162, 60) drawn only when the digit is non-zero, tens to (172, 60), units to (182, 60) always, slot
10 to (192, 60) always. Every origin is written whether or not the pad is drawn.

The tens rule is the ARM's branch shape rather than a rounding trick: 0x5DA9C jumps past the blit when
the tens digit is non-zero and 0x5DAA4 jumps past it when the hundreds digit is not 1, so a zero tens
digit is drawn only at 100 percent. A leading zero is dropped, except when a hundreds digit justifies
it.

The range bar has three gates. StrategItem.bCraftClass (+2, read with LDRSB) of
strategList[nInterceptStrategIdx] must be non-zero -- 255 becomes -1 and passes. Then
nRadarRangeCur + 560*(nRadarCraftLevel - 13)/114 must be <= nRadarRangeLimit; nRadarCraftLevel is the
per-class level RadarScreen_Init stores (8, 6, 4, 2, 0 at 0x5F6D8, 0x5F7A8, 0x5F878, 0x5F944, 0x5F9E8,
with three of the eight class arms leaving it alone), so the term is always negative and a higher class
loosens the gate. Then nRadarPulseTimer must be exactly 255. Two rects share a y and a height derived
from the range -- y = 183 - 114*nRadarRangeCur/560 and height = that quotient - 15 -- one 3 wide at x 67
(index 0x28, mid 0x64) and one 1 wide at x 68 (index 0x50, mid 0xDC), so the narrow bar is painted over
the wide one. A zero range gives a negative height, which clips to nothing.

Then Game_RandU16(100) < 70 -- a 70 percent roll -- picks a fuel penalty by bCraftClass and adds it to
apCraft[nInterceptShipIdx]->nFuel as i16 (0x5D8E0..0x5D8FC): classes 1 and 2 pay rand(8) - 20, classes 3
and 4 rand(10) - 40, class 5 rand(30) - 120, class 6 rand(20) - 80, class 7 rand(30) - 140, and any
other class pays nothing. nRadarPulseTimer is set to 230 on every path that got past the pulse gate.

Deviation: the gauge returns the percentage it drew where the original returns the last
PadImage_BlitEx result, which no caller uses. The port takes a zero uFuelMax as a ratio of zero (the
original divides by zero) and refuses a digit outside the pad table (the original indexes it out of
bounds); both are port-side guards over cases the original leaves undefined, and both are checked.

## RadarScreen_Init (0x5f490, 3600 B), RadarScreen_SetActive (0x6144c, 76 B), RadarScreen_RollDetection (0x602a0, 720 B)

Ported as `RadarScreen_Init`, `RadarScreen_SetActive` and `RadarScreen_RollDetection` in
`src/pufo/game/pufo_geoscape.c`; the map, the `RadarUiState` / `RadarSessionEnv` / `RadarDetectEnv`
structs and the `g_aRadarUfoClass` table are in `src/pufo/game/pufo_geoscape.h`.

### RadarScreen_Init

One function doing both directions, toggled on `bRadarScreenActive` @ 0x159678 (LDRB at 0x5F494): the
flag-zero path opens the radar screen, the flag-one path closes it. That is why `RadarScreen_SetActive`
calls it on both of its own branches.

Open path (0x5F498..0x5FE80): `Sound_Play(7)` (the `MOV R1, #4` before it is dead -- Sound_Play @
0x9E0C0 reads only R0); set the flag; clear `bRadarCraftOutOfFuel`, `bRadarBlinkPhase`, `bRadarFlip`,
`bRadarTraceLost` and `unk_159650` (all five are STRB, so all five are bytes); allocate five single
pads; `nRadarMsgTimer = 255` and `nInterceptTargetHp = 0`; the class switch; centre the overlay pad as
`115 - (uWidth >> 1)` at y 180; re-sync `StrategItem.nHp` (+0x6C) with `nInterceptTargetHp` (-1 means
"this contact has not fought yet"); draw the two mounts' ammo and split a twin mount's pool;
`nRadarRangeTarget = nRadarRangeCur = 560`; `pRadarUfoPad->nOriginX = 55`; the 766-dword palette copy
and `Palette_Load("base.pal", 3)`; five `UiControl`s with their click handlers and descriptors; five
button pads; `nRadarCursorX/Y = 117/86`; eleven digit pads; `bUiAnimStarted = 0`.

Close path (0x5FF88..0x60298): write the radar ammo back into the craft -- identical mounts get
`(u8)(nRadarAmmoL + nRadarAmmoR)` into `bAmmo<kind>`, different mounts each get their own counter, and
mount kind 28 or any unknown kind writes nothing; clear the flag; free 11 digit pads, 5 controls, 5
button pads and the five single pads; `Palette_Load("menu.pal", 1)`.

The switch at 0x5F658 is one flat table. Cases 1, 3 and 5 set the HP/palette/overlay/limit half and
fall through into cases 2, 4 and 6 for the art and level half only, and the `if (nInterceptTargetHp ==
0)` guard inside 2, 4 and 6 is always true because 0x5F614 zeroed that field moments earlier -- so the
fall-through never changes anything a preceding case already set. The eight rows, read out of the
switch's literal pool and out of RollDetection's speed table:

| bCraftClass | art (mode 23) | flash / missile (mode 27) | level | target HP | palette -> slot 17 | overlay pad (mode 17) | range limit | dSpeed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | ufo_4 | ufo_4f / ufo_4m | 8 | 50 | 85.pal | 85 | 240 | 36.6666 |
| 1 | ufo_3 | ufo_3f / ufo_3m | 6 | 200 | 86.pal | 86 | 360 | 40.0 |
| 2 | ufo_3 | ufo_3f / ufo_3m | 6 | 250 | 87.pal | 87 | 360 | 45.0 |
| 3 | ufo_2 | ufo_2f / ufo_2m | 4 | 500 | 88.pal | 88 | 400 | 66.6666 |
| 4 | ufo_2 | ufo_2f / ufo_2m | 4 | 500 | 89.pal | 89 | 400 | 71.0 |
| 5 | ufo_1 | ufo_1f / ufo_1m | 2 | 1200 | 90.pal | 90 | 480 | 80.0 |
| 6 | ufo_1 | ufo_1f / ufo_1m | 2 | 2200 | 92.pal | 92 | 480 | 53.6666 |
| 7 | ufo_0 | ufo_0f / ufo_0m | 0 | 3000 | 91.pal | 91 | 480 | 83.3333 |

Any other class writes none of it: the level, target HP, target HP max and range limit keep whatever
the previous intercept left, and no ufo art or overlay pad is loaded. The doubles are the original's
own literals -- 0x60324 stores 0x40425553_2617C1BE, which is exactly the double `36.6666`.

Deviation (shape, not behaviour): the per-case store order is normalised into one table application.
Each case writes the same eight things into eight distinct globals, so the order is not observable.

ORIGINAL BUG, reproduced (bugs.tsv 0x5FC34): the palette copy at 0x5FC34 runs 766 dwords while a slot
holds 256, so it overwrites slot 1 (menu.pal, the target) and then all of slot 2 and 254 of 256
entries of slot 3, reading from slot 26 through slot 27 and 254 entries of slot 28. `base.pal` repairs
slot 3 at 0x5FC58 and the close path restores slot 1 at 0x60290, but nothing anywhere reloads slot 2.

Other deviations: `operator new`/`delete` become `malloc`/`free`; the port NULLs the freed pointers the
original leaves dangling; the `strategList` and `apCraft` lookups are bounds-checked where the original
dereferences them directly; the pad and control allocations are guarded for NULL as the original does.

### RadarScreen_SetActive

`RadarScreen_Init()` on both branches (0x61458 and 0x61474 -- Init decides which half runs from the
flag), then `GameTime.bPaused` (STRB at 0x159618+4) and `bUiFrameStyle` (0x186566, the panel root's
frame-style byte at root+0x6E) both take `bActive`. Opening the radar screen pauses the game clock and
picks the bright panel frame. The first argument is never read and the `&pObj` result is never used, so
the port returns void.

### RadarScreen_RollDetection

`Game_RandU16(nChance) != 0` skips the whole speed half and goes straight to the flag check, so the
event happens once in nChance. On a zero roll it rewrites the tracked item first:
`dSpeed = g_aRadarUfoClass[bCraftClass].dSpeed` (an out-of-range class writes nothing) and
`dTrackA = dSpeed * 0.02`. Then it compares `(double)apCraft[nInterceptShipIdx]->uFuelCap * (1/60)`
against that speed. `uFuelCap / 60` is the craft's own speed -- the same basis
`StrategList_ProcessEvents` uses for an inactive craft (pufo_strateg.c:504) and `Ship_BurnFuel` burns
by -- so the test is literally "the tracked contact outruns our intercept craft". When it does not,
nothing is set and the result is whatever `bRadarTraceLost` already held. When it does: `bRadarFlip =
1`, `bRadarTraceLost = 1`, `nRadarRangeTarget = 560`, result 1. If the result byte is non-zero either
way, `nRadarMsgTimer = 0` and TEXTS[1599] is copied into `szRadarMsg` @ 0x186B10; lang.dat decodes
that record as cp1251 "Ñëåä ÌÀÊ ïîòåðÿí" (the middle word is Cyrillic ÌÀÊ, which reads like "MAX").

`bRadarTraceLost` is also the gate the four corner buttons open on, so losing the trace freezes the
radar cursor; only the open path of RadarScreen_Init clears it.

Deviation: the original's strcpy-until-NUL at 0x6054C has no bound; the port bounds it to the
destination.

Tests: `TestRadarSession` and `TestRadarDetect` in `tests/test_geoscape.c`, 194 checks, run against the
shipped archives. Every pad the original loads is loaded for real and compared byte-for-byte against a
directly loaded reference member (radar.pad 85x114, ufo_2 27x27, 88 154x58, i_but3 45x22, i_but6
89x22, i0 8x13, perc 13x14); the class table is checked for all eight classes; the palette copy is
checked against independently reloaded palettes, including the slot-2 overrun before and after the
close; the twin-mount split is checked for an odd and an even pool, for mount kind 28 and for an
unknown kind; and the radar message is compared against the real lang.dat TEXTS[1599], with its
neighbours 1598 and 1600 asserted to be different strings so the record index cannot be off by one.

## RadarScreen_DrawCraftArmament (0x5edf4, 1692 B)

Ported as `RadarScreen_DrawCraftArmament` in `src/pufo/game/pufo_geoscape.c` behind `RadarArmamentEnv`.
`RadarScreen_Update` at 0x60870 is its only caller and it discards the returned bound, so the port
returns void.

**The mount table.** `Ship.bWeaponL @ 0x22` and `Ship.bWeaponR @ 0x23` are two `WeaponMount` ids
(24..30, now an enum in `pufo_ship.h` and in the IDB). Ids 25..30 pick a row of `g_aRadarMountDraw`
out of the two switches' literal pools (0x5EE7C..0x5EF3C left, 0x5F1A4..0x5F25C right):

    id  name (lang.dat TEXTS 1446 + id)   glyph (basebits +)  mount range
    25  1471 "Êîðàáåëüíàÿ ïóøêà"          +50                 140
    26  1472 "Óñò-êà Ñòèíãåð"             +48                 260
    27  1473 "Óñò-êà Ýâàëàíø"             +49                 360
    28  1474 "Ëàçåðíàÿ ïóøêà"             +52                 180
    29  1475 "Ïëàçìåííàÿ ïóøêà"           +53                 300
    30  1476 "Òåðìîÿä. ðàê. óñò."         +51                 420

Id 24, the psi amplifier, is in no switch: it draws no icon and stores a zero bound. The seven names
were read straight out of the shipped lang.dat TEXTS blob (1650 records of 200 bytes), which is the
same 1446 + id rule the resupply note above already uses.

**The engage gate.** `nRadarRangeCur + _rt_sdiv(114, 560 * (nRadarCraftLevel - 26))` is the current
reach, in the same 560/114 scale `RadarScreen_DrawRangeBar` and the NE/SW cursor setters use. When it
is GREATER than the mount's range the target is out of gunshot and the ARM's predicated store group
(0x5EF88..0x5EFB0 left, 0x5F2A8..0x5F2C4 right) writes three things: `bRadarEngageL/R = 0`, that
mount's cooldown forced to 255 (already "ready", there is nothing to shoot), and the in-flight
projectile `nRadarShotYL/R = 0`. Otherwise only `bRadarEngageL/R = 1` is written and the cooldown and
projectile are left alone. Hex-Rays shows the left test twice because the two STR groups are
separate; the ARM shows them as one CMP with MOVLE/STRBLE and MOVGT/STRBGT pairs.

**The bar.** `h = _rt_sdiv(560, 114 * range)`, then the 1-wide rect (37, 170 - h, 1, h - 34) for the
left and x 98 for the right, in the colour 0x78/0xC8/0x28, which `SoftSurf_BlitRectProxy` packs to
0x7E45. A 3x3 cap is added at (36, 169 - h) / (97, 169 - h) only when the range is above 170. Measured
against the shipped font: the 140 range scales to 28 pixels, so `28 - 34` is negative and the cannon
draws NO bar at all -- but its tick row is gated on `bWeaponL != 0`, not on the bar, so the five 2x1
ticks at x 54,57,60,63,66 and the 3x3 at (51, 141) are still drawn. The 180 range scales to 36 and
draws just 2 rows while still getting its cap.

**The labels.** -2 draws nothing, -1 draws the single '-' of asc_AB340, anything else j_itoa; the
string is centred on the bar's own column, `x = 37 - Text_MeasureWidth/2` (98 on the right), y 153.
Under the real font metrics "7" is 7 wide and lands at x 34, "3" at 95.

**The halves are not mirror images in order.** The left draws bar, cap, label, ticks; the right draws
label, bar, cap, ticks. The port keeps each half's own order.

**The tail (0x5F45C..0x5F484).** A mount holding the -2 sentinel inherits the OTHER mount's bound.
With both empty the second copy moves the first copy's value, so both end at the same number.

**Deviation, port-side fix.** `Map_nGlyphPalBase @ 0x1183F4` is ONE global and the font reads it
directly (`Font_DrawGlyph` picks palette slot `Map_nGlyphPalBase + nPal`, `Text_DrawString` forces it
to 2 for its own duration and restores it). The port kept a second copy in `PufoWorldState`, so a
write through one never reached the other. That copy is removed and every env is wired to
`g_nGlyphPalSlotBase`. This is a port modelling defect, not an original bug, so it carries no
bugs.tsv row.

**Deviation.** The original's j_itoa writes into the 52-byte buffer at sp+0x18 with no bound; the port
uses snprintf into the same size. The original also dereferences `apCraft[nShipIdx]` with no test at
all (LDRSB [R3, #0x22] at 0x5EE2C); the port returns early for an out-of-range index, after setting
`Map_nGlyphPalBase` the way the original sets it first.

Tests: `tests/test_geoscape.c:TestRadarArmament`, 69 checks on a real 240x320 surface with the shipped
font.dat and basebits.dat loaded, so every icon and label is the original's own sprite. The mount
icons are 15x17 basebits frames at (30, 136) and (91, 136), and each id's icon is compared against a
direct draw of its own basebits frame, which pins the glyph offsets 50, 48, 49, 52, 53, 51.

## RadarScreen_DrawOverlay (0x5dc84, 2788 B)

Ported as `RadarScreen_DrawOverlay` in `src/pufo/game/pufo_geoscape.c` behind `RadarOverlayEnv`.
`RadarScreen_Update` at 0x60898 is its only caller. It is the shot animation that consumes the state
`RadarScreen_DrawCraftArmament` sets up, and it calls the already-ported `RadarScreen_RollWeaponHit`.

**Idle, then two gates, per mount.** A mount is idle when its ammo is exactly 0 AND its projectile
offset is 0; an idle mount has its engage byte cleared (0x5DCA8..0x5DCEC). `bRadarLastShotHit` is
cleared unconditionally at 0x5DCC0, before either half. Then a half runs only when that mount's engage
byte is non-zero AND its cooldown is exactly 255 (0x5DCFC / 0x5DD0C right, 0x5E238 / 0x5E248 left). The
halves are independent: skipping the right one does not gate the left one. The idle test is `== 0`, so
the -2 sentinel is NOT idle.

**One round per shot start.** The decrement runs only when the projectile offset is 0, i.e. when a shot
starts, not when it is in flight or landing. Only the -1 "unlimited" sentinel is exempt.

**ORIGINAL BUG (0x5DD1C / 0x5E258), reproduced.** The -2 "no weapon on this mount" sentinel is not
exempt. A mount id outside 25..30 -- 24, the psi amplifier, which the shipped data does use -- stores a
zero weapon range in `RadarScreen_DrawCraftArmament`, so once the radar's reach falls to 0 the engage
byte is set and the cooldown stays at 255 because nothing ever lands. This function's switch has no arm
for that id, so the projectile offset is never advanced and the "a shot started" test stays true on
every frame: the ammo counter walks off through -3, -4, -5 ... without bound, and
`RadarScreen_DrawCraftArmament`'s label test is `!= -2`, so the radar screen prints the runaway number
where an ammo count should be. Pinned by three consecutive calls in `TestRadarOverlay`.

**The flight gate and the step, per mount id:**

    id  gate: offset <                              step           cooldown on landing
    25  nRadarCraftLevel + barH - 33                +6, +8 flipped 255
    26  nRadarCraftLevel + barH - 33                +2, +4 flipped 240
    27  nRadarCraftLevel + barH - 33                +2, +4 flipped 235
    28  2                                           +1             251
    29  2                                           +1             249
    30  nRadarCraftLevel + barH - 33                +2, +4 flipped 230

with `barH = _rt_sdiv(560, 114 * nRadarRangeCur)` -- the same 560/114 scale the range bar and the two
mount bars use, so the gate literally means "the projectile has not travelled past the target's
distance yet". `bRadarFlip` adds 2 to the step of the four gated weapons (0x5E1BC `ADDNE R0, R0, #2`);
the laser and plasma have no flip term.

**The laser and plasma have a third case.** When the offset is neither below 2 nor exactly 2 the half
does nothing at all: no cooldown, no roll, no draw (0x5DFEC `BNE loc_5E22C`, 0x5E518 `return`). A beam
that got past 2 without landing never resolves.

**The columns.** The two halves agree on the cannon (x 67 and 69 on both sides) and differ by 6 on the
rockets -- x 64/65/63 left, 70/71/69 right -- except the laser, which is x 64 left and x 72 right
(0x5E4DC `MOV R1, #0x40` against 0x5DFDC `MOV R1, #0x48`). The avalanche and plasma draw their wide
outer column first and their 1-wide inner column second, so the inner overwrites the outer's middle
column; the port keeps that order.

**Deviation.** The ARM stores the zeroed projectile before the roll on the right half (0x5E218 then
0x5E224) and on the left half for ids 25..28 (0x5E750 then 0x5E754), but runs the roll first for the
left half's ids 29/30 (0x5E498 then 0x5E49C). Not observable: `RadarScreen_RollWeaponHit` reads neither
offset. The port uses one order.

Tests: `tests/test_geoscape.c:TestRadarOverlay`, 89 checks on the same real 240x320 surface, covering
the idle clear, both gates, the independence of the halves, the step and flip step of every weapon, the
landing cooldowns 255/240/235/251/249/230, the laser's dead third case, the left/right column
asymmetry, the inner-over-outer draw order, and the runaway -2 counter.

## RadarScreen_Update (0x60570, 3804 B)

The radar frame driver: it draws the whole panel, resolves the damage a landing shot caused, and owns
the three ways an intercept ends.

**Panel geometry.** Five blits (0x605EC..0x60690) build the frame: the 188-wide top strip at (20, 50)
plus four 93..97-wide side pieces, and five rails (0x60694..0x6076C) at x 22/113/208 and y 52/172. The
panel is 140 tall normally and 190 tall while `bRadarBlinkPhase` is set, which is what makes the
0x1F/0x4A/0x75 wash at (26, 176, 180 x 64) visible only in the blink phase.

**The signal bars.** Five bars whose mid colours are 0x55/0x5A/0x5C/0x5A/0x55, at x 117 + 10*i and the
three rows y 57 (h 22), y 156 (h 14 -- 0x60D98 `MOV R8, #0xE`, not the 22 the top row uses) and y 176
(h 14). `nRadarScanOffset @ 0x159724` advances by 10 and wraps to 0 above 39 (0x61078 `ADD R0,R0,#0xA`,
0x61088 `CMP R0,#0x27`, 0x61094/0x6109C `MOVGT/STRGT #0`). `RadarScreen_Init` does NOT clear it, so the
scroll carries across screens.

**The controls.** Five nav speed controls are refreshed (0x6084C..0x60864), but only the first four
`aRadarButtonPads` are ever blitted -- 0x611A8 `MOV R8, #4` bounds that loop, so the fifth pad is
loaded by `RadarScreen_Init` and never drawn.

**The damage ladder is only reachable through a same-frame hit.** `RadarScreen_DrawOverlay` clears
`bRadarLastShotHit` at 0x5DCC0 before either mount runs, and the ladder's gate at 0x608C8 tests that
byte. So a target already at 0 HP is not noticed until a shot actually lands in the same frame. With the
shot landed (0x60898 loads `bRadarInterceptDone`, re-loaded needlessly at 0x6089C):

- `nInterceptTargetHp <= 0` and not done: TEXTS[1600] (0x103A10), `*0x162028 = 1`,
  `StrategList_RemoveAt(nInterceptStrategIdx)`, `Ship_ClearInterceptByStrategIdx`, done = 1
  (0x6094C..0x609A8).
- 40 <= hp_pct < 70, `bRadarTraceLost == 0`, the contact's tile is not 255 and `Game_RandU16(4) == 0`:
  TEXTS[1601] (0x103ADD), the tile's race gets `Funding_AddRaceBonus`, `nType = 4`, `nTimer = 7200`,
  done = 1 (0x60A4C..0x60B4C). The item stays in the list -- it came down on land.
- hp_pct < 40: done = 1 FIRST (0x60C10), then the same tile branch; on a 255 tile the contact is removed
  instead of converted (0x60CB8), and 0xFF feeds the monthly multiplier rather than a race score.
- hp_pct >= 70: nothing.

The percentage is recomputed as `100 * nInterceptTargetHp / nInterceptTargetHpMax` at both 0x60A24 and
0x60B90; the second computation re-reads the HP the first branch may already have changed.

**The three tails.** `done && nRadarMsgTimer > 30` closes the screen and retargets every uncrewed craft
chasing this contact (0x6125C..0x612D8, with the craft count re-read per iteration because a replacement
spawn raised by `StrategList_RemoveAt` can grow the roster mid-loop). `bRadarCraftOutOfFuel &&
nRadarMsgTimer > 30` closes the screen, sets `byte_1870C8` as a DWORD, posts message 44 with the ship
index in colour slot 0, writes the craft's display name into `szScratch186488 @ 0x186488` and calls
`Ship_RemoveWithCargo` (0x6132C..0x613A0). Otherwise the full-zoom exit runs when
`bRadarFlip != 0 && nRadarRangeCur == 560` (0x613BC, 0x613D0).

**ORIGINAL BUG, 0x61434.** The `Ship_ClearInterceptByStrategIdx` there is unreachable: `BLEQ` needs the
zero flag set, and the only way to arrive with it set is `bRadarTraceLost == 0 AND bRadarFlip == 0`
(0x61428..0x61430), while the entry gate at 0x613BC already requires `bRadarFlip != 0`. So when an
intercept reaches full zoom with the trace still held, the OTHER craft chasing the same contact are
never sent home. The port reproduces the behaviour by not calling it either; see bugs.tsv.

**`Craft_CountSoldiersAboard` at 0x612BC** is passed the loop index -- a craft index, not a base index.

**Deviations.** The original dereferences `PtrArray_Get(strategList, StrategList_FindByShipId(...))` at
0x61418 with no test; the port returns early when the lookup misses. The original's three TEXTS copies
have no length bound; the port bounds them by the caller's buffer.

Tests: `tests/test_geoscape.c:TestRadarUpdate`, 84 checks on the real 240x320 surface with the
shipped pads and lang.dat, covering the closed screen, the animation gate, the scan scroll and its wrap,
the blink wash pixel, the five controls, every ladder branch (destroyed, escaped, no escape, ocean tile,
lost trace, crash on land, crash at sea, 70 percent and above, no shot, already done), all three tails
including the unreachable 0x61434, and the two gates that keep the full-zoom exit from running.

## FundingScreen_Init (0x5c084, 1256 B) and FundingScreen_OpenMonthly (0x5d160, 92 B)

The monthly funding report's arithmetic, ported as `FundingScreen_Init` / `FundingScreen_OpenMonthly`
in `game/pufo_baseui.c`. This is what gives the whole funding block its meaning, and it renames 23
globals on the way (see the rename ledger).

**The five rows are five countries.** lang.dat TEXTS[1302..1306] are the row titles of the monthly
report: "ÑØÀ", "Åâðî Àëüÿíñ", "Àçèàòñêèé Àëüÿíñ", "Àâñòðàëèÿ", "Àôðèêà". The rows are NOT in the
order of the five race-score slots: the row -> slot permutation is **0, 2, 3, 1, 4**, and both halves
of the original agree on it -- `FundingScreen_DrawExtended` reads shares 0x186580, 0x186588, 0x18658C,
0x186584, 0x186590 for rows 0..4 (0x5B804..0x5B8A4) and `FundingScreen_Init` writes the same five in
the same order (0x5C34C..0x5C38C). So the SHARE, BAR and ARROW arrays are slot-indexed while the
BASELINE array at 0x1595F0 is row-indexed.

**The money.** With P = `g_nFundPending @ 0x1865BC` and S = the sum of `g_nFundScore0..4`:
bonus = (P / (S+1)) * `g_nFundMult`, P becomes P + bonus, and the per-score share is
(P + bonus) / (S+1). Two `_rt_sdiv` calls (0x5C13C, 0x5C164), divisor in R0 both times. Each score
times that share goes to `g_nFundShare0..4`.

**The bases.** For each of the `nBaseCount` bases, `BaseRec.bKind` (+0x11, renamed from `bUnk17`)
selects a slot through the same table `Funding_AddRaceBonus` uses, and a hit adds **3 * share**
(0x5C1BC..0x5C220). The count is read once as a SIGNED byte (LDRSB at 0x5C188, BLE at 0x5C1B0).

**The upkeep, by month.** `nMonthCounter @ 0x159648` (was `unk_159648`) is incremented by
`FundingScreen_OpenMonthly` at 0x5D170 *before* the recompute, so the first report of a new game runs
at month 1. The table at 0x5C22C..0x5C324 gives one figure per row group -- USA, Euro and Asia share
one, Australia and Africa each have their own:

| month | USA / Euro / Asia | Australia | Africa |
|---|---|---|---|
| <= 0 | -1100 | -300 | -800 |
| 1, 2, 3 | -300 | -100 | -200 |
| 4 | -500 | -200 | -350 |
| 5 | -700 | -300 | -500 |
| >= 6 | -1100 | -300 | -800 |

Month 0 is not "no upkeep": `BLE loc_5C31C` at 0x5C230 and `BNE loc_5C31C` at 0x5C250 land in the
SAME block, so a zero counter gets the heaviest upkeep of all. The figure is stored into that row's
baseline AND added to that row's share.

**The bars.** Per row: `arrow = Funding_DeltaToArrow(share[slot], baseline[row])`, then
`level = Funding_ScoreToBarLevel(row, arrow)` stored into `g_nFundArrow[slot]`; when
`nMonthCounter < 3` and the level is negative the level is zeroed first (0x5C3AC..0x5C3BC and its four
copies), and the level is then ADDED to `g_nFundBar[slot]`. Finally every slot whose bar ended
negative has BOTH its bar and its arrow zeroed (0x5C4D4..0x5C53C), so a country in the red shows no
arrow at all. `Funding_ScoreToBarLevel`'s first argument is the ROW, not a score -- Init passes
0,1,2,3,4 in draw order (0x5C39C..0x5C4A0) while the shares belong to slots 0,2,3,1,4 -- so the
3/5/4/1/3 factor table is per row and the port's parameter is renamed `nRow`.

**`g_nFundArrow*` is not an arrow.** It holds the bar LEVEL, a money amount (+-25000 or +-50000 times
the row factor), not the -2..2 arrow. `FundingScreen_DrawExtended` re-derives the arrow from the share
and the baseline at 0x5B804..0x5B8A4 and uses the stored dword only for its negative test.

**Pending money.** `g_nFundPending` is written by `Tact_CheckBattleEnd` (0x3656C),
`StrategList_ProcessEvents` (0x7FDC0) and `Smap_BeginCraftSelect` (0x84168) between reports, folded
into the shares here, and zeroed at 0x5C544.

**Deviation.** The original indexes `apBases` with an unchecked byte and dereferences every entry; the
port stops at the count it is given and skips a NULL entry.

Open naming question, recorded rather than changed: the 0x80..0x89 id space is used both as the base
kind (`BaseRec.bKind`, `aNewBaseCostByRace @ 0xAB488`) and as the tilemap tile value the radar passes
to `Funding_AddRaceBonus`, and the funding screen's own labels call the five targets countries. The
port's `PUFO_RACE_ID_*` constants therefore read as "race" where the evidence says region/country.
Renaming them touches the radar and the base-creation chain, so it is left as its own unit.

Tests: `tests/test_baseui.c:TestFundingRecompute`, 70 checks -- the pad and close-control wiring
against the shipped archives, the full month-4 chain (shares, base bonus, upkeep, all five bars and
the three negative-bar wipes), the month-1 chain (the below-month-3 clamp, the zero-direction case,
arrows -1/0/+1/+2), months 0 and 6 reaching the same upkeep block, the signed base count, kind 0x86
feeding nothing, and the opener's increment-then-recompute order.

## The 0x80..0x89 id space is a world region, not a race (naming fix)

Evidence chain. Geoscape_DrawGlobeHover @ 0x67914 prints `TEXTS[905 + tile]` as the hovered
tile's own name, and the ten records TEXTS[1033..1042] are "Ñåâåðíàÿ Àìåðèêà", "Þæíàÿ Àìåðèêà",
"Åâðîïà", "Àçèÿ", "Àâñòðàëèÿ", "Àôðèêà", "Àíòàðêòèêà", "Àðêòèêà", "Êàíàäà", "Çäåñü íåëüçÿ
ñòðîèòü". So the tile byte, the new-base placement cost index (aNewBaseCostByRegion @ 0xAB488,
ten dwords indexed by region - 0x80), the base's own region byte (BaseRec +0x11), the pending
placement byte (bPendingRegionId @ 0x159DF4) and the funding bonus source are all the same ten
world regions. 0xFF is the ocean tile. The funding screen groups them into its five investing
countries (TEXTS[1149] "Èíâåñòèðîâàíèå ñòðàí"): 0x80/0x81/0x88 -> USA, 0x82 -> Euro Alliance,
0x83 -> Asian Alliance, 0x84 -> Australia, 0x85 -> Africa; 0x86 (Antarctica), 0x87 (Arctic) and
0x89 ("cannot build here") feed nothing.

The region counter table. BaseFac_FormatCostLabel @ 0x6a404 and Base_CreateNamedEntry @ 0x66930
both load `0x1864DD + region` (0x6A46C / 0x66A64, LDRSB [R7,#-0x1B] off 0x1864F8 + region) and
the label path stores back at `0x18655D + region - 0x80` (0x6A488 ADD R2,R6,#0x65 / 0x6A4A0
STRB [R2,#-0x80]) -- the same byte. The table is therefore g_anRegionBuildCount @ 0x18655D,
nine signed counters for regions 0x80..0x88: InitUI seeds the nine with 1 (0x85814), StartNew
sweeps ten (0x94650, the tenth byte being 0x186566, IDA's bUiFrameStyle), and the save writes
and reads exactly the nine (0x3F304 / 0x40428). 0x1864DD is only the -0x80 bias anchor, not a
table; the only code that reads it directly is Game_StartNew's starting base, which passes
region 0 (MOV R3,#0 at 0x94950) and so gets BaseRec.bUnk16 = (byte at 0x1864DD) - 1.

Corrections made. The earlier reading of the same index as a facility kind 0..16 produced a
false bugs.tsv row ("kinds 15 and 16 read and write past a 15-byte abBaseKindTable") - removed.
The port's 17-byte abKindTable buffer, indexed by the raw region id, was an out-of-bounds read
for every real region (index 128..137 in a 17-byte array); it is replaced by the nine-counter
model with RegionBuildCountAt() guarding the region range. Renames: Funding_AddRaceBonus ->
Funding_AddRegionBonus, aNewBaseCostByRace -> aNewBaseCostByRegion, bPendingBaseKind ->
bPendingRegionId, abBaseKindTable -> abRegionCounterBiasAnchor, BaseRec.bKind -> BaseRec.bRegionId,
PUFO_RACE_ID_* -> PUFO_REGION_ID_*, plus the PufoRegionId enum in the IDB and in the port.

Deviation recorded. Region 0x89 has no counter of its own: the original's store for it lands on
0x186566 (bUiFrameStyle). The port's tenth byte is the same slot of the same sweep StartNew
writes, so the two agree; the shipped placement flow never reaches 0x89 through this call.
## The funding screen's own UI

Four functions carry the screen itself, on top of the recompute ported earlier:

- FundingScreen_Toggle @ 0x5abe4 (1560 B): open/close. Open sets bFundScreenOpen, zeroes
  nFundDisplayTotal, loads its own "funding" pad at origin (0,0), and builds three 5-line panels
  (nStyle 5, nFont 16, y 70, x 10 / 100 / 170). Close frees exactly those four objects.
- FundingScreen_Open @ 0x5b560 (60 B): the toggle, then the shared close control g_pUiCloseCtl to
  (224, 1) with FundingScreen_CloseThunk @ 0x5abd8.
- FundingScreen_Draw @ 0x5b1fc (868 B): gated on the flag. Pad, the 96 shared frame rails, the close
  control's pad, TEXTS[1149] centred at y 20, TEXTS[1150] at (10, 50), the three panels, then
  TEXTS[1151] + itoa(nFundDisplayTotal) + '$' at (10, 160).
- FundingScreen_DrawExtended @ 0x5b59c (2780 B): the monthly report. No open gate, and it never
  reads the three panels -- it re-derives everything from the funding arrays.

### What the toggle pins that the recompute could not

The names panel copies the five country names in SLOT order: TEXTS[1302] USA, TEXTS[1305]
Australia, TEXTS[1303] Euro, TEXTS[1304] Asia, TEXTS[1306] Africa (0x5AF5C..0x5B038). That is an
independent confirmation of the slot model the recompute inferred from the base-region chain: slot 0
USA, 1 Australia, 2 Euro, 3 Asia, 4 Africa. The report rows use the permutation {0, 2, 3, 1, 4} with
titles TEXTS[1302 + row], so the panel order and the report order differ, and the test shows both.

A bar that is not positive zeroes its bar AND its arrow (0x5B0EC..0x5B11C) -- the same rule the
recompute applies at 0x5C4D4..0x5C510, applied again at draw time. The '$' line is not a leftover of
the recompute: nFundDisplayTotal @ 0x159604 is zeroed on open (0x5AC0C) and rebuilt from the five
bars (0x5B124..0x5B144).

### The report's commentary table

TEXTS[1307..1333], selected by [arrow + 2][group][line]. Group 1 is rows 1 and 2 (Euro and Asia,
0x5BA34, 0x5BB80, 0x5BD70, 0x5BEA4); group 0 is rows 0, 3 and 4. The third line has a "this country
is in the red" variant only for the two negative arrows (0x5BF60, 0x5BE34); 0, +1 and +2 use one
line whichever way the flag falls. The red flag is (arrow < 0) && bar[slot] < 0 (0x5B810..0x5B820):
the BAR decides, not the share. The test proves it by flipping only the bar and watching the tail
record move from 1318 to 1317.

While nMonthCounter < 3 every negative arrow is drawn as 0 (0x5B8CC..0x5B8F0), the same clamp
FundingScreen_Init applies to the stored level.

An arrow outside -2..2 copies nothing and redraws the previous row's three buffers -- the original's
scratch buffers are not cleared between rows. Funding_DeltaToArrow only ever returns -2..2, so that
branch is unreachable through it and the port keeps it as a comment rather than a test.
