### Deviations

- The original dereferences the panel allocations with no null test (0x5AC98 and after) and copies
  each name byte by byte into a 50-byte line buffer; the port guards the allocation and bounds the
  copy.
- The original reads aTextRecs and the six funding globals unconditionally; the port returns when an
  env field is missing.
- FundingScreen_DrawExtended has no open gate and ignores the three panels; the port keeps both
  facts, and the test draws the report after closing the screen to show it.

IDB: unk_1595EC -> bFundScreenOpen, unk_159604 -> nFundDisplayTotal, dword_1595E4 / dword_1595E0 /
dword_1595E8 -> pFundPanelNames / pFundPanelBars / pFundPanelArrows; function comments added at
0x5abe4, 0x5b560, 0x5b1fc and 0x5b59c.
## Closing the inventory screen (Inv_CloseAndCommit, 0x15a48)

This function completes the `tact-ui` subsystem: 52 of 52 functions, 43,764 of 43,764 bytes.

### The loadout snapshot (0x15A60..0x15C4C)

While the commit byte at Map+1 is set, every XCom unit that is NOT large gets its inventory written
into two per-slot arrays:

- Soldier+0x3C2, u16[25]: the slot item's object sort key (`LDRH R3,[R3,#0xC8]` at 0x15BFC).
- Soldier+0x3F4, u8[25]: the LOW BYTE of TactItem.nIndex (`LDRB R3,[R6,#4]` at 0x15C28). nIndex is
  the ammo type the weapon has loaded, not a round count -- the round count is nAmmo at +6, which the
  snapshot only uses as a gate.

An empty slot, an object with bTwoHanded, or an item whose nAmmo is 0 or 255 (the "never runs out"
marker) stores 0 in the ammo half (0x15C08..0x15C24). These are the same two arrays
Tact_EquipTeamFromCraft reads back when it re-equips a unit from the craft, which is what they are
for: a unit's declared loadout, as (weapon object index, loaded ammo object index) per slot.

The walk covers 24 slots in the order the jumptable at 0x15AB0 walks them: 268/272 pocket 0,
280/284 pocket 1, 292/296 pocket 2, 304/308 pocket 3, 260/264 the two hands, 316..332 backpack[0..4],
344 backpack[7], 364..392 belt[0..7]. Backpack slots 5 and 6 and belt slot 8 have NO case in the
switch, so the original never looks at them even though the backpack has 8 cells and the belt 9. The
arrays have 25 entries and only 0..23 are ever written.

### The clip merge (0x15CBC..0x15F24)

Whichever hand holds an object with bTwoHanded == 0 and bListPri == 1 is the weapon; the other hand's
item is the clip. The weapon's three anAmmoTypeId entries (ObjectRec+0xA8) are resolved through
Map.apObjects (Map+0x108) and compared with the clip's object. On a match the weapon takes the type id
into nIndex and the clip's nAmmo into its own nAmmo, the clip leaves the hand, and the clip's
TactItem is dropped from the pool: the hole is closed with the LAST entry (0x15EE0 reads index
count-1 through the alias constant 0x23434), then operator delete, then the count is decremented
unconditionally -- an item that was not in the pool at all still costs one entry.

The two halves are not symmetric in one detail worth recording: the left-hand weapon case stops at the
first match (`BEQ loc_15D38` at 0x15D20), while the right-hand weapon case runs all three ids and a
later match overwrites the earlier one (0x15E80..0x15E88). Both are pinned by tests.

Then Unit_RecalcInventoryStat on the selected unit and Map_nUiScreen = 0.

### Deviations

The original dereferences the selected unit, both hands' items, their objects, the unit array entries
and the object table with no test, and walks the pool with no bound. The port refuses a null context,
treats a null item or object as an empty slot, and bounds the pool walk to the count.

IDB: function comment at 0x15a48. The two Soldier arrays stay auUnk962 / abUnk1012 in the IDB -- the
MCP rename tool only accepts globals and struct members are not globals.

## The four post-battle tallies (0x3348c, 0x33780, 0x33c80, 0x344b4)

Ported into `src/pufo/game/pufo_tactend.c` as `Tact_TallyBattleStats`, `Tact_TallyUnitResults`,
`Tact_TallyItemRecovery` and `Tact_TallyCraftRecovery`. All four run back to back inside
`Tact_CheckBattleEnd` (0x34fbc, not ported yet) at 0x35240, 0x35284, 0x352b0 and 0x352bc, and their
outputs are the mission debrief.

### What each counter is for

`Tact_CheckBattleEnd` labels every counter it prints with a TEXTS record, built as
`LDR R0, =0xB38D0` plus `MOV R3, #hi; ORR R3, #lo` -- `aTextRecs + 205*n`, the in-memory stride
(`PUFO_TEXT_REC_STRIDE`; the on-disk record is 200 bytes and the loader leaves five bytes of slack).
That gives the debrief line for each out-param, which is what the port names them after:

| out-param | debrief line | ARM |
|---|---|---|
| `Tact_TallyUnitResults` param 6 | TEXTS[162] "Operatives killed" | 0x35428 |
| `Tact_TallyUnitResults` param 7 | TEXTS[163] "Tanks Destroyed" (score term * 0x50) | 0x35500 |
| `Tact_TallyUnitResults` param 8 | TEXTS[164] "Civilians Killed" | 0x355c4 |
| `Tact_TallyUnitResults` param 9 | TEXTS[165] "Civilians Rescued" (score term * 30) | 0x35688 |
| `Tact_TallyUnitResults` param 10 | TEXTS[166] "Aliens Killed" | 0x3575c |
| `pnAlloys` | TEXTS[171] "Alien Alloys" (score term (n+7)>>3) | 0x35b40 |
| `pnElerium` | TEXTS[172] "Elerium 115" | 0x35c6c |
| `pnNavigation` | TEXTS[173] "UFO Navigation" | 0x35d70 |
| `pnPowerSource` | TEXTS[174] "UFO Power Source" (score term * 20) | 0x35e80 |
| `pnReproduction` | TEXTS[175] "Alien Reproduction" | 0x35f90 |
| `pnFood` | TEXTS[176] "Alien Food" | 0x36090 |
| `pnEntertainment` | TEXTS[177] "Alien Entertainment" | 0x36298 |
| `pnSurgery` | TEXTS[178] "Alien Surgery" | 0x363a0 |
| `pnExamination` | TEXTS[198] "Examination Room" | 0x3618c |

The first three `Tact_TallyUnitResults` out-params are loss lines, not survival lines. The IDB's
original `pnSurvived` / `pnKilled` / `pnMIA` names described the type ranges; the IDB now carries the
debrief names instead.

### The tile facility byte, Mc1Rec+0x1E

`Tact_TallyBattleStats` walks four layers x (10 * nMapDimY) rows x (10 * nMapDimX) columns and, per
cell, the four sprite slots in the order floor, wall A, wall B, ceiling (ARM 0x335C8). The byte at
`Mc1Rec+0x1E` names the alien-base facility the sprite contributes to. It is the only read of that
byte in the whole binary (0x33618), which is why it had stayed a gap.

The names come from two sides that agree. The debrief line each counter feeds is above; the value
distribution across the 1,163 records of the 27 shipped `.MC1` sets in main.dat is:

| value | records | where | counter |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 911 | every natural, craft and furniture set | none |
| 1 | 109 | AVENGER, LIGHTNIN, PLANE, XBASE1 | none |
| 2 | 1 | U_WALL02 | power source +1, Elerium += `unk_138E6C` |
| 3 | 6 | U_WALL02 | navigation |
| 5 | 4 | U_DISEC2 | reproduction |
| 7 | 4 | U_PODS | entertainment |
| 8 | 6 | U_DISEC2 | surgery |
| 9 | 4 | U_OPER2 | examination |
| 10 | 133 | U_BASE 66, U_EXT02 26, U_WALL02 19, UFO1 14, U_OPER2 6, MARS 2 | alloys |
| 12 | 49 | the alien base wall/ext/pod sets | none |
| 13, 14 | 1, 4 | MARS, BRAIN | none |

Two counters are not tile counts at all. Elerium grows by `unk_138E6C` (Map+0x254B4, the
`rand(0x28) + 10` roll the mission setup seeds) once per kind-2 sprite, so it is an amount and not a
room count. Food is written only by the tail, from `word_138E70` (Map+0x254B8, `rand(0x14)`), and
only when `Map_nTerrainVariant > 3` or the mission type is `MissionType_AlienBase` (ARM 0x3373C:
`CMP #3 BHI` / `CMP #4`). The sixth counter has no writer and no reader anywhere in the binary.

The gate at 0x334B4 is `Map_bAltOutcomePath != 0 || unk_128A8C == 0`: the walk runs only with
`unk_128A8C` set and the alternate outcome path clear.

### The unit type and rank table

`Tact_TallyItemRecovery` credits one `apObjects` slot per `(nUnitType, bRankType)`, reading them out
of the Map slot block at Map+0x23C..Map+0x2AC, Map+0x2D0 and Map+0x348..Map+0x358. Those 37 slots are
now named `Map_apObjects77` .. `Map_apObjects148` in the IDB, and every one of them is that race's
soldier record in the shipped OBJECTS.DAT. That pins the unit types: 9 Sectoid, 0xA Muton, 0xB
Floater, 0xC Snakeman, 0xD Ethereal, 0xE Chryssalid, 0xF Celacid, 0x12 Cyberdisk, 0x13 Silacoid,
0x14 Riper, 0x15 Sectopod. The ranks are 2 soldier, 3 navigator, 4 leader (the records spell it
"lider"), 5 engineer, 7 medic, 8 commander -- rank 7 is the only one whose slot lies outside the
race block, in the 144..148 medic block. The Muton row has no rank 4 and no rank 8 because the
shipped Muton block (92..94) has no leader or commander at all, and the switch credits nothing for
those ranks while still raising the debrief score.

`Tact_TallyUnitResults` independently confirms the civilian half: 0x10 and 0x11 are the only types
that can reach "Civilians Rescued" / "Civilians Killed", while 9..0xF and 0x12..0x15 all fall into
"Aliens Killed".

### Behaviours worth pinning

- The box is **inclusive** in `Tact_TallyUnitResults`, `Tact_TallyItemRecovery`'s alien pass and its
  HWP pass, but **exclusive at the top** in the cell walk (0x33EB8 and 0x33EC4 are CMP/BLT against
  nY1 / nX1). The same four numbers are used both ways in one function.
- A unit counts as lost when `uHp == 0`, or when both outcome flags are clear, or when the alternate
  path is set and `bInZone` is 0. With both flags clear every operative and every hardware unit lands
  on the "killed"/"destroyed" line whatever its hit points, and no civilian can be rescued.
- The zone-marking pass has the same type-8 ceiling as the Xcom one, so a real civilian of type 0x10
  or 0x11 is never marked and never gains a mission count.
- `apEnemyUnits` is never marked: an enemy's `bInZone` is whatever an earlier pass left on it.
- Item chain rules: a single-handed weapon (`bTwoHanded == 0`) is always counted, and its clip object
  is counted too when `nAmmo` is neither 0 nor 0xFF and equals `apObjects[nIndex]->bAmmoCap`; a clip
  (`bTwoHanded == 1`) is counted only when full; an alien corpse (`bTwoHanded == 2`) only when
  `uSortKey` is in 59..69 and `pLinkedSoldier` is null. Other `bTwoHanded` values are counted by
  nobody.
- A live alien counts only when one item on its cell has `pLinkedSoldier` pointing back at it; a dead
  one with such an item is skipped outright.
- The HWP pass zeroes the deployed craft's `anCargoQty[0..3]` first, then credits apObjects[31..35]
  for unit types 4..8 and adds `pHandL->nAmmo` into cargo column 0, 1, none, 2, 3. Type 6 is the Tank
  laser, whose `bAmmoCap` is 255, so it has no cargo column. With both outcome flags clear the pass
  returns at the first hardware unit -- after the hold has already been emptied.
- `Tact_TallyCraftRecovery` caps recovery against `ObjectRec.aItemQty[craftIdx]` per craft, and the
  leftover splits by mission type: the Xcom base defence adds it into `auPerBaseVal[nCraftHomeBase]`
  and deliberately leaves `uRecovCount` in place; any other mission parks a non-zero remainder in
  `aSmapSites[nSmapSiteCount].auItemQty[object index]`, sets that record's `bHasLoot` and sets the
  dword out-param. The out-param is not zeroed by the callee -- the caller zeroes it at 0x34FF4.

### Deviations

1. The original passes the debrief counters as ten (and five) separate pointers; the port passes one
   struct per tally. Same writes, fewer arguments.
2. `Tact_TallyItemRecovery`'s return value is a leftover register the caller overwrites at 0x352b8;
   the port returns nothing.
3. The original bounds nothing on `apObjects[nIndex]`, the craft index list, `auPerBaseVal[]` or
   `aSmapSites[nSmapSiteCount]`. The port bounds each and records it. The list in particular is a
   20-dword stack array appended to without a check, so more than 20 crafts home at the defended base
   would walk off the frame.
4. The HWP pass dereferences `pHandL` with no test; the port skips the cargo add when it is null.

### Open question: the polarity of unk_128A8C -- RESOLVED, and the answer was the other way
### (see the later section "Map_bMissionVictory: the byte the port had backwards": the byte is the
### victory flag, and the port's pbMissionAborted name was wrong)

The port calls this byte `pbMissionAborted`, "the mission ended in a retreat rather than a completed
landing". The counting rule reads more naturally the other way: with the byte clear every operative
and every tank is counted as lost and no civilian is rescued, while with it set only dead units are
lost and live civilians are rescued. That is consistent with the byte meaning "the team was
extracted". All eight of its xrefs are reads (TactHud_DrawStatusBanner, Tact_Shutdown), so no writer
is visible in the IDB and the name is left as it is. To be settled with `Tact_CheckBattleEnd`.

## Map_bMissionVictory: the byte the port had backwards (Map+0x150D4, was unk_128A8C)

The four tallies gated on this byte and its counting rule read like "the team was extracted", so the
port named it `pbMissionAborted` and recorded the polarity as an open question. `Tact_CheckBattleEnd`
(0x34fbc) writes it, and the writes settle it the other way round: **the byte is the victory flag.**

| site | condition | write |
|---|---|---|
| 0x350F0 | `Map_nEnemyReserveCount + (live apEnemyUnits entries of type != 0x10/0x11) == 0`, and not an unfinished alien base (`Map_nMissionType != 4 || Map_bSpawnAlt == 0`) | set |
| 0x35070 | `Map_nXcomUnitCount == 0` | clear |
| 0x351CC | `bAbort != 0 && Map_nMissionType == 3` (a base-defence mission called off) | clear |

and the debrief reads it as the win/lose switch:

- 0x353C4 copies TEXTS[160] "Victory" (`aTextRecs + 205*160 = 0xBB8F0`) into `Map_szMissionCaption`
  @ Map+0x15094; 0x35400 copies TEXTS[161] "Defeat" (`0xBB9BD`) when it is clear.
- `TactHud_DrawStatusBanner` (0x1E968) draws that caption green (0,255,0) when set, red (255,0,0)
  when clear.
- `Tact_Shutdown` (0x3DF48..0x3E058) transfers the tactical loot on a held site when set and
  demolishes the facility when clear; on a leaving craft it removes the craft itself only when clear.

So the tally rule reads correctly: won -> only dead units are lost and live civilians are rescued;
lost outright -> every operative and every tank is lost and nobody is rescued; aborted -> whoever is
outside the camera box is lost.

**Why no writer looked to exist.** All eight IDB data xrefs to 0x128A8C are reads, in
`TactHud_DrawStatusBanner` and `Tact_Shutdown`. Every write in `Tact_CheckBattleEnd` goes through a
register-built offset -- `MOV R8,#0x15000; ORR R8,R8,#0xD4; ... STRB R7,[R5,R8]` -- and ARM cannot
encode a 6684-byte displacement in one instruction, so IDA never records a data xref for them. Any
Map field past +0xFFF has to be reached that way, which is a general trap for xref-based reasoning
about this binary.

### Two Map fields this function owns that had no name

- `Map_nDebriefLine` @ Map+0x150D0 (was an unnamed gap): the debrief line cursor, shared by the label
  panel `pUiPanel0 @ 0x1568E8` and the value panel `pUiPanel1 @ 0x1568E4`. Zeroed at 0x3539C, advanced
  once per emitted line, and copied into both panels' `nStyle` at 0x36524 / 0x36530.
- `Map_nMissionOutcome` @ Map+0x1A1C (was an unnamed gap): written 1 (no Xcom left), 0 (no enemies
  left) or 2 (aborted), and **never read anywhere in the binary** -- a dead store, like the tallies'
  sixth counter.

`Map_szMissionScore` @ Map+0x150B2 (was `byte_128A6A`) holds `itoa(debrief score)` (0x36548) and is
drawn at (200, 260); the same score is added to `g_nFundPending` at 0x3657C.

### The debrief label addresses are TEXTS records, and the stride is 205

Every label the debrief copies comes from `aTextRecs + 205*n`, built as `LDR R0,=0xB38D0` plus
`MOV R3,#hi; ORR R3,#lo`. The label block runs 0xBB8F0..0xBD75E, and consecutive labels are exactly
205 apart -- 160 Victory, 161 Defeat, 162..166 the unit lines, 167 live aliens recovered, 168 Craft
Lost, 169 Base Destroyed, 170 Base Lost, 171..178 the alien-item lines, 198 Examination Room. IDA
types none of them as strings (they are in the loaded-texts image, not in .rdata), which is why
`get_string` returns nothing there.

## Tact_ClearSoldierBattleFlags (0x346e0) and the rank ladder (0x47280)

2268 + 1096 = 3364 bytes, ported as `Tact_ClearSoldierBattleFlags` in src/pufo/game/pufo_tactend.c
and `Soldier_PromoteByTypeScores` in src/pufo/game/pufo_roster.c.

### The five steps of 0x346e0

1. clear `Soldier.bRankDirty` (0x1BC) over `Map_apSoldiers` (0x34724)
2. `Soldier_PromoteByTypeScores` (0x47280) at 0x3473C -- whoever climbs sets bRankDirty
3. per-soldier stat refresh, gated on `bInZone` (0x3C0) != 0 and `Unit_bIsOperative`
   (bStatus @ 0x17 == 0)
4. the promotion report, for the refreshed soldiers that still hold bRankDirty
5. clear bRankDirty again (0x34F9C)

Step 1 is why a bRankDirty the caller left behind is not a report row: the flag is wiped before
the ladder runs, so at step 4 it means "promoted by this call" and nothing else.

### The rank ladder (0x47280)

Five rungs, run top-down, one step per rung per call -- a soldier promoted by the 2->3 rung is
not reconsidered by the 3->4 rung, which already ran. Mission score is
`5 * (uKills + 2 * uMissions)` (Soldier_MissionScore).

  rung   gate on the target rank   candidates            threshold   ARM
  4 -> 5 count(5) == 0            best of two rank-4    375         0x472C0
  3 -> 4 count(4) < 2             best of two rank-3    270         0x47374
  2 -> 3 count(3) < 2             best of two rank-2    125         0x47440
  1 -> 2 count(2) < count(1)/3    count(1)/3 attempts   90          0x47504
  0 -> 1 none                     every rank-0 soldier  > 45        0x47654

`count(n)` is Soldier_CountSmallByType: live (uHp != 0) and non-large. The engineer rung tests
`== 0` where the two above it test `< 2`, so one existing rank-5 soldier closes that rung while
one rank-4 soldier does not close the leader rung.

"Best of two" compares only the two lowest-indexed candidates through
Soldier_PickBestScoreAmong (0x47190). With pick 0 (candidate A won) and the score short of the
threshold the ARM jumps the whole rung -- candidate B is never tried (0x47308 -> 0x47338).

The 1->2 rung is the odd one out. Its two scans test `bRankType` alone: no alive test and no
large-unit test, so a DEAD rank-1 soldier holding the best score is the one that climbs, even
though count(1) only counted the live ones. It also seeds its running score from
`nPromoteBestPick` (0x47548, 0x47624) -- the previous rung's 0/1 pick, not a score. Harmless
(0 and 1 sit under every real score and under the 90 gate) but reproduced.

### The stat refresh: the base index is not the stat index

    auStat[k] = (u16)((double)g_aClassStatGrowth[9 * nClass + j] * rate * (double)uMissions
                      + (double)auStatBase[b])

  j  k  b  rate                    auStat meaning
  0  0  0  0.8166666666666667      auStat[0] -> uTu
  8  9  8  0.31666666666666665     auStat[9] -> uStunOrArmor
  1  1  1  0.4                     auStat[1] -> uHp
  2  2  2  0.3833333333333333
  3  3  3  0.35
  4  4  4  0.31666666666666665
  5  5  5  0.2833333333333333
  7  8  7  0.4

Class column 6 is never read and auStat[6]/auStat[7] are never recomputed. Each rate is a literal
double written as two dword halves (`LDR R2,=0x22222222` / `LDR R3,=0x3FEA2222` at 0x347D8), and
the product goes through _dtou -- truncated toward zero -- before STRH.

**The bug this unit found in the port.** The first version used the stat index for the base too.
The ARM spells the difference out in the operand offsets: the j=8 rule reads
`LDRH R0,[R8,#Soldier.auStatBase+0x10]` (auStatBase[8]) and stores `STRH R0,[R8,#Soldier.auStat+0x12]`
(auStat[9]); the j=7 rule reads `[R8,#0xF2]` (auStatBase[7]) and stores `[R8,#0xB2]` (auStat[8]).
auStatBase has nine entries, so reading index 9 ran off the end of the array into the bytes before
uKills (0x0FA). The pairing is exactly the compaction Unit_ResetBattleState (0x498b0) writes --
auStatBase[7] = auStat[8], auStatBase[8] = auStat[9] -- so every rule reads the base of the stat it
grows. Fixed by giving StatGrowthRule a `b` field.

g_aClassStatGrowth @ 0xAA930 (was byte_AA930) is 6 x 9 bytes of 1..3, Tact_ClearSoldierBattleFlags
is its only reader in the binary, and docs/parity/audit_tables.py now byte-checks all 54 entries
against the shipped image: exact match.

### The promotion report

For each refreshed soldier still holding bRankDirty: `Soldier.szName` (0x0BA) into
`pUiPanel2 @ 0x1568E0` apLines[n] (0x34E34) and `aszTextE[20 * bRankType]` into
`pUiPanel3 @ 0x1568DC` apLines[n] (0x34E74), then both nLineCount += 1 (0x34EAC, 0x34EC0) and
`Map_bPromotionReport` (0x1153D8) = 1 (0x34EDC). Both copies are terminator-inclusive byte walks,
into 50-byte line buffers. aszTextE @ 0xB2200 is a loaded TEXTS block of six 20-byte entries --
its text is not in the image (get_bytes there is all zero), so the port takes the names through
the env and the test checks the 20 * bRankType indexing rather than the wording.

Rows follow roster order, and the bInZone gate applies here too: a soldier the ladder promotes but
that sits outside the zone changes rank and gets no row.

### Deviations

- The port bounds-checks `nClass` against 0..5 before indexing g_aClassStatGrowth. The original
  indexes it blind. Unit_ClassFromStats only ever produces 0..5, so the branch is unreachable.
- nPromoteBestScore / nPromoteBestPick stay locals in the port's shared scratch: nothing outside
  Soldier_PickBestScoreAmong and Soldier_PromoteByTypeScores reads either global.
- Tests: 33 new checks in tests/test_roster.c (each rung's threshold, the engineer `== 0` gate
  against the leader `< 2` gate, the count(1)/3 attempt count, the dead high-scorer promoted by
  the 1->2 rung, one-step-per-rung ordering) and 74 in tests/test_tactend.c (the exact auStat
  values for class 0 and class 5, auStat[6]/[7] left alone, both gates, the report rows and their
  order, a stale bRankDirty producing no row, Map_bPromotionReport clear when nobody is promoted).

## Tact_CheckBattleEnd (0x34fbc): the debrief emitter

5,748 bytes, 122 blocks, ported as `Tact_CheckBattleEnd` in src/pufo/game/pufo_tactend.c. This is the
function the four tallies from the tally unit run inside, and the one that writes the victory flag the
naming unit settled.

### The head

`bAbort` is stored into Map_bAltOutcomePath at 0x34FE4 before anything else -- the caller's abort
request IS the alternate-outcome path the tallies gate on. Then:

  Map_bBattleEnded != 0                    -> return (0x34FEC)
  Tact_ScanVictoryTiles() != 0             -> Tact_Shutdown(1) + EndScreen_Init(1), tick hold,
                                             battle ended, return (0x35004..0x35030)
  bAbort != 0                              -> Map_nMissionOutcome = 2, tick hold, and NEITHER side
                                             of the win/lose decision is evaluated (0x35104). The
                                             abort leaves Map_bMissionVictory exactly as it was.
  Map_nXcomUnitCount == 0                  -> Map_bMissionVictory = 0, tick hold, outcome 1
  live non-civilian enemies + reserve == 0 -> Map_bMissionVictory = 1, outcome 0, tick hold (0x350F0),
                                             and only when it is not an unfinished alien base: the
                                             gate is `nMissionType != 4 || Map_bSpawnAlt == 0`. The
                                             enemy count walks apEnemyUnits @ Map+0x151CC and skips
                                             nUnitType 0x10/0x11, the civilians (0x350A0, 0x350A4).
  Map_bTickHold == 0 after all that        -> return, the battle is still running (0x35118)

Map_nMissionOutcome @ Map+0x1A1C gets 1 / 0 / 2 for lost / won / aborted and still has no reader
anywhere in the binary.

### The fourth exit (0x35124..0x35198)

  (nMissionType == 4 || nMissionType == 9) && Map_bSpawnAlt != 0
  abFacilityGrid[0x618] == 1 && nMissionType == 3

either, together with Map_bMissionVictory == 0, gives Tact_Shutdown(1) + EndScreen_Init(0) and
returns. The second arm is only reachable when the type is neither 4 nor 9 -- the first arm falls
through to it and then fails its `== 3` test -- which is what makes it the failed base-defence path.
abFacilityGrid+0x618 is read with LDRSB at 0x35160, so it is a SIGNED byte compared to 1: -1 is not
"set".

### The debrief setup

An aborted MissionType_XcomBase mission clears Map_bMissionVictory AND the local copy of bAbort
(0x351CC, 0x351D0), which is why a base defence gets TEXTS[170] "Base Lost" instead of TEXTS[168]
"Craft Lost". Then Map_nUiScreen = 13 (0x351EC, a STRH), Map_bBattleEnded = 1, Map_nBannerFadeTicks
= 10 (0x351FC), pTactCtx272->bBusy = 0 (0x35228), Map_bEnemyTurnActive = 0 (0x3523C).

After the four tallies: Map_bPromotionReport = 0, both promotion panels' nLineCount = 0, and every
soldier in apSoldiers gets `bFlags |= 0x20` when

  (Map_bAltOutcomePath != 0 && Soldier.bInZone == 0) || (Map_bAltOutcomePath == 0 && lost)

(0x3531C..0x35364). Bit 5 of bFlags is the dead bit Unit_AnimatePose reads, so a wipe or an abandoned
squad is killed off rather than removed. Note that the geoscape roster is never re-marked in-zone by
Tact_TallyUnitResults -- only the tactical rosters are -- so an aborted mission marks every
apSoldiers entry it walks.

### The debrief lines

Map_nDebriefLine @ Map+0x150D0 is the cursor. Each line copies its TEXTS record into
pUiPanel0 @ 0x1568E8 apLines[n], colours both columns with UiPanel_SetLineMeta, and writes the value
into pUiPanel1 @ 0x1568E4 anLineAux[n]. Three meta shapes appear: loss (255, 0, 0, 90, 0, 0), gain
(0, 255, 0, 0, 90, 0) and the loot lines' third shape (0, 255, 255, 0, 90, 90) -- the only one whose
third meta byte is non-zero.

  gate                                      TEXTS  value column / score term
  operatives lost > 0                       162    -30 each
  tanks lost > 0                            163    -80 each
  civilians killed > 0                      164    -30 each
  civilians rescued, and won                165    +30 each
  aliens killed, won                        166    +20 each
  live aliens recovered > 0, won            167    +30 each
  won and nMissionType == 4                 169    +500
  lost and nMissionType == 3                170    -700
  lost, not a base defence, not aborted     168    -400
  won, alloys / 8 > 0                       171    alloys / 8
  won, elerium > 0                          172    elerium
  won, navigation > 0                       173    15 each
  won, power source > 0                     174    20 each
  won, reproduction > 0                     175    2 each
  won, food > 0                             176    1 each
  won, examination > 0                      198    the raw count, 10 each in the score
  won, entertainment > 0                    177    2 each
  won, surgery > 0                          178    2 each

TEXTS[198] is the one line where the value column and the score term differ: the column shows the
room count (0x36218) and the score pays 10 per room (0x36230). Only one of the three base/craft
lines can appear. The nine loot lines run only when the mission was won.

The score is the sum of the emitted terms; it lands in g_nFundPending (0x365B0) and, as text, in
Map_szMissionScore @ Map+0x150B2 (0x36534). Both debrief strings sit in 30-byte slots -- 0x150B2 -
0x15094 and 0x150D0 - 0x150B2 -- and the original's copies are terminator-inclusive walks with no
bound.

### Committing the loot to the working site (0x364A0..0x36510)

Each loot line writes its count into aSmapSites[nSmapSiteCount].auItemQty[obj] and adds it to
apObjects[obj]->uRecovCount (ObjectRec+0xCC), with obj = 106 alloys, 105 elerium, 109 navigation,
107 power source, 111 reproduction, 110 food, 143 examination, 142 entertainment, 108 surgery. If
any loot was recorded -- from these lines or from Tact_TallyCraftRecovery -- the site is committed:
bHasLoot(+0x2E4) = 1, bFlag1(+1) = apBases[apCraft[Map_nCraftIndex]->bHomeBase]->bUnk4, bFlag0(+0)
= 8, nSmapSiteCount++. Both panels' nStyle then take the line count (0x36514, 0x36524), which is
what makes the debrief draw exactly the rows that were emitted.

### The Mars restart tail (0x36594..0x365F8)

0x162028 (the replacement-spawn gate) is set to 1 unconditionally at 0x36584. Then, when the mission
was MissionType_MarsOrSpecial with the alternate spawn, it restarts in place as an alien base:
Tact_Shutdown(0), Map_nMissionType = 4, Map_bMissionMode = 2, Map_nTerrainVariant = 0,
Map_nMapLayers = 0, Map_bUnk15115 = 0, Tact_InitMission(0), and Map_bFrameScratch = 1 last.

### Naming fixed on the way

- `Tact_ScanVictoryTiles` (0x33264) had its parameters named bCraftTileA0NonZero / nCraftTileX /
  nCraftTileY, which read as though the 2x2 probe started at the deployed craft. The three addresses
  it actually reads are Map_bSpawnAlt @ 0x128B00, Map_nSpawnTileX @ 0x128B04 and Map_nSpawnTileY @
  0x128B08, so the parameters are now bSpawnAlt / nSpawnTileX / nSpawnTileY.
- Three globals named in the IDB: `unk_113A13` -> `Map_bEnemyTurnActive` (Map+0x5B), `dword_113A1C`
  -> `Map_nBannerFadeTicks` (Map+0x64), `unk_157180` -> `pTactCtx272` (the pointer to the TactCtx272
  singleton whose bBusy at +0xF8 this function clears).

### Deviations

- Tact_Shutdown, EndScreen_Init and Tact_InitMission arrive as hooks in `TactBattleEndHooks`. The
  first two need the app layer's teardown env and the third needs the whole mission-init env; the
  same shape already carries Input_OnLeft's shutdown hooks. Each hook call site cites the original
  address.
- j_itoa is `snprintf("%d")` bounded to the 30-byte slot. itoa of an int cannot exceed that, so the
  two agree.
- The caption copy is reproduced as the original's unbounded terminator-inclusive walk. A TEXTS
  record longer than 30 bytes would run into Map_nDebriefLine; the shipped Victory/Defeat records do
  not, and the port does not add a bound the original does not have.
- Tests: 130 new checks in tests/test_tactend.c -- every head gate including the civilian skip and
  the unfinished-alien-base clause, the four arms of the cannot-complete exit including the signed
  facility byte, the full ten-line won debrief with its aux values, meta shapes, score, site commit
  and per-object recovery tallies, the lost debrief's base-lost and craft-lost lines, the empty
  debrief of an aborted win, and the Mars restart tail.

## Unit_ApplyFallDamage (0x4a7b0) and Tact_ProcessFallAction (0x52adc): the fall processor

Ported in src/pufo/game/pufo_tactstate.c as `Unit_ApplyFallDamage` plus
`Tact_ProcessFallAction` with static helpers `Fall_*`. 6,716 bytes, the largest
tact pair ported so far.

### Unit_ApplyFallDamage @ 0x4a7b0

Three early returns, in order: the unit's own cell has a floor sprite
(`MapCell_TestFlag` 5, 0x4A7C4), `g_aUnitTypeRecord[4*nUnitType + 0]` is set
(0x4A7E0 - the fall-immune types), or the cell is already at layer 0 (0x4A7F0).

A large unit then returns if ANY of its three footprint cells at its own layer has
a floor (0x4A86C, 0x4A880, 0x4A894) - it is standing on something.

The descent (0x4A8AC..0x4A988). `nLayer` starts at the unit's `nZ`. A small unit
tests its own column; a large unit tests the other three footprint cells and
descends only when all three are open (0x4A91C is the AND of the first two tests,
then the third goes through the shared LABEL_14). The loop stops ON the first layer
that HAS a floor, or leaves `nLayer` at -1 when the column runs out. The three
footprint cells the landing sweep then uses are the ones the loop last computed, so
they sit on the stopping layer.

Damage (0x4A98C..0x4AA14):

    damage = (int)((float)(nZ - nLayer - 1) * (float)auStat[1] * 0.4f)

clamped at zero by the MOVMI/STRMI pair at 0x4AA0C. `_itos` / `_muls` / `_stoi` are
coredll's soft-float helpers, not a fixed-point format, and the constant
1053609165 = 0x3ECCCCCD is the IEEE-754 single 0.4f. So a fall costs 40% of max HP
per floor fallen, and `nZ - nLayer - 1` counts FLOORS, not layers: a one-layer step
is zero damage. The clamp is unreachable in practice - both descent paths test the
unit's own layer first, so `nLayer < nZ` always holds - and the port keeps it anyway.

The landing sweep (0x4AA3C..0x4AB1C) covers one cell for a small unit and the full
2x2 for a large one. For each occupant: a small unit landing ON a large one breaks
out of the sweep (0x4AAE4) and is then killed with its HP untouched (0x4AB28 tests
the falling unit, not the occupant); a large occupant has `uHp` zeroed first
(0x4AAFC); `Unit_bIsOperative` is called and its result dropped (0x4AB04). Then,
unless the falling unit already has `bFlags` bit 5 set (0x4AB4C), it is placed on
the landing layer, loses the damage from `uHp` with a floor at zero, and runs
`Unit_EnqueueIfApSpent`.

### Tact_ProcessFallAction @ 0x52adc

`switch(nCmd)` over 1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 0xA, 0xC, 0xE, 0xF, 0x10, 0x11, 0x12; commands
2, 6, 7, 9, 11 and 13 only advance the cursor.

**LABEL_186 (0x540E0)** is the shared tail and `Map_bTickHold` skips all of it:
`bFlag0 = 0`, cursor + 1, and when the cursor reaches `nQueueLen` the queue is
closed (`nQueueLen = 0`, `bQueueActive = 0`, `nAnimPhase = 0`).

**LABEL_150** is `Tact_RefreshTeamVisibility` (0x4F368), which rewrites the current
entry into command 12, sets `nQueueLen = cursor + 2` and `bFlag1 = 1`, then runs the
visibility hook per Xcom unit.

**LABEL_111** is `Unit_UpdateVisibility(pActor)` (0x5365C). Not every exit reaches
it: the message-only exit LABEL_101 (0x5359C) and the two "morale survived" exits
(0x52D48, 0x53620) jump straight to LABEL_186. The port carries that as an explicit
flag rather than flattening it.

- **nCmd 1 (0x53668)** - the move tail. Bit 5 set: nothing. Otherwise the draw
  offsets clear and, when bit 4 is clear, `uStunOrArmor += -2 - 4*burden/strength`
  with the quotient cut to 16 bits by the `LSL#16`/`LSR#16` pair at 0x536B0. The
  layer scratch is `nZ + 2` when the ceiling sprite's signed byte at Mc1Rec+0x24 is
  strictly below -15 (`LDRSB` / `CMP #-15` at 0x536D4), else `nZ + 1`. Then the
  proximity detonation, then opportunity fire (which sets `pTactCtx272->nPhase = 1`
  and skips the rest), then LABEL_111, then the spotted-message tail gated by
  `Map_bEnemySpotted != 0 && bUnk70114 == 0` - one condition, so `bUnk70114`
  suppresses the message AND the team pass. Finally the tracked unit is dropped when
  the cell has no `bFlags44` bit 0.
- **nCmd 3 (0x53930)** - detonate, blast-scan flag to LABEL_150, else visibility,
  the spot tail, then `UnitList_ForEachRefresh`.
- **nCmd 4 (0x539B0)** - the door span. `aDirDeltaXY[nFacing] * n` for
  `n < nTurnDir` writes `nTraceX/Y/Z`, and both `bFlags29` writes index with the
  entry's own `nZ`, so they land on the same cell (bit 0 off, bit 2 on). Then 4 TU,
  visibility, the spot tail, `UnitList_ForEachRefresh`, detonation, blast-scan flag.
- **nCmd 5 (0x5381C)** - the vertical step. 8 TU, `Unit_PlaceOnMap` at
  `nZ + nFacing` (nFacing is read signed), `nDrawOffY = 0`, and a floor sprite at the
  new cell clears bit 4 and re-poses. `nLayerScratch = new nZ + 1` only when
  `nFacing == -1`.
- **nCmd 0xF (0x53BF0)** - gated on `Map_bFallDamagePending`; runs
  `Unit_ApplyFallDamage` over both rosters, clears the arming byte and
  `nFireTickProgress`, sets `nLayerScratch = nMaxLayerClamp`, then LABEL_164.
- **nCmd 0x11 (0x53CEC)** - the thrown-item landing. The flight end is three doubles
  with 16 sub-cells to a cell in X and Y and 12 to a layer. The search steps the
  layer down while the cell has no floor sprite, for at most three tests, so three
  open layers land at `base - 2`; running off the map clamps the layer into 0..3.
  The item is inserted by priority, `Sound_Play(13)`, and a `uSortKey` 14 marker is
  taken back off the cell and stamps `nFlags40 = old & 0xFFFFFF87 | 0x18` over the
  3x3 around the landing.
- **nCmd 0x12 (0x52BE0)** - the special action. First the melee target cell loses
  `bFlags29` bit 5 and the fire-animation flag `gap_70112[1]` goes down. Then
  `pWeapon->pObj->uSortKey`: 23 commits the attacker as the look unit, selects the
  target and opens screen 4. Otherwise `switch(nMode)` on 5, 4, 6, and the default
  arm tests the medikit sort key FIRST - so a medikit carried by a mode-10 or
  mode-13 action heals instead of attacking - then mode 13 (alien melee) and mode 10.

### The psi gate (0x52C90, 0x52F18, 0x53548)

    ratio = max(1600, victim.auStat[6] * victim.auStat[7])
            / (actor.auStat[6] * actor.auStat[7])
    hit   = ratio <= 1 || Game_RandU16(150) <= 100 / ratio

`_rt_sdiv` takes R0 = divisor and R1 = dividend here (proven independently at
0x1B118, where `MOVS LR,R1` tests the remainder of `nTileY % 2`), so the quotient
is victim-over-actor: a weaker attacker cannot fail.

The morale a hit leaves behind (0x52D0C, 0x52FDC, 0x535FC):

    morale = actorProduct / -150 - <600|1000> / victim.auStat[2] + victim.bMorale

clamped at zero by `MOVMI R0, R11` and truncated to a byte by `AND R0, R0, #0xFF`.
Mode 4 uses 1000, modes 5 and 10 use 600. Above 50 the victim holds; at or below 50
mode 5 panics and mode 10 stuns in place.

### The panic tail (0x52D54) and the chryssalid transform (0x53130)

Panic: the victim leaves its side list, both arms refill `uTu` from its own
`auStat[0]` (0x52E64, 0x52DC8), and then the arms differ. With
`pTactCtx272->bBusy` set the victim joins `Map_apEnemyUnits` with `bStatus = 1`,
loses `bFlags` bit 0, and the composed "<name> under alien control" is pushed forced
(the name is copied terminator-inclusive and `strcat` appends the suffix AT the
terminator). Otherwise it joins `Map_apXcomUnits` with `bStatus = 0` and becomes the
selected unit. Both arms then link `pLinked1040` to the attacker, sweep the Xcom
roster and reach LABEL_66 - `Tact_CheckBattleEnd(0)`.

Transform: the victim leaves its side list, becomes type 22 with the transform name,
and takes the type-22 record's stats with a `rand(20) - 10` jitter on HP, stat 2,
stat 3 and stat 8. Its current TU is written from the ATTACKER's maximum at 0x53194
and then overwritten by `Unit_ResetBattleState` (0x49994) - see the ledger. The cell
is saved into `pStepFromCell` before that reset because the reset clears `pCell`
(0x498E0), and the placement uses the saved cell. The victim joins the enemy roster.

Alien melee by attacker type: 14 chryssalid (converts types 0..3, 16, 17, otherwise
the HP path), 15 celacid (`90 - (1 - readiness/100) * bUnk248`, minus
`rand(power/4)`, then 100 TU charged on the victim), 19 silacoid and 20 riper (a flat
80, knock-down counter `(80 - auStat[1]/2)/10 + 1` only when
`(auStat[1] & 0xFFFE) <= 0xA0`). All three end at LABEL_93, which runs
`Unit_EnqueueIfApSpent(victim, 1)` and charges the attacker 20 TU.

### Deviations

- Cell lookups go through the port's bounds-checked `MapCellLookup`, so an out of
  map footprint or a landing below layer 0 yields NULL and is skipped, where the
  original reads a neighbouring row or the memory before the cell array.
- `_rt_sdiv` with a zero divisor is undefined in C and the ARM runtime has no test
  for it, so the port's `Fall_Div` returns 0. It guards `auStat[8]` (strength) in
  the burden term, `auStat[2]` (reaction) in the morale term and `abReady252[2]` in
  the celacid term. This is an assumption, not an observation.
- `pfnUpdateVisibility` stands for `Unit_UpdateVisibility` at every call site here
  when it is supplied, which is what makes the LABEL_111 / LABEL_101 difference
  observable in a test.
- The composed panic message is built into a bounded 140-byte buffer instead of a
  `strcat` into an unbounded one.
- `Tact_SelectUnit` and `MapCursor_SetPos` are called through their port contexts
  rather than through the Map block.


## Tact_ProcessFireAction (0x50adc): the fire-phase processor

`Tact_ProcessFireAction` is the interpreter for one queued tactical action while the
unit is in its fire phase. It reads the queue entry's `nCmd` and runs one case per
call; the phase ends by setting `pState->bFlag1` (the "this action is finished"
flag the queue walker at 0x54130 tests). Three shared exits carry the phase bookkeeping:

- LABEL_157 @ 0x52AC8 - `nPhaseCounter++`, `nPhaseTick++`, then fall into LABEL_155.
- LABEL_155/156 @ 0x52AC0 - `CMP R3,#0xB`; when the value in R3 is above 11 the phase
  ends (`bFlag1 = 1`). cmd 0x10 hands it `nPhaseTick` (0x529C4), cmd 0x12 hands it
  `nPhaseCounter` (0x52ABC) - see the ledger.
- LABEL_70 @ 0x51170 - the "no time to spend" exit used by cmd 0.

### The Map scratch the phase shares with the aim setup

The phase does not keep its own state; it reads and writes the Map block, which the
aim setup (`Tact_ComputeAimVector` @ 0x2f9c0) filled in when the shot was aimed:

| Map offset | name | role here |
|---|---|---|
| 0x13EE8 / 0x13F38 / 0x13F88 | `Map_adMtX/Y/Z` | the ten flight samples, voxel coordinates |
| 0x13EF0 / 0x13F40 / 0x13F90 | `Map_dThrowX/Y/Layer` | sample slot 1, the throw's previous position |
| 0x127A38 | `Map_dTrajBound` | the weapon's flight bound |
| 0x127A30 | `Map_dArcDenom` | the throw arc's denominator |
| 0x1279BC..C4 | `Map_nAimOriginX/Y/Z` | the muzzle, voxel coordinates |
| 0x14040..48 | `Map_nAimTargetX/Y/Z` | the cell the samples last fell into |
| 0x14020 | `Map_dTravel` | this phase's own travelled distance |
| 0x14038 | `Map_dTravelSave` | the distance the aim's arc walk took (0x302D0, 0x323BC) |
| 0x1406C | `Map_bFireHitResult` | 1 when the aim's arc walk left the map (0x2FC54 clears, 0x3010C sets) |
| 0x1406D | `Map_bTrajHitStop` | cmd 0x11's throw gate; the port calls it ThrowPending |
| 0x1139E0 | `Map_nBurstShots` | how many shots the burst still owes |

`Map_dTravel` is reset to 0.0 by the aim setup and is NOT touched by the arc walk, so
the flight starts from zero on every action. `Map_dTravelSave` is the arc walk's own
length, which is why the shot lands when `dTravel` passes it.

### cmd 0 - turn

`nPhaseTick++`; the phase ends when `nPhaseMax < nPhaseTick`. When the unit has no TU
left, or the armour/TU warning hook refuses, the action ends through LABEL_70 with a
`MOVE_MSG_NO_TIME` push and a team-wide visibility pass; otherwise `uTu--`. Facing
wraps with `>7 -> -8` and `<0 -> +8`. After `Unit_UpdateVisibility`, a spotted enemy
(and `!Map_bUnk70114`) clears `bAiDone` and pushes the "spotted" text record.

### cmd 1 - the fire-frame step

`bFlags & 0x20` (the shot-trace mark) returns without ending the phase. The anim phase
byte advances and wraps `>7 -> 0`; TU is spent on even ticks only (`nPhaseTick % 2 == 0`).
At tick 4 the unit is re-placed at `pStepFromCell + facing delta`. The eight facings each
get their own draw-offset ladder built from `nHalf = (t<=3 ? t+1 : t-7)` and
`nNeg = (t<=3 ? -1-t : 7-t)`; the final term adds or subtracts `nStepFrameDiv * t` on Y.
Both offsets are truncated to `i8`. The kneel/stand toggle runs only at tick 4 and only
for unit types whose `g_aUnitTypeFlag0` entry is 1: standing when the destination cell
has a floor sprite, kneeling when it does not, each followed by `Unit_UpdateAnimPose`.
The phase ends when the tick passes 6.

### cmd 3 - the door

At tick 3 the entry's own cell is looked up. Facing 2 swaps `pWallSprA`/`pWallSprB`
downwards (`nGlobalIdx - 1`), any other facing swaps them upwards (`nGlobalIdx + 1`),
each through `Font_GetSprByIndex`. The phase ends at tick 4.

### cmd 4, 5, 8 - small cases

cmd 4 advances the anim phase and ends past tick 3. cmd 5 sets
`nDrawOffY = -2 * nPhaseTick * (i8)nFacing`. cmd 8 is a large-unit / non-zero-arg bail
out; otherwise the anim phase advances until tick 8, which zeroes it and ends the phase.

### The arc's verdict: `Map_bFireHitResult @ 0x1406C`

`Tact_TraceProjectileArc` clears it at 0x2FC54 on every call and sets it to 1 at 0x3010C
in the same branch that clears `Map.bFireStatus1` and ends the walk - the branch taken when
the walked sample leaves the map (`x<0 || y<0 || z<0 || x >= 160*nMapDimX || y >= 160*nMapDimX
|| z >= 47`). The fire phase reads it at five places (0x519BC, 0x51C3C, 0x51EE4, 0x51F50,
0x5287C) and never writes it, so all five reads inside one action return what the aim setup
left there. It means "the traced arc already ran off the map", which is why such a shot
resolves on its first pass instead of stamping the muzzle layer.

Both writes are invisible to an xref search: 0x2FC54 is `MOV R11,#0x14000; ORR R11,R11,#0x6C;
STRB R3,[R0,R11]!` and 0x3010C writes through a stack-held pointer. An earlier draft of this
report named the field `Map_bFireInFlight` and recorded it as never written - that was the
xref blind spot, and the name and the ledger row are corrected here.

### cmd 0xE - the shot in flight

Refuses unless the unit carries the aiming flag (0x04). `dTravel += 10.0`. For each of
the ten samples the OLD sample's cell loses the 0x20 trace mark, then the sample is
recomputed from the muzzle at `dBack = dTravel - i * 1.41`; a sample whose `dBack` is
not positive is parked at -1000.0 on all three axes. The samples are measured from the
muzzle, not from the unit's head, so at travel 10 the first eight samples are still
inside the muzzle cell.

The shot keeps flying unless `dTravel > dTravelSave`, or the weapon's sort key is one
of the two multi-target keys (13, 35) and the burst still owes shots while
`dTravel >= dTrajBound`. While flying, the muzzle layer scratch is set from
`1 - (int)(z * (-1/12))` and every sample's cell is stamped with the 0x20 mark.

On the resolve path a non-mode-7 shot clears the fire-status byte; a mode-7 shot whose
arc stayed on the map instead stamps the muzzle layer. Inside mode 7, the shot resolves
only when the arc is exhausted or the burst is spent; the resolution writes
`nStepZDelta`'s low byte to 1, sets the fall-damage pending flag, and re-sweeps the
samples with the integer conversion form. The tail sets `bFireStatus9` from the same
arc-off-map flag (1 means the arc left the map), zeroes `nFireTickProgress` and ends
the phase.

### cmd 0xF, 0x10, 0x11, 0x12

cmd 0xF waits for the fall-damage pending flag while the arc stayed on the map, counts to
10 and ends. cmd 0x10 sweeps all four layers x `10*nDimY` x `10*nDimX` cells and decays
every cell whose `nFlags32 & 0x78` is non-zero, ending past tick 11. cmd 0x11 is the
throw: the step is `5.0` or `(dBound/|dZ|) * 5.0` when the rise exceeds the bound, the
previous sample moves into slot 1, and the new position uses the ballistic drop term
`(travel^2 * G) / ((arcDenom^2 * cos(pitch)) * cos(pitch) * 2)`. The landing is stamped
only while `dTravel <= dTravelSave` and inside `x,y < 160*nDimX`, `z < 47`. cmd 0x12
stamps the 0x20 mark on the cell the samples last fell into.

### Two conversion forms for the same sample

The shot loop converts a sample height to a layer with `(int)(z * (1/12))` (0x51264);
the three resolve loops use `(int)z / 12` (0x51E5C, 0x52124, 0x527B8). 1/12 is not
exact in binary, so at a height that is an exact multiple of 12 the two disagree by one
layer, and the muzzle heights the aim setup builds are `12*nZ + 6`, which makes the
case reachable. The port keeps both forms in separate helpers so the difference stays
visible.

### Deviations

- Cell lookups go through the port's bounds-checked `FireCell`, so an out-of-map
  sample or a NULL grid slot yields NULL and is skipped, where the original reads the
  neighbouring row or aborts on a NULL pointer.
- `pStepFromCell` is tested before it is dereferenced for the cmd 1 scratch cell. The
  original reads it unconditionally; the phase owner is expected to have set it.
- `Map_bFireHitResult` is carried as a caller-supplied byte rather than read from a Map
  block; the port's producer for it is `ShotTrace.bLeftMap` in `Tact_TraceProjectileArc`.
- `Map_TraceVoxelOccupancy` reads its two skipped units from `Map.pSelUnit @ 0x15334` and
  `Map.pThrowTargetUnit @ 0x150F0`; the port passes them as arguments. An earlier version
  of `GameMap` claimed a `Soldier *` exclusion pair at 0x1406C/0x14070 - those two slots are
  `Map.bFireHitResult` (a byte) and `Map.pArrowThrownItem` (a `TactItem *`), and the claim
  is removed.
- `Map_TraceLos` also writes `Map_adMtX/Y/Z[0]` (0x30CE0, 0x30EE0); the port's LOS
  helper does not reproduce that side effect.
- No app-layer wiring exists yet for `FireActionCtx`: the queue walker
  `Tact_TickActiveUnit` @ 0x54130 is unported, so the phase is driven from tests only.


## Tact_TickActiveUnit (0x54130): the queue walker

`Tact_TickActiveUnit` is the only thing `GameTick_OnTimer @ 0x274f0` does with the action
queue, and it is the link that was missing between the three phase processors and the game
tick. It is a loop, not a single dispatch.

### The gates

1. If `nQueueLen == 0`, `Tact_ProcessActionPhase` runs first - the phase machine can
   enqueue the opportunity-fire action, and 0x54198 re-reads the length, so a queue that
   looked empty is dispatched on the same call.
2. Return when `nQueueLen == 0` or `bQueueActive == 0`. These are two independent gates.
3. **`bFlag0` selects the processor**: set runs `Tact_ProcessFireAction`, clear runs
   `Tact_ProcessMoveAction`. They are alternatives, not both - which is why the move
   processor's prologue raising `bFlag0` matters: it flips the next tick to the fire phase.

### The camera follow

Only while `pTactCtx272->bBusy`. The current entry is `aQueue[nQueueCursor]` (aQueue is at
`TactState+0x18`, an entry is 56 bytes), and its command decides what the camera follows:

| nCmd | follows | tracked unit adopted |
|---|---|---|
| 0, 1, 8 | `pUnit->pCell`, gated on `pCell->bFlags44 & 1` | the unit, **before** the focus |
| 0xE | the cell the last aim sample fell into | `Map_apXcomUnits[0]`, **after** the focus |
| 0x12 | the same sample cell, gated on `pTarget->pCell->bFlags44 & 1` | `pTarget`, **after** the focus |

With nothing tracked the camera always follows. With a unit already tracked, a shot
re-centres only when `(int)Map_dTravel % 60 == 0` (0x54750).

The move path has a step the fire path does not: when the context is busy and
`nQueueLen > 1` it clears `Map_pSelUnit`'s `bUnk148` and, if the selected unit is not the
camera unit, drops `pCameraUnit` and calls `Render_Frame`. And when `nQueueCursor == 0` it
zeroes the kill accumulator before the move processor runs.

### The completion tail (bFlag1 raised)

`Tact_ProcessFallAction` runs, then `Map_bTickHold` or `Map_bFrameScratch` returns. Then:

- **The AI-action pair.** `TactState+0x111C8` and `+0x111E2` are one pair and neither was
  named before this unit (`gap_70088` head, `bUnk70114`). `EnemyAi_TryFireOrWander (0x4ABC8,
  unported)` stores the acting unit at +0x111C8 (0x4AC04) and raises +0x111E2 (0x4AC1C)
  together, and it does so **unconditionally, before** the branch at 0x4ACA0 that chooses
  between the random fire burst and the weapon-drop-and-wander. So the flag means "an AI
  action is in progress", not "a wander is running" - which is what its two other readers
  need it to mean: the move processor suppresses the player-facing "not enough time" record
  while it is set, and the fire processor skips the enemy-spotted reaction while it is set.
  It is cleared on the wander path's failure (0x4B024) - the fire path never clears it - by
  `Tact_InitMission`, and by the walker: when the queue has finished it clears the flag and
  zeroes the acting unit's `uTu` through the pointer (0x544E0, `STRHEQ R1,[R3,#6]`). Named
  `pAiActionUnit` / `bAiActionActive` in the IDB struct and in the port.
- **The kill credit.** `TactState+0x111D0` is a u16 accumulator. The walker walks
  `aQueue[0 .. nQueueCursor-1]` - and because `Fall_Tail` has already advanced the cursor
  past the entry it just ran, that range is every executed entry - and stops at the first
  one whose command is 14, whose unit has `nUnitType <= 8` and is operative. That unit's
  `uKills` (Soldier+0xFA) gets the accumulator, which is then zeroed as a dword.
- **The opportunity-fire epilogue.** On `bUnk70103`: park the cursor at (-2,-2), select
  `pTactCtx272->pScanUnit` - falling back to `Map_apXcomUnits[0]` when that unit carries
  `bFlags` bit 0x20 - and clear the flag. Then `Tact_ProcessActionPhase` runs once more.

### The re-run

After the tail (and also when `bFlag1` was never raised): re-run while the context is busy,
`pTrackUnit` is NULL, `pMapTactical->bUnk70115` is clear and `apUiSlotsA[10]`
(`dword_113A40`, the cursor-direction countdown) is 0, calling `GameTick_Step` on each pass.
The countdown is read **after** the game tick, so a running countdown still allows one tick.

### Deviations

- The walker reaches everything the original reads through the Map block as context fields:
  `Map_pSelUnit`, `Map_apXcomUnits[0]`, `Map_bTickHold`, `Map_bFrameScratch`,
  `apUiSlotsA[10]`, the aim samples and `Map_dTravel`. The three phase processors get their
  own contexts, so `TactTickCtx` is where the port wires them to the queue.
- The five world calls (`Tact_ProcessActionPhase`, `Render_Frame`, `MapView_FocusOnCell`,
  `MapCursor_SetPos`, `GameTick_Step`) are injected through `TickHooks`, so the walker is
  testable without a renderer or a camera.
- The port guards `pUnit`, `pCell`, `pTarget` and `pAiActionUnit` before dereferencing, and
  routes the sample-cell index through the bounds-checked lookup. Six ledger rows record
  where the original does not.
- No app-layer wiring yet: `GameTick_OnTimer`'s `pfnTickActiveUnit` seam is still unfilled,
  because the app layer does not yet own a `TactTickCtx`.


## EnemyAi_TryFireOrWander (0x4abc8): the low-morale AI

The AI that runs when an alien's morale breaks. A LARGE unit does nothing at all -
0x4abdc branches straight to the function epilogue, so it does not even push the status
message, and `Map.pSelWeapon` is not even cleared.

### The choice

`Game_RandU16(2)` is drawn first, then the AI-action pair is raised -
`pMapTactical->pAiActionUnit = pUnit` (0x4AC04) and `bAiActionActive = 1` (0x4AC1C) -
and only then does 0x4ac94 choose: `roll == 0` AND a usable one-handed weapon gives the
random fire burst, anything else gives the weapon-drop-and-wander. The pair is raised on
BOTH paths, which is why it cannot mean "a wander is running".

A usable weapon (0x4ac24..0x4ac90) is a hand that exists, whose `ObjectRec.bTwoHanded`
is 0, and which either has ammo or whose `ObjectRec.bAmmoCap` is 255. Left hand first,
right second; the winner is stored into `Map.pSelWeapon` (0x113A00), which was zeroed at
0x4AC20. The store happens before the path choice, so a unit that ends up wandering still
leaves its weapon in `Map.pSelWeapon` - and then, for `nUnitType <= 3`, drops that very
item into a cell list, leaving the global pointing at an item the unit no longer holds.

Both paths end at 0x4B028 pushing the unit's name through `StatusMsg_Push` with
`bForce = 0`. The original strcat's `unk_104078` onto the name; that buffer is all zeros
and its only three references in the whole binary are this call site, so it appends
nothing.

### The fire burst (0x4aca4..0x4ae28)

`Map.nActionMode = 1`, then `Ui_FillActionCosts`. Shot count is
`bAmmoCap == 255 ? 3 : min(nAmmo, 3)`; a count of 0 skips the loop but still clears the
action latch and kicks the queue. Each pass draws `x = nX + rand(5) - 2`,
`y = nY + rand(5) - 2`, `layer = rand(4)` into three Map scratch globals
(`Map_nAiFireX/Y/Layer` @ 0x128A20/0x128A24/0x128A28, which have no other reference
anywhere in the binary) and retries until `Map_IsValidCell` accepts it. Then:

- drawn x is not the shooter's column -> burst at the drawn target;
- drawn x IS the shooter's column -> the drawn row is replaced by the shooter's own row,
  and **a shooter not on row 0 jumps back to the draw without spending a shot**
  (0x4ada4 `BNE loc_4ACE0`, not to the 0x4ae0c decrement), while a shooter on row 0 fires
  at its own cell.

This is the one place Hex-Rays actively misleads: its pseudocode falls through to the
decrement, which would fire zero shots where the ARM fires one. The test
`TestSameColumnRedraw` pins it - one scripted shot, a rejected same-column draw, and the
shot still lands, with 7 draws consumed (1 roll + 3 + 3).

Each burst takes `nTuCost = Map.anActionCost[mode]` (Map+0x4E4C) and
`nArg = Map.anActionEnabled[mode]` (Map+0x4E7C) - the same two tables
`Tact_TryFireMode4` and `Input_OnPointerUp` read, and the same pair
`Tact_TryFireMode4`'s UI path passes. The AI ignores the enqueue's result: a unit that
cannot afford the burst gets nothing queued, and the latch clear, the queue kick and the
name push still happen.

### The wander (0x4ae2c..0x4b024)

`nUnitType <= 3` first drops both hands. From the unit's own layer it walks DOWN while
`MapCell.pFloorSpr == NULL`; `SUB R7,#1 / CMP R7,#0 / BGT` at 0x4ae84-0x4ae90 means
layers nZ..1 are tested and **layer 0 is reached untested**. Both items go into that cell
through `MapCell_ListInsertByPri`, the hands are cleared, `Unit_UpdateAnimPose` runs.
Types 4..23 skip the whole block, including the pose refresh.

Then it draws `x = nX + rand(20) - 10`, `y = nY + rand(20) - 10` and retries until
`Map_IsValidCell(map, x, y, 0)` accepts it - the bounds test is always against layer 0.
The candidate cell is taken at the UNIT'S OWN layer. If `g_aUnitTypeFlag0[type] == 0` the
candidate is walked DOWN while `pFloorSpr == NULL`, and this walk's `SUBS / BPL` at
0x4afcc-0x4afd0 tests layers nZ..0 inclusive - one layer deeper than the drop walk in the
same function. The draw is retried while the candidate is the unit's own cell or
`MapCell_HasOccupant` says it is occupied.

Finally `Unit_PathToCell(map, cell->nX, cell->nY, cell->nZ, 1)`. On failure the unit is
left with `uTu = 0` and `bAiActionActive` is cleared (0x4b00c..0x4b024); on success the
flag stays up and the queue walker's completion tail (0x544D8) is what clears it.

### Original bugs found (7 ledger rows)

Four unguarded dereferences: the drop descent loads `apCells[layer][y][x]` and reads its
`pFloorSpr` with no NULL test (0x4ae74), the wander walk does the same (0x4afbc), both
hand drops pass that cell to `MapCell_ListInsertByPri`, which dereferences
`pCell->pItemList` (0x4aec4), and `byte_A7B80` is indexed by `nUnitType` with no bounds
test (0x4af8c). Three behavioural ones: the drop descent tests layers nZ..1 while the
floor walk in the same function tests nZ..0 (0x4ae8c); the same-column redraw that spends
no shot and lets a row-0 shooter fire at its own cell (0x4ada4); and `Map.pSelWeapon`
left pointing at an item the wander path just dropped (0x4ac90).

### Deviations

- `Unit_PathToCell` (0x2c2a8) is unported - it needs `Unit_CanStepTo` (0x27bb8) - so it is
  a hook on `EnemyAiActCtx`, as is `Ui_FillActionCosts` (the port's version takes an
  explicit env the AI does not own) and `StatusMsg_Push` (which needs a `StatusStack`).
- The port guards the four dereferences the original does not, and bounds the
  `nUnitType` index against `PUFO_UNIT_TYPE_COUNT`.
- The three draw scratch globals are kept as locals, which is faithful: they have no
  reader outside this function.
- The name copy is bounded to `Soldier.szName` (40) and to the 200-byte message buffer;
  the original's `LDRSB` loop has neither bound.

## Tact_EnemyAiTick (0x4cbe0): the enemy AI driver

`Tact_ProcessActionPhase` reaches this through `TurnHooks.pfnEnemyAiTick` when the context
is busy and the phase is 3. It handles **one** enemy per call and ends the enemy turn when
nothing was queued. Ported as `Tact_EnemyAiTick` in `src/pufo/game/pufo_enemyai.c`.

### Entry and unit selection (0x4cbf4..0x4cc5c)

`STRB R0,[R1,#0x100]` clears a **byte** at `pTactCtx272+0x100`. Hex-Rays renders the field as
`Soldier *pSavedFocus` because every read is `LOBYTE(pCtx->pSavedFocus)`, but all seven
accesses in the binary are 0/1 byte stores or tests (0x4CC00, 0x4D688, 0x4D84C, 0x4D86C,
0x4D878, 0x4D888, and the test at 0x4D920) and nothing ever loads it as an address. The unit
the enemy turn restores is at +0x104, which is what `Tact_EndEnemyTurn` reads. The port names
the field `bAiFocusSaved`.

`CMP R3,#0; BLS loc_4D920` sends an empty enemy roster straight to the tail. Otherwise the
roster is walked in order and the first unit passing every gate acts:

| gate | ARM | effect |
|---|---|---|
| `nAiTick > 15` | 0x4CC34 `CMP R0,#0xF; BGT` | skipped **without** `++nAiTick`, so it stays skipped forever |
| `bAiDone` | 0x4CC48 `CMP R3,#0; BNE` | skipped, after `++nAiTick` |
| `uTu >= 15` | 0x4CC54 `CMP R3,#0xF; MOVCC/STRBCC` | this unit acts |
| otherwise | same | `bAiDone = 1`, skipped |

### What the acting unit does

1. `Unit_UpdateVisibility(pUnit)`, then `pTrackUnit = NULL` unless it already points at this
   unit (0x4CC78).
2. `bMorale < 20 && nUnitType > 3` hands the unit to the panic AI: `Tact_SelectUnit`,
   `EnemyAi_TryFireOrWander`, focus saved, `bAiDone = 1`, tail.
3. Up to three draws of `apMultiTargets[rand(nMultiTarget)]`, stopping at the first one that
   is not large. `nMultiTarget` is read as a **signed** byte (0x4D194 `LDRSB`).
4. The pick is accepted when it is small, not type 16/17, `rand(5) == 0` and the roster is
   non-empty (0x4cd60..0x4cda0). Accepted -> the neighbour-melee hand-off below. Otherwise
   LABEL_24: `nMultiTarget == 0` goes to the fallback move; else `Tact_SelectUnit(self)` and
   a split on `g_aUnitTypeRecord[4*type + 3]` (`LDRB R3,[R3,#3]` at 0x4CDBC). That column is
   set for exactly six rows - Chryssalid 0xE, Celacid 0xF, both civilians 0x10/0x11, Silacoid
   0x13 and Riper 0x14 - and this is its only reader in the whole binary, so the port names it
   `g_aUnitTypeFlag3`. Those are the units with no weapon to fire and only a melee action.

### The neighbour-melee hand-off (0x4d660..0x4d734)

Another enemy is searched for with `bPsiActive != 0`, `!= self` and `uTu > 15`. Found:
`Tact_SelectUnit(that unit)`, `Map.pSelWeapon = &TactItem_156910`, mode 4 or 5 by `rand(2)`,
`Map.nBurstShots = 0`, the three melee-cell globals set to the multi-target's cell, a
command-18 enqueue against that cell's occupant, then `Map_pSelUnit->uTu >>= 1`
(`LDRH/LSR#1/STRH` at 0x4d728..0x4d730). Every one of those addresses the neighbour: the unit
this tick was picked for spends no TU, is not marked done, and is picked again next tick.
Ledger row 0x4d660.

### The melee branch (0x4cde0..0x4d188)

Three attempts. Each draws a fresh multi-target, loads the cell one row north and the two
other cells of a large unit's 2x2 footprint (0x4ce50, unguarded), and builds a candidate: the
cell at the unit's facing delta **on the target's layer**, falling back to the target's own
cell when that cell is out of bounds or is not occupied by the target (0x4CEC4). Reach is
`(int)sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2) < 2` from the unit's own cell, or - for a large unit - from any of its
four footprint cells (0x4D048..0x4D098). On reach: `uTu = 0`, the three melee globals, and a
command-18 enqueue with mode 13 carrying `&TactItem_156A58`.

On no reach, eight directions are scanned (0x4D09C..0x4D150). The layer is `nZ + 1` when the
unit's own ceiling sprite has `iCeilParam < -15` (`MOV R6,#0xFFFFFFF1; CMP` at 0x4D0D8),
otherwise `nZ` - note `Unit_UpdateVisibility` uses the same byte with a **-10** threshold, so
the two thresholds really differ. An occupant counts when `bStatus == 0` or its type is 16 or
17. A hit faces the unit and enqueues command 13. Otherwise `Unit_PathToCell(target, bFlag 0)`;
success ends the tick, failure retries until the three attempts are spent.

### The throw / fire branch (0x4d194..0x4d8b0)

A fresh multi-target and `rand(3)`. The throw needs roll 0, distance <= 10, a non-NULL
`apBelt[0]` whose object has `nCategory == 3`, and `nUnitType > 3`. It moves the belt item to
`pHandR` and into `Map.pSelWeapon`, refills the action costs, stores `pHandR` into
`Map.pSelWeapon` a second time (0x4D818), sets the item's +7 to 0 and +8 to 1, sets action
mode 11, and enqueues with `Map_nThrowTuCost` / `Map_nThrowArg` - loaded by literal at 0x4D82C
and 0x4D80C, and just `anActionCost[11]` / `anActionEnabled[11]`.

Otherwise the weapon is the left hand for types > 3 (refusing when it is empty, and leaving
`Map.pSelWeapon` untouched), or for types <= 3 the last hand holding a one-handed object with
`nCategory <= 2`, so the right hand wins ties. After `Ui_FillActionCosts` and
`TactItem_bTryReloadClip`, mode 7 is chosen when the weapon object's `uSortKey == 13`, the
target is not type 16/17 and the distance is >= 10 - and mode 7 also arms
`Map.nMultiTargetCount = 1`, `Map.nBurstShots = 1` and `Map.apMultiTargets[0]`. Otherwise mode 1.

The affordability gate is soft-float at 0x4d448 / 0x4d458:

    (double)uTu >= anActionCost[mode] * (2.0 / 3.0) + 8.0

with `0x3FE5555555555555` = 2/3 and `0x4020000000000000` = 8.0, and the charged cost is the
truncated `(int)(cost * 2/3)`, not the table value. A 26-cost mode therefore needs 26 TU and
charges 17.

### The fallback move (LABEL_82, 0x4d8b8..0x4d918)

Rank 4 or 8 draws `rand(6)` and keeps it only when it is 1; every other rank draws `rand(3)`.
A draw of 0 turns the unit through `EnemyAi_EnqueueRandomTurn` and marks it done. Otherwise the
RMP walk starts at `rand(nRmpCount)` and, because the index is incremented **before** it is
used (0x4D8F8), that first draw is never itself a candidate - it only picks where the walk
begins; the index wraps at `nRmpCount - 1`. A node is a candidate when
`sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2) <= 19.875` (`_led` against `0x403E000000000000`, on the **untruncated**
sqrt, unlike every reach test above) and the node's byte at +0x1A matches the unit type - the
original reaches it by casting the node to a `Soldier *` so the read lands on
`Soldier.nMultiTarget`. On a candidate the unit is selected and `Unit_PathToCell(node, bFlag 1)`
runs; success saves the focus, failure counts toward a limit of 10, past which the unit is
marked done. After `nRmpCount` nodes have been scanned the tick moves to the **next** enemy
unit - the only path that does not end the roster loop.

### The tail (0x4d920)

`pTactCtx272->nPhase = 3`, then `Tact_EndEnemyTurn` only when the +0x100 byte is still 0, then
`TactState_KickQueue(pMapTactical)`. Because `Tact_EndEnemyTurn` writes phase 0 back, a tick
where nothing acted leaves the machine at phase 0, and a tick that queued something leaves it
at 3.

### Original bugs found (3 ledger rows)

- 0x4d660 - the neighbour-melee hand-off described above.
- 0x4d09c - the eight-direction scan indexes `apCells` with no bounds test at all, unlike the
  facing-delta lookup at 0x4ce8c, which does call `Map_IsValidCell`.
- 0x4ce50 - the three footprint cells are loaded the same unguarded way.

### Deviations

- `Unit_PathToCell` (0x2c2a8, unported - it needs `Unit_CanStepTo`, 0x27bb8),
  `Ui_FillActionCosts`, `Unit_UpdateVisibility` (ported, but it needs a whole `VisCtx`),
  `AfterEnemyStep` (0x4c4a0, unported) and the clip lookup inside `TactItem_bTryReloadClip`
  are hooks on `EnemyAiTickCtx`.
- The port bounds-checks the footprint and eight-direction cell reads and the `nUnitType`
  index into `g_aUnitTypeFlag3`.
- The RMP node's role byte is passed to the shared predicate directly instead of through the
  original's `Soldier *` cast, because `Soldier` shifts on Win64 and the cast would read the
  wrong byte. `EnemyAi_MultiTargetTypeMatch` and the RMP walk now share one role-based core.
- `TactCtx272+0x100` is typed `u8 bAiFocusSaved` with 3 pad bytes, not `Soldier *`.
- `unk_156910`, `unk_156A58` and `unk_156A88` are typed `TactItem` in the IDB and named
  `TactItem_156910` / `TactItem_156A58` / `TactItem_156A88`: each has a `TactItem_ctor` thunk
  (0x37124, 0x37134, 0x37088) and `Tact_InitMission` stores an `apObjects` entry into its
  `pObj` at +0. The port previously modelled them as `ObjectRec **` pointer variables.

## The enemy-turn bracket: BeforeEnemyStep (0x4b9b8), Tact_UpdateUnitControl (0x4a444), AfterEnemyStep (0x4c4a0)

`BeforeEnemyStep` and `AfterEnemyStep` bracket the enemy turn, and both call
`Tact_UpdateUnitControl` once per unit - which is why the enemy pass runs before the XCom one:
BeforeEnemyStep clears the idempotence guard byte `Soldier.bControlRecovered` (+0x1B2) for the
enemy roster at 0x4BB80, AfterEnemyStep for the civilians (0x4C8B0) and the XCom roster
(0x4C720). Ported as `BeforeEnemyStep`, `Tact_UpdateUnitControl` and `AfterEnemyStep` in
`src/pufo/game/pufo_turn.c`, driven from `tests/test_turn.c`.

### Tact_UpdateUnitControl (0x4a444..0x4a714)

Guard first (0x4a450): `bControlRecovered` non-zero returns at once, and the function sets it,
so each unit is processed once per turn. The unit arithmetic - `uHp -= bKneelOrPrimed` (floored
at 0), `bUnk1037 = 0`, the TU rule (+3 when the cell's `nFlags32` low 3 bits are non-zero, else
-10 when `uTuSpent >= 10`, else 0, and left alone entirely for a large unit), morale +5 or 100
from 95 up - is the already-ported `Unit_ApplyControlRecovery`. The original applies morale
last, at 0x4A714; the port applies it with the rest because nothing in between reads it.

The recovery arm (0x4A4E0..0x4A5A4) needs all of: `uTuSpent < uHp`, `bFlags` bit 0x20 SET, the
cell unoccupied, `uHp != 0`, not large. It enqueues RECOVER, and for `nUnitType <= 3` pushes
`szName` + aTextRecs record 39 (male) or 40 (female) as a FORCED status message, then
`TactState_KickQueue` and `pLinked1040 = 0`.

Both side transfers (0x4A5A8, 0x4A64C) need bit 0x20 CLEAR - the opposite polarity. An
XCom-side unit of an enemy type becomes an enemy (`bStatus = 1`, `uTu = 0`, appended to
`apEnemyUnits`, and `Tact_SelectUnit(apXcomUnits[0])` if it was `Map.pSelUnit`); a controlled
unit of an XCom type returns to `apXcomUnits` and pushes name + record 52 / 53 unprompted.
`Tact_RemoveUnitFromSideLists` runs first and updates the canonical counts, which the port has
to do explicitly because `SideLists` carries its counts by value - the same `Fall_SyncCounts`
pattern.

### BeforeEnemyStep (0x4b9b8..0x4c49c)

Eight steps: clear `pTrackUnit` and the XCom `bUnk1037`; the XCom-base reserve spawn; the enemy
pass (`bControlRecovered = 0`, `Tact_UpdateUnitControl`, `nAiTick = 0`, with the count re-read
each iteration); the fire tick over all four layers; clear the flag for civilians then XCom; the
enemy refill (`uTu = auStat[0]`, `uStunOrArmor = auStat[9]`); clear `bFlags44` bit 0 everywhere;
`UnitList_ForEachRefresh`.

**The burn run probes against its own axis.** 0x4BC78 multiplies the axis delta by a counter
running 0, -1, -2, so with the west axis the probe steps EAST over three cells and the forward
pass then starts at `cell + axisDelta * (nBack + 1)` - two cells east of the burning cell - and
walks back west across at most 7 cells. `tests/test_turn.c::TestBeforeEnemyStepBurnRun` pins
this with three layouts that differ only in where the wall gap is.

**The face loop makes six passes over four counters.** Passes 4 and 5 are the west and north
neighbour cells, gated on that neighbour burning, and both rewrite the slot index (0x4C09C
`MOV R1, #1`, 0x4C0EC `MOV R1, #2`). They therefore charge the cell's own wall A / wall B
counter through the same wall sprite - a wall between two burning cells takes double damage -
and nothing in the loop ever reaches `nPathCost` at +0x14.

**The heat term is `counter + step`, and it is added twice.** 0x4C10C / 0x4C110 build
`R2 = counter + 20` (or +5), 0x4C15C compares that against `Mc1Rec.bStrength`, 0x4C160 zeroes
it when the sprite covers it, and 0x4C1F0 stores `counter + R2`. So a sprite absorbs the hit
whenever `bStrength >= counter + step` - a `bStrength` of 255 always does - and the only
counters that ever grow belong to faces with no sprite, growing to `2 * counter + step`.

**The countdowns are gated by the burning state.** The `nFlags40` bits 3..6 decrement unless
zero or already 0xF (0x4C014). If `nFlags32`'s low 3 bits are 0 the cell takes no further
countdown at all (0x4C038); if they are non-zero but not 4 the face loop is skipped while the
low 3-bit countdown still runs (0x4C040); at 0 the burning state steps down and the countdown
re-arms to `rand(2) + 2`.

### AfterEnemyStep (0x4c4a0..0x4c9f8)

`nEnemyUnitCount / 3` random enemies are topped up to `auStat[0] * 0.4` - the constant pair at
0x4C520 / 0x4C528 is `0x3FD99999` / `0x9999999A`, i.e. 0.4, which Hex-Rays prints as two raw
halves and reads easily as 0.2. The comparison is `uTu < cap` and the store is `(u16)cap`, so
the top-up never lowers uTu. Then the proximity tick plus `bFlags44` bit 0 over every cell; the
right-hand action item of every enemy with `nUnitType > 3` back to `apBelt[0]` with its `bUnk8`
cleared; `bUnk148 = 0` for every enemy; the XCom refill
`q = (4 * uInvBurden - 4) / auStat[8]`, `d = (2 * q * auStat[0]) / 10`, `uTu = auStat[0] - d`,
then `uStunOrArmor += auStat[9] * auStat[8] / (10 * uInvBurden)` capped at `auStat[9]`;
`Tact_UpdateUnitControl` for XCom then the civilians; the panic AI for every XCom unit under 20
morale; `Unit_UpdateVisibility` for every enemy; `TactState_KickQueue` and the two refreshes;
and finally `bUnk1037 = 0` for the XCom roster.

`auStat[8]` is the mean-stun stat. Hex-Rays prints it as `auStat[offsetof(Soldier,
uStunOrArmor)]`, which reads like `auStat[9]` and is not - the penalty divisor and the stun
numerator's second factor are different fields.

### Original bugs found (12 ledger rows)

- 0x4C1F0 - the heat term is added to the counter twice, so a face with no sprite grows to
  `2 * counter + step`.
- 0x4C09C / 0x4C0EC - the neighbour passes reuse the wall A / wall B counter and sprite.
- 0x4C158 - a sprite absorbs the hit when `bStrength >= counter + step`, so 255 always absorbs
  and only sprite-less faces accumulate.
- 0x4BC78 - the burn-run probe steps against the run direction.
- 0x4BCD4 / 0x4BE40 - the burn walk dereferences neighbour cell pointers with no null test.
- 0x4BC88 - `Map_IsValidCell` is called with layer 0 while the index uses the cell's own `nZ`.
- 0x4BF84 - a negative fire-damage base gets +3 before the shift, so the roll range can exceed
  the base.
- 0x4A4FC vs 0x4A5C8 / 0x4A66C - the recovery arm needs `bFlags` bit 0x20 SET, both transfers
  need it CLEAR.
- 0x4A604 / 0x4A6A4 - both transfers append at the current roster count with no bound.
- 0x4A544 - the status message is built in a 52-byte buffer from a 40-byte name plus a
  200-byte TEXTS record.
- 0x4C77C - the XCom refill divides by `auStat[8]` and `uInvBurden` with no zero guard, and
  `4 * uInvBurden - 4` is negative at burden 0.
- 0x4C014 - BeforeEnemyStep guards the 0x78 countdown against its maximum; GameTick_Step
  (0x27324) shares the arithmetic with no such guard.

### Deviations

- `MapCell_TickProximityItems`, `Map_RefreshCellMeta`, `UnitList_ForEachRefresh`,
  `Unit_UpdateVisibility`, `Game_RandU16`, `Tact_SelectUnit`, `StatusMsg_Push`,
  `EnemyAi_TryFireOrWander` and `Rmp_PickSpawnForUnit` are seams on `EnemyStepCtx`; the app
  layer owns no `TactTickCtx` yet, so nothing in the app builds the context.
- The port bounds-checks the burn walk's neighbour cell reads and the countdown's grid slot
  reads, where the original dereferences them.
- `Turn_PushUnitNameMsg` truncates instead of overflowing the 52-byte buffer.
- `AfterEnemyStep` skips both burden terms when the divisor is zero.
- `MapCell.abFaceDamage` is indexed through the field, not through the original's
  `pCell + 0x10 + slot`: on Win64 `MapCell`'s widened pointers move that field and a raw offset
  lands on `pWallSprB`. `Cell_FaceDamage` was removed for the same reason.

## The tactical map click: Tact_HandleMapClick (0x1512c) and TactAction_ConfirmMeleeMode6 (0x17bb8)

Ported in `src/pufo/game/pufo_input.c` (`Tact_HandleMapClick`, `MapClickCtx`) and
`src/pufo/game/pufo_tactui.c` (`Ui_ConfirmMeleeMode6`). These were the last two addresses
`audit_names` flagged, so every credited address in the port now has a function behind it.

### Tact_HandleMapClick (0x1512c, 1104 B)

Reached only from `Input_OnAction @ 0x15668`, and only when no UI screen is open.

1. `MapCursor_IsValid @ 0x1513C` on the stored cursor. It checks x and y only - the layer is
   not checked, so an out-of-range `nLayerScratch` still reaches the grid read.
2. The cursor cell is `apCells[nLayerScratch-1][nCursorY][nCursorX]`. 0x1519C indexes with base
   `0x11AF8`, which is `apCells @ 0x15338` minus one 14400-byte layer. Clicking the cell the
   selected unit already stands on returns immediately (0x151A0).
3. A switch on `Map_bActionLatch` (Map+0x02), modelled as `TactActionLatch` in the IDB:

   - **1 (0x153B0)** `TactState_EnqueueThrow` at the cursor cell. Cost `anActionCost[nActionMode]`
     (Map+0x4E4C), argument `anActionEnabled[nActionMode]` (Map+0x4E7C, the adjacent array), then
     `TactState_KickQueue`.
   - **2 (0x1535C)** `TactState_EnqueueFireBurst` aimed at the cursor cell, same cost/argument
     pair, carrying the multi-target list for mode 7, then the same shared kick at 0x153A0.
