- unk_1864F4..F7 renamed to bGeoscapeScrollUp / bGeoscapeScrollRight / bGeoscapeScrollDown /
  bGeoscapeScrollLeft (426 -> 430 on record), with a comment at 0x1864F4 tying them to the nav Prev /
  Next buttons that write them.
- Function comments at 0x954dc and 0x84484, plus line comments at 0x9552C (the LDRB count and the
  jump-into-the-clock-block), 0x955B0 (the three-part match), 0x95644 (the phase gate), 0x95718 (the
  direction terms and the 120/160 preset), 0x95874 (the flags cleared), 0x95B8C (the four saturating
  counters), 0x84588 (the unconditional pause) and 0x84598 (the fourth read).

65 new checks in tests/test_geoscape.c. A mutation of the port -- the zoom step changed from 5 to 25 --
turns two of them red, which confirms the scroll checks are position-sensitive rather than
self-satisfying. One fixture lesson recorded here because it cost a crash: PtrArray_DeleteAt frees the
item it drops and PtrArray_Remove frees the slot array and installs a freshly malloc'd one, so a test
that hands in a static array crashes, and a test that keeps a second handle on the items double-frees
after a removal. The fixture now hands in malloc'd storage and lets the PtrArray own both.
## Unit 85: Geoscape_DrawGlobeHover @ 0x6727c (2,208 B)

The new-base globe hover frame: the crosshair, the scan animation, the two random readout lines, and the
terrain / cost / Build base labels over the hovered region. It is reached from the geoscape dispatcher's
jumptable default arm (screen ids 13 and 14) at 0x91D8C; that dispatcher is still unported, so it is
named by address only.

### What the frame does

- 0x67290..0x672D8: the wash key is Game_RandU16(10) and any roll below 8 collapses to 0 (MOVLT at
  0x672B4), so only 8 and 9 survive. The whole 240x320 surface is then washed with palette index 0xFF at
  that key. Key 0 leaves every pixel alone, which is how the globe underneath shows through.
- 0x672DC..0x67450: the crosshair -- a 1-wide rule at x=120 from y=0 to 320 - uHeight, a 1-tall rule
  across the full width at (320 - uHeight) / 2, and eight tick marks at (i + 3)^2 = 9, 16, 25, 36, 49,
  64, 81, 100 mirrored on both axes.
- 0x67450..0x67494: the bottom panel opens through Ui_AnimExpandBlit(0, 320 - uHeight, 236, uHeight - 6,
  index 4, source 0x46/0x4B, key 0xC8, mode 3). While the animation is incomplete the function returns 0
  there (ANDS / BEQ loc_67B10) and the scan animation, the readouts, the labels AND the counter advance
  never run.
- 0x67498..0x676A8: the scan animation and its counters. Two 75x30 dark rects at (160, 200) and (5, 200),
  a colour pair whose green is 5 * (51 - key) -- 255 for the ordinary key 0, 210 or 215 when the wash let
  the globe through -- a 10x72 strip at y=242 in two copies driven by nGlobeScanX @ 0x159E00 (left copy
  gated on scanX + 10 < 230, right on 230 - scanX > 10), a vertical pair driven by nGlobeSweepV @ 0x159DFC
  while it is under 37, and a horizontal pair driven by nGlobeSweepH @ 0x159DF8 while it is under 15. All
  three counters then step by one; nGlobeScanX zeroes past 320, and nGlobeSweepV + 1 > 40 zeroes BOTH
  sweep counters -- one CMP at 0x67694, two STRGT.
- 0x676AC..0x67854: two readout lines at (5, 200) and (5, 214), each " " plus three
  itoa(Game_RandU16(900) + 100) joined by '.'. Six rolls per frame, none of them buffered.
- 0x67858..0x67894: the pending pick. gSmapCam.nPickX / nPickY are copied into abFacilityGrid + 0x62C /
  +0x630 (0x159D94 / 0x159D98, now nPendingPickX / nPendingPickY) BEFORE this frame's
  Smap_GetTileAtScreen at 0x67894, so the stored pair is the PREVIOUS frame's pick.
- 0x678B8..0x67B0C: the labels. Ocean (0xFF) gets TEXTS[1042] centred at y=250 and nothing else. A region
  gets TEXTS[1136] + TEXTS[905 + tile] centred at 250, then TEXTS[1137] +
  itoa(aNewBaseCostByRegion[tile - 0x80]) + "$" centred at 270 while bPlacementPending @ 0x1870AC is
  clear, then the confirm control moved to (120 - uWidth/2, 290) and blitted, then TEXTS[1603] centred
  over it at 290. The tile is the return value, which the caller stores with STRB into
  bPendingRegionId @ 0x159DF4.

### The four label sources are TEXTS records, not literals

0xE7B3A, 0xEC680, 0xEC74D and 0x103C77 read like string literals in the decompilation but sit past the
end of .data's initialised span: the section declares a virtual size of 929,136 bytes and only 26,624
bytes of raw data, so everything from 0xAC800 up is zero-filled at load. Each address is an exact
multiple of 205 past aTextRecs @ 0xB38D0 -- 205*1042, 205*1136, 205*1137 and 205*1603 -- so they are
TEXTS records reached by absolute address instead of through the base. Read out of lang.dat they are
"Can`t build here", "Terrain: ", "Base cost: " and "Build base".

That also explains the ocean branch. TEXTS[1042] is the record TEXTS[905 + 0x89] would name, so the ocean
tile and region 0x89 read identically, and aNewBaseCostByRegion[9] == 0 fits 0x89 being the unbuildable
slot. The nine buildable regions are TEXTS[1033..1041].

### The halving triple, twice more

0x6733C..0x6734C and 0x67884..0x67890 are both `RSB #0x140 / CMP #0 / ADDMI #1 / ASR #1`, which is C's
(320 - uHeight) / 2. Hex-Rays renders the second as `v25 = 320 - h; if (h > 0x140) v25 = 321 - h;
v25 >> 1`, which reads like a special case for a tall strip and is not one -- it is the same
truncation-toward-zero the ADDMI triple implements. The port writes the division, and the tests pin the
sample row for two different strip heights.

### Deviation

0x67980 indexes aNewBaseCostByRegion[tile - 0x80] with no range test, so a tile outside 0x80..0x89 reads
past the ten-entry table. The shipped tile grid carries only 0x80..0x89 and 0xFF, and 0xFF takes the
other arm; the port skips the cost line for an out-of-range tile rather than reading out of bounds.

### IDB corrections this unit

- unk_159E00 / dword_159DFC / dword_159DF8 renamed to nGlobeScanX / nGlobeSweepV / nGlobeSweepH, and the
  two previously unnamed dwords at 0x159D94 / 0x159D98 named nPendingPickX / nPendingPickY.
- unk_E7B3A / unk_EC680 / unk_EC74D / unk_103C77 renamed to aTextCantBuildHere / aTextTerrainPrefix /
  aTextBaseCostPrefix / aTextBuildBaseCaption (430 -> 439 on record).
- aNewBaseCostByRegion retyped from a lone dword to u32[10]: 800000, 600000, 1000000, 800000, 750000,
  650000, 900000, 950000, 800000, 0.
- A function comment at 0x6727c and line comments at 0x672B4 (the key collapse), 0x6733C and 0x67884 (the
  two halving triples), 0x67490 (the animation gate), 0x67694 (the paired sweep reset), 0x6786C (the
  pending-pick ordering), 0x67914 (the region-name record), 0x67980 (the unchecked cost index) and
  0x67AC0 (the ocean label).

108 new checks in tests/test_geoscape.c. Two mutations of the port were run to confirm the checks are not
self-satisfying: the tick base changed from 3 to 4 turns five checks red, and the horizontal sweep gate
changed from 15 to 16 turns two red. The label checks use the differential method -- each case runs twice,
once with the TEXTS record intact and once with its first byte zeroed, and only the pixels that differ are
asserted -- because the frame paints a solid panel and two dark rects behind every label. Two helper bugs
surfaced while writing them and are recorded because either would have made a whole group vacuous:
tallying the blanked run's colour instead of the drawn run's makes every label look like it has the same
ink, and a fixture runner that does not restore the animation counters makes the two runs of one
differential differ for reasons that have nothing to do with the record being blanked.
## Unit 86 -- BasePlane_ResetDetailState @ 0x79cb8 (328 B)

The plane screen's stat panel, rebuilt for the currently selected base. Seven globals are cleared, the
row count starts at 1, and the loop walks the whole object list looking for the six craft weapons the
base actually holds.

### The row count starts at 1, not 0

0x79D20..0x79D24 store 1 into the result and into nPlaneStatRowCount @ 0x161A38 before anything is
looked at. That is not an off-by-one: the panel always has its column-header row, and
BasePlaneScreen_DrawStatLabelA @ 0x79e00 sizes its three nested rects from it -- 230 x 20*(n+1), then
228 x 20*n+18 and 226 x 20*n+16. A base holding no craft weapon at all still gets a panel, one row
tall, holding only the three headers.

### The loop reads every slot and keeps six

0x79D48..0x79DE8 runs i from 0 to Map_nObjectCount-1 and evaluates apObjects[i]->auPerBaseVal
[nSelectedBaseIdx] for EVERY slot -- the LDRH at record +0x2A is outside the switch. Only slots 25..30
have a switch arm, so every other slot's read is computed and thrown away, and the default arm does not
bump the row count either (0x79DE4 is reached only from the six arms). The observable effect comes from
those six alone.

The shipped OBJECTS.DAT (main.dat, 30,992 B / 208 = 149 records) makes the boundary concrete: 25 Craft
cannon, 26 Stingray launcher, 27 Avalanche launcher, 28 Laser cannon, 29 Plasma cannon, 30 Fusion ball
launcher -- their names sit exactly 208 bytes apart at 0x2A082E, 0x2A08FE, 0x2A09CE, 0x2A0A9E, 0x2A0B6E
and 0x2A0C3E. Slot 24 is Psi-arm (a soldier weapon) and 31..35 are Tank - cannon, Tank - rocket
launcher, Tank - laser cannon, Hovertank - plasma and Hovertank - blaster launcher. So 25..30 is not an
arbitrary window: it is the craft-weapon run, with a soldier weapon on one side and the vehicle weapons
on the other. A new IDB enum PufoCraftWeaponSlot records all eleven.

### The six counts are dwords, and each one gates its row's control

Every store is a STR and every read an LDR, in this function and outside it. Geoscape_OnPointer
(0x88674..0x88730) and Geoscape_OnPointerUp (0x8a38c..0x8a460) each hit-test a row's control only when
that row's count is non-zero -- six `if (nPlaneStat* != 0) UiControl_HitTest(...)` in a row -- so the
weapons a base does not hold have no clickable row at all. The value stored is the u16 read at +0x2A
widened to a dword.

They are not contiguous in memory: they sit in the gaps between the plane screen's panel pointers at
0x161ED0..0x161EFC, which is why the IDB carries them as six separate unk_ globals.

### One global, two unrelated uses

nPlaneStatRowCount @ 0x161A38 is also the start-menu row-key flicker's scratch. 0xA0AEC stores nMapPhase
straight into it, 0xA0B14 adds Game_RandU16(8 - nMapPhase), and 0xA0B20 writes (it * 32 - 1) into
MainMenu_anRowKeys[i]. The port had named it g_nKeyAccum after that second use, which made the plane
screen's row count look like an unrelated global; it is now g_nPlaneStatRowCount, named after the global
rather than after one of its uses. This is a design problem in the original -- one dword serving two
subsystems -- recorded here rather than papered over.

### Deviation

0x79D5C dereferences apObjects[i] and indexes auPerBaseVal with 2 * (char)nSelectedBaseIdx with no test
at all. nSelectedBaseIdx is loaded with LDRSB, so it is a signed byte, and an out-of-range value reads
inside the record: auPerBaseVal[-1] is the u16 at +0x28 (bTwoHanded / bUnk41) and auPerBaseVal[8] is
aItemQty[0] at +0x3A. No shipped path sets a base index outside 0..7, and the port refuses the read and
reaches the same observable result -- six zeroes and one row.

### IDB corrections this unit

- unk_161ED8 / unk_161EE8 / unk_161EF8 / unk_161EF0 / unk_161ABC / unk_161ED4 renamed to
  nPlaneStatCraftCannon / nPlaneStatStingray / nPlaneStatAvalanche / nPlaneStatLaserCannon /
  nPlaneStatPlasmaCannon / nPlaneStatFusionBall, all typed int (439 -> 446 renames on record).
- New enum PufoCraftWeaponSlot: PW_CRAFT_CANNON 25 .. PW_FUSION_BALL_LAUNCHER 30, plus the five vehicle
  slots 31..35 that must NOT be craft rows.
- A function comment at 0x79cb8 and line comments at 0x79D20 (the row count starts at 1), 0x79D44 (the
  LDRSB base index), 0x79D5C (the unchecked read), 0x79DE4 (the count bump is inside the six arms) and
  0x161A38 / 0xA0AEC (the two-use global).

49 new checks in tests/test_baseui.c, on the shipped 149-record object layout with the real slot names.
Two mutations confirm they are not self-satisfying: moving the first weapon slot from 25 to 24 turns 13
checks red, and dropping the non-zero filter turns 4 red. The out-of-range guard is tested by putting a
distinguishable value exactly where the unchecked read would land -- 0x1234 in bTwoHanded/bUnk41 for
auPerBaseVal[-1] and 0x5678 in aItemQty[0] for auPerBaseVal[8] -- and the last case re-runs the same
object with a valid index to prove those zeroes came from the guard and not from an empty fixture.
## Unit 87 -- BaseFac_BuildStatusMsg @ 0x6a4bc (1,520 B)

The geoscape's two-line base-facility status string, thirteen arms keyed on a character code.

### Where the arguments come from

The only call site is 0x8C82C, inside the geoscape dispatcher (still unported, so it is named by
address only), and it builds every argument out of line 0 of the root message list @ 0x158890: the case
byte is UiLineList_GetFlag(line 0) sign-extended from a byte (0x8C818), the base index is that line's
colour dword slot 2 (0x8C7C4), the row index is slot 0 (0x8C7EC), the column index is slot 1 (0x8C7D8),
and the first argument is abFacilityGrid, loaded into R7 at 0x8C790. The dispatcher then switches on the
SAME flag byte again at 0x8C83C and draws the two lines this function leaves behind. The return value is
dropped.

### The pause is ahead of the switch

0x6A4D4 calls GameTime_Pause before any case dispatch, so it runs on all thirteen arms AND on the
default. The tests assert that separately from the text, because it is the one thing every arm does.

### Thirteen arms on a character code

`SUB R0, R3, #0x20 / CMP R0, #0xC / ADDLS PC, PC, R0, LSL #2` at 0x6A4E0, with R3 sign-extended from the
char: cases 0x20..0x2C, i.e. ' ' ! " # $ % & ' ( ) * + ,. Anything else leaves both buffers untouched.
Two pairs are the same arm written twice: '!' (0x6A5A0) and '"' (0x6A610) are the same eleven
operations, and '$' (0x6A700), ')' (0x6A998) and '*' (0x6A9C8) all jump to the same LABEL_60 tail.

### The six label prefixes are TEXTS records -- and the record-0 offset matters

0xF650E / 0xF690F / 0xF69DC / 0xF6AA9 / 0xF6B76 / 0xF6C43 sit past .data's initialised span (929,136
virtual bytes, 26,624 raw) and each is an exact multiple of 205 past aTextRecs: records 1334, 1339,
1340, 1341, 1342 and 1343. Out of lang.dat they read "Base: ", the same word with a space before the
colon, "Production: ", "Research: ", "Module: " and "Craft: ".

Getting those numbers right needed the blob's record-0 offset, and the two candidates differ by exactly
one record -- 0x102 and 0x1CA in lang.dat -- which is the worst kind of mistake here because the wrong
offset still produces a plausible string at every index. It was settled against the shipped facility
names: with record 0 at 0x102, records 106..118 read Access Lift, Living Quarters, Laboratory, Workshop,
Short Range Radar, Long Range Radar, General stores, Alien Containment, Psi Laboratory, Hyper Wave
Decoder, Mind Shield, Hangar, Gravity shield, and 463 / 120 / 121 / 122 read Missile Defences, Laser
Defence, Plasma Defence and Fusion Ball Defence -- exactly the g_anFacNameRec order Geoscape_InitUI
@ 0x86A58 copies into aBaseFacFlags. With record 0 at 0x1CA the same indices are shifted by one and the
sequence starts at Living Quarters. The offset is now written down as a comment at aTextRecs.

### The '&' arm reads the facility grid

The facility kind is `abFacilityGrid[480 + 6 * (24 * nBaseIdx + nFacRow) + nFacCol]`, and the name comes
from aBaseFacFlags[kind]. The grid is eight 144-byte 24x6 blocks starting at abFacilityGrid + 372, so
+480 is row 18 and nFacRow 0..5 selects the grid's last six rows -- a different window from the hangar
arm's rows 12..17, which reaches the same grid through +372 with `6 * (24 * base + row + 12) + col`. The
tests pin the arithmetic by planting four different kinds at the cell under test and its three
neighbours, so an error in the 144 / 6 / 1 split names the wrong facility.

### The '%' arm reads the topic byte one record in

0x6A7B4 is `LDRB [R7,#0x22]` on aTopics[nBaseIdx] -- offset 34 on a 34-byte record, so it reads
aTopics[nBaseIdx + 1].abUnk0[0]. That is the same off-by-one-record pairing
ResearchScreen_RebuildTopicList reads the topic ranges through, and the test distinguishes it by giving
record nBaseIdx its own decoy byte: reading in place would name a different topic, and the two candidate
topic names are asserted to differ so the check cannot pass by accident.

### szScratch186488 is a channel between calls

''' and '(' write an object name into szScratch186488 and ',' appends whatever it finds there. The
status line therefore has state that survives from one call to the next, and the test sets the scratch
explicitly before checking ','.

0x10DA38, the source the ''' arm copies from when the object index is the 255 sentinel, is inside
.data's zero-filled span, so it copies a single NUL: a clear, not a message. It is the same all-zero
source the three screen openers use at 0x10DA38 / 0x10DA39.

### Deviation

Every copy here is an unbounded strcpy/strcat loop into fixed scratch buffers, and none of the index
arithmetic is tested: apObjects[] is dereferenced raw, the grid byte and the topic index are computed
with no bound, and aBaseFacFlags is indexed by a byte that can exceed its 17 records. The port bounds
each copy by the buffer sizes the env carries and skips a dereference whose index is out of range,
reaching the same observable text for the values the shipped game produces.

### IDB corrections this unit

- unk_F650E / unk_F690F / unk_F69DC / unk_F6AA9 / unk_F6B76 / unk_F6C43 renamed to aTextRec1334 /
  aTextRec1339 / aTextRec1340 / aTextRec1341 / aTextRec1342 / aTextRec1343 (446 -> 452 on record).
- BaseFac_BuildStatusMsg's arguments named abFacilityGrid / nCase / nBaseIdx / nRowOrIdx / nColOrIdx --
  the last two are genuinely overloaded: nRowOrIdx is the grid row in '&', the craft index in '\'' and
  '+', and the object index in '('.
- A function comment at 0x6a4bc and line comments at 0x6A4D4 (the pause ahead of the switch), 0x6A78C
  (the 1000 gate), 0x6A7B4 (the one-record-in topic byte), 0x6A858 (the grid cell), 0x6A8D0 (the
  all-zero clear source) and 0x8C82C (what the call site feeds each argument).
- A comment at aTextRecs @ 0xB38D0 recording the lang.dat record-0 offset and the facility-name proof
  that pins it.

54 new checks in tests/test_baseui.c, against the real lang.dat TEXTS table. Three mutations confirm
they are not self-satisfying: shifting every prefix index by one record -- the exact mistake made while
writing this unit -- turns 31 checks red, moving the '&' cell read to the hangar offset turns 4 red, and
reading the '%' topic byte in place instead of one record in turns 1 red.
## Unit 88 -- Ufopaedia_RefreshEntry @ 0x9a014 (1,528 B) + Ufopaedia_PrevEntry @ 0x9a60c (328 B) + Ufopaedia_NextEntry @ 0x9a754 (364 B)

The encyclopedia's paging and entry layout, 2,220 B. The screen's builder, Ufopaedia_Open @ 0x9a8cc
(3,368 B), is the next unit; these three are what runs after it has built the panels.

### The two tables that drive it

aUfopaediaCatTopics @ 0xAA830, 9 rows of 22 research topic numbers -- one row per category panel. Row
5 is the only row that fills all 22 slots; every other row ends at a zero byte. IDA's old name,
aFghijklmnop, came from row 0's bytes happening to be ASCII 'f'..'p' (102..112), which is also why the
table reads as a string in the listing.

anUfopaediaEntryNum @ 0xAA5F0, 144 dwords, research topic -> ufopaedia entry number. Topics 47, 94, 95,
96 and 143 have no entry. The alien-race topics 118..142 all map onto the five race entries 54..58, so
each race appears once per race topic. Entry numbers are not sequential per category: topics 55..76 map
to 54..75, 77..93 to 76..92, 102..112 back to 93..103, and the rest to 1001..1051, 2026..2036, 2097..2101
and 3000..3016. RefreshEntry branches on those ranges.

### The category panels reuse UiPanel's own storage for their entry list

Both paging functions read the topic as `panel + 4 * (n + 1261)`. 4 * 1261 = 5044, which is exactly
anLineAux's offset in the 7092-byte UiPanel, so apLines[n] holds the entry name and anLineAux[n] holds
its topic number; nLineCount is the entry count and nUnk3032 the row the pointer last selected. No new
structure is needed -- the port's existing UiPanel already has all four fields at the right offsets.

g_apUfopaediaCatPanels @ 0x1871D0 is a ten-dword block: slots 0..8 are the nine panels, slot 9 (0x1871F4)
is the current entry index, slot 10 (0x1871F8) is the current category byte. The paging code writes the
entry index as `dword_1871D0[9]`, which is what hides the fact that it is a separate variable.

### PrevEntry and NextEntry are not symmetric

NextEntry tests `++idx == 22 || aUfopaediaCatTopics[22 * category + idx] == 0` at 0x9A7A8 -- it stops at
the table's own terminator, and the 22 test exists only because row 5 has no terminator. PrevEntry has no
table test at all: 0x9A640 walks the index down to -1, wraps the category there and restarts at slot 21.
Only the panel's line-count filter at 0x9A684..0x9A694 rejects the slots past a short row. The two
functions share the accept test and the tail, so the port factors those and keeps the loops separate.

The unlock gate at 0x9A6BC..0x9A6E8 is two byte reads:

  MOV R0,#0x22 ; MUL R0,R11,R0 ; ADD R0,R0,R4 ; LDRB R0,[R0,#0xD]   -> aResearchTopics[topic].bUnlocked
  MOV R0,#0x1C00 ; ORR R0,#0x24 ; ADD R1,R1,R4 ; LDRB R1,[R1,R0]    -> aResearchTopics + topic + 0x1C24

0x15EF08 + 0x1C24 = 0x160B2C, so the second is abResearchZero[topic] -- the mirror
ResearchScreen_RebuildTopicList sets at 0x74334 when a topic's bUnlocked becomes 1. Hex-Rays renders it
as `aResearchTopics[211].abActivateTopics[topic + 1]`, because 211 * 34 + 0x1E = 0x1C24: the same address
but one byte late, and it would read the NEXT topic's mirror byte. The ARM is the authority and the port
follows it.

### The wrap loop is UiPanel_WrapText, inlined

0x9A308..0x9A4D0 is a byte-for-byte clone of UiPanel_WrapText @ 0x37144: same cursors, same
`psz[++v7 - v9] = 0` break, same `i = v7` resume, same trailing flush, same `nLineCount = nLineStart +
count` tail, same space appended to the working copy. Only the working buffer differs (200 bytes here,
104 there). The port calls the shared function instead of duplicating the loop, and passes the
description without the trailing space because UiPanel_WrapText adds it.

### The layout bands

The cascade at 0x9A14C..0x9A1F0 has a goto in it, but every path lands in exactly one of four bands:

  entry <= 1000            220 px, style 7, panel at y 230, no wide flag
  1000 < entry < 2000      220 px, style 7, y 230, wide flag set
  2000 < entry < 3000      180 px, style 13, y 50, wide flag set
  entry > 2999             200 px, style 8, y 110, wide flag set

Entry 1000 and entry 2000 both keep the default layout, and entry 3000 is the 200 px band, not the 180 px
one -- the cascade's `<= 1000` arm is inclusive and its `< 3000` arm is exclusive. Four further tests at
0x9A200..0x9A244 only set the wide flag: 93..97 (which also indents the text by seven lines so the panel's
first rows stay clear of the entry's picture), 54..75, 76..84 and 85..92. Entries 54..58 are the five alien
races; what the rest of 54..92 depicts is not recorded anywhere in the IDB, so those bands carry no subject
name.

### The description and the pad

The text is TEXTS[4*topic + 534], then records 535, 536 and 537 appended -- 109470 / 109675 / 109880 /
110085 are 205 * 534..537. Four records of up to 204 bytes each into an 800-byte stack buffer.

The pad is a toggle, not a rebuild. Paging sets bUfopaediaEntryDirty to 0 (0x9A700 / 0x9A868), so the
refresh it triggers takes the create arm; a refresh that did not come from paging finds the flag set and
frees instead. Only entries below 1000 get art: "<n>.pal" into palette slot 17, then PadImage_Load with the
bare number at mode 17.

### Deviations

- The four description records are copied with strcpy/strcat into an 800-byte buffer and can need 816. The
  port bounds each append by the buffer size.
- The original never nulls g_pUfopaediaPad after operator delete, and 0x1872E4 is read again by the next
  refresh. The port nulls it, the same policy as CloseFreePad elsewhere in the file.
- The original calls PadImage_Load on the pad even when operator new returned null. The port guards.
- Neither paging function bounds the category index or the entry index before using them, and the wrap has
  no bound against the panel's 50 line buffers. The port bounds the indices; the wrap stays as the original
  wrote it.

### IDB

- aFghijklmnop -> aUfopaediaCatTopics, typed `unsigned char [9][22]` (the listing had it as a 12-byte
  string, which is why the row-5 terminator test looked odd).
- dword_AA5F0 -> anUfopaediaEntryNum, typed `int [144]`.
- dword_1871D0 -> g_apUfopaediaCatPanels, typed `UiPanel *[9]` at 36 bytes; a new int symbol
  g_nUfopaediaEntryIdx created at 0x1871F4, which had no name of its own.
- unk_1871F8 -> g_nUfopaediaCategory, unk_187200 -> g_pUfopaediaTextPanel, unk_187204 ->
  g_pUfopaediaSelPanel, unk_187300 -> g_nUfopaediaTopic, dword_1872D8 -> g_nUfopaediaEntryNum,
  unk_1872E4 -> g_pUfopaediaPad, unk_187304 -> g_bUfopaediaPadDirty.
- Function comments at 0x9a014, 0x9a60c, 0x9a754; line comments at 0xAA830, 0xAA5F0, 0x1871F4, 0x9A640
  (PrevEntry has no table test), 0x9A7A8 (the terminator test), 0x9A308 (the inlined UiPanel_WrapText)
  and 0x9A6D4 (the 0x1C24 mirror read, with the one-byte-late Hex-Rays rendering spelled out).

107 new checks in tests/test_baseui.c. Seven mutations confirm they are not self-satisfying: dropping
NextEntry's table terminator test turns 3 red, giving PrevEntry the table test NextEntry has turns 9 red,
reading the mirror byte one late -- exactly what Hex-Rays claims -- turns 2 red, making the > 2999 boundary
exclusive turns 3 red, shifting the description window one record early turns 6 red, removing the 93..97
indent turns 2 red, and wrapping the category in the wrong direction turns 3 red.
## Unit 89 -- Ufopaedia_Open @ 0x9a8cc (3,368 B)

The ufopaedia's builder and its teardown, in one function on one flag.

### One function, two jobs, on a toggle

0x9A8E0 tests g_bUfopaediaScreenBuilt (was unk_187308). Clear, the build arm sets it at 0x9A8E8 and
returns from inside its last loop at 0x9B4FC -- so the release code that follows the whole build block
only runs on the NEXT call, which clears the flag first at 0x9B50C. Calling it twice is open-then-close.
The build arm never clears the flag, which is what makes the pairing work.

### What gets built

A 9-line selector panel (nStyle 15, font 24, at 120/50, 230 wide, centred rows, the -106 byte at
bUnk7088, row-blit key 0xB4, colour 0xF0/0xF0/0xF0, source rect 50/50/250), a 50-line text panel (nStyle
7, font 12, at 5/230, colour 0xBE/0x78/0xF0, and the only panel that clears bFlag7072), then nine category
panels: font 16, x 120, 230 wide, nStyle clamped to 13 at 0x9AE44, and posY = 160 - 8 * visible rows
(0x9AE58..0x9AE6C, where the `if (n & 0x8000000) ++v12` is the ARM's arithmetic-shift rounding and never
fires for a non-negative count).

**The clamp lands on nStyle only.** The panel is constructed with the FULL shown count, so category 5 keeps
all 22 line buffers and pages through 22 entries while showing 13. That is also what the paging filter at
0x9A684 compares against -- panel->nLineCount is the full count, not the visible one.

### Which entries show

The test is evaluated twice: a counting pass at 0x9AB04 that sizes each panel, then a filling pass at
0x9B0C4 that writes the names. Both use

  (aResearchTopics[topic].bUnlocked != 0 && topic != 0) || raceOverride != 0

The override is non-zero only in category 5 (0x9AB3C: `if (v4 != 5) goto LABEL_45`) and only for the five
race topics 55..59, and it means "this race has been met".

### The race lists are hand-written and two of them are incomplete

The 25 encounter topics 118..142 form five families by residue mod 5, but the original's AND-chains do not
cover them:

  Sectoid  (55): 118, 123, 128, 133, then 138            complete
  Snakeman (56): 121, 126, 131, 136, then 141            complete
  Floater  (59): 124, 129, 134, 139, 59, then 119        complete
  Ethereal (57): 122, 127, 132, 137, then 57             142 never appears
  Muton    (58): 120, 125, 58, then 130                 135 and 140 never appear

So researching topic 142, 135 or 140 shows nothing in the ufopaedia, while researching 138, 141, 119 or 130
brings its race up. Ethereal's fallback is its own topic 57 rather than a family slot.

**Opening the screen writes the research mirror.** When a race passes its gate, 0x9AD68 (and 0x9B344 in the
filling pass) stores 1 into abResearchZero[topic]. That is why the paging gate at 0x9A6D4 accepts on
abResearchZero[topic] at all: the ufopaedia itself put the byte there. A race met in the field becomes
pageable without its own research topic ever being unlocked.

### Names

The row name is TEXTS[aResearchTopics[topic].wGate4] (0x9B38C, the same `MUL #0xCD` against 0xB38D0 the
research screen uses), and for the five race rows it is then overwritten with a literal -- aSectoid @
0xAC610, aSnakeman @ 0xAC618, aEthereal @ 0xAC624, aMuton @ 0xAC630, aFloater @ 0xAC638 (0x9B3D8..0x9B4E0).
Rows are packed from row 0: the row index counts only accepted slots.

The selector's nine rows are cleared, not labelled. The nine sources at 0x105EE6..0x10654E are 205 bytes
apart and all sit above 0xAC800, inside .data's zero-filled span, so each copy writes a single NUL -- the
same all-zero source the rest of the binary uses for a clear.

### The teardown, and the pad it misses

0x9B50C..0x9B5DC releases the selector panel, the text panel, the screen pad at 0x1872E0, the nine category
panels in slot order, and six controls. The control loop starts at 0x1872E0 and reads slot +2 on each of its
six steps, so the six released are 0x1872E8, 0x1872EC, 0x1872F0, 0x1872F4, 0x1872F8 and 0x1872FC -- and
0x1872E4, the live entry's PadImage that every Ufopaedia_RefreshEntry allocates at 0x9A530, appears in no
release path at all. **Original bug, recorded in the ledger and not reproduced:** closing the ufopaedia after
any entry has been shown leaks that pad.

0x9B544 also writes nLineCount = 50 into the text panel *before* the null test at 0x9B550, so a null text
panel would fault there.

### Deviations

- The pad leak above: the port releases 0x1872E4.
- The original dereferences the freshly allocated panels without testing them (0x9A928, 0x9AA6C); the port
  guards.
- The name copy is an unbounded strcpy into a 50-byte line buffer, and the row index is not bounded against
  the panel. The port bounds both.
- The nLineCount write ahead of the null test is moved inside the guard.

### IDB

- byte_160B2C -> abResearchZero (the port has called it that for several units; the IDB still had the
  address name), unk_187308 -> g_bUfopaediaScreenBuilt, unk_1872E0 -> g_pUfopaediaScreenPad (463 -> 466 on
  record).
- A function comment at 0x9a8cc; line comments at 0x9AB50 (the five race lists, with the two incomplete
  families spelled out), 0x9AD68 (the mirror write), 0x9AE44 (the clamp lands on nStyle only), 0x9AF2C (the
  selector clear), 0x9B3D8 (the race-name overwrite), 0x9B544 (the write before the null test), 0x9B5B8 (the
  leak), 0xAC610 (the five literal names) and 0x160B2C (what the mirror is and who writes it).
- One new ledger row (227), 90 ORIGINAL BUG markers.

125 new checks in tests/test_baseui.c. Nine mutations confirm they are not self-satisfying: completing
Ethereal's family with 142 turns 1 red, completing Muton's with 135 and 140 turns 2 red, removing the
abResearchZero write turns 1 red, raising the nStyle clamp to 22 turns 2 red, using 16 instead of 8 per
visible row turns 10 red, skipping the race-name overwrite turns 9 red, not freeing the entry pad on
teardown turns 1 red, building the category panel with the clamped count turns 4 red, and labelling the
selector rows instead of clearing them turns 1 red.
## Unit 90 -- PsiScreen_BuildPanels @ 0x716d4 (2,940 B) + PsiScreen_SelectListed @ 0x71298 (848 B) + PsiScreen_Init @ 0x72b40 (332 B) + PsiScreen_ApplyAssignments @ 0x72250 (328 B)

The psi screen (geoscape screen 17): four parallel per-base columns, the psi-lab assignment toggle, and
the apply pass that writes the toggle back into the soldier records.

### Four parallel per-base columns

Each column is its own UiPanel and each is an array of eight entries indexed by base:

    unk_15EED0      -> g_apPsiNamePanel    the soldier name,        nPosX 10,  nUnk7052   5, nViewW 230
    byte_15EE84+4   -> g_apPsiStatPanel    "auStat[6]\auStat[7]",  nPosX 154, nUnk7052 175, nViewW 10
    byte_15EE84+36  -> g_apPsiDeltaPanel   the training delta,      nPosX 184, nUnk7052 209, nViewW 10
    unk_15EE58      -> g_apPsiCheckPanel   the assignment box,      nPosX 215, nUnk7052 210, nViewW 10

The middle two are not separate globals in the image: they are the dword runs at byte_15EE84+4 and +36,
and the same 72-byte block holds the row-selected flag at +0 (set by Init at 0x72C70, cleared by the
screen-17 branch of Geoscape_OnPointerUp at 0x890C4) and a scratch row index at +68 that SelectListed
uses to hand one row to its four SetLineMeta calls. The port keeps four named arrays plus the two
scalars.

All four share nStyle 14, nFont 16, nPosY and nUnk7056 of 70, SetBytes0to2(B4,B4,B4) and
SetBytes6to11(F0,F0,F0,14,14,14). Only the name column gets SetBytes3to5(32,32,FA) at 0x718D4,
bFlag7073 = 1 at 0x718C0 and bUnk7088 = 0x96 at 0x718F4; only the three narrow columns get nUnk7076 = 1
(0x719CC, 0x71AA0, 0x71B68). The name column is the only one with a click handler (0x7183C).

### What the rows carry

anLineAux is the row payload and each column uses it for something different. The name column stores
the SOLDIER INDEX into Map.apSoldiers (0x71C6C), not a base-relative slot. The checkbox column stores 1
when the soldier is assigned to this base's psi lab. The delta column stores the training total. The
stat column stores nothing. PsiScreen_ApplyAssignments is what turns the checkbox column back into game
state, and the delta column is what it feeds into Soldier.nPsiTrainDays.

### BuildPanels is a build/release toggle, like Ufopaedia_Open

byte_15EEF0 (now g_bPsiPanelOpen) clear means build: it is set at 0x716F0 and never cleared by the build
arm. Set means release: nGeoscapeScreen goes to 0 at 0x7212C, the flag clears at 0x72134, and the screen
pad, the four panels of every base and the two scroll controls at 0x15EE7C / 0x15EE80 are freed. The
same flag is what Base_HitTestFacilityStrip @ 0x671b0 and the geoscape pointer handlers test to disable
the base-tab strip while the screen is open.

Building runs three passes. 0x71734 counts each base's soldiers (Soldier.nKind == base). 0x7178C builds
four panels per base, each constructed with that base's own count. 0x71BA8 fills the rows and rezeroes
the same count array as the row cursor (0x71BDC), so rows are packed from 0 in Map.apSoldiers order and
a base's panel holds exactly its own roster.

### The row colours

UiPanel_SetLineMeta's first triple marks the row: (240, 120, 240) assigned, (240, 240, 240) free; the
second triple is (10, 10, 10) either way. The original passes the third byte of the first triple as -16,
which is 240 once it is stored as a byte. BuildPanels applies the assigned colour only, and only on rows
whose soldier is assigned (0x71D1C..0x71D9C) -- an unassigned row gets no meta at all. SelectListed
applies whichever colour the row is moving to, on all four columns (0x7137C..0x713FC or
0x714D4..0x71554).

### Original behaviour found

- Assigning a soldier at the psi screen is what makes them psi-capable. 0x71D00 stores 1 into
  Soldier.bPsiActive (+0x1A6) for every row whose bPsiAssigned is set, before the stat columns and the
  training countdown read that byte. A soldier assigned who had no psi powers has them from the first
  build.
- The two stat columns are gated on bPsiActive alone, not on the assignment (0x71E2C): a psi-capable
  soldier shows "auStat[6]\auStat[7]" and the delta even with their box clear. Only a soldier with no
  psi powers gets the cleared pair at 0x71FDC / 0x72008.
- The training countdown, 0x72034..0x720B0. Assigned and psi-capable with auStat[6] < auStat[7] arms
  30 * auStat[7] / 100 days. Already at or above auStat[7] still arms exactly ONE day (0x7209C), so
  auStat[6] keeps climbing past auStat[7]. Either flag clear arms nothing. Geoscape_TickBases spends one
  day per tick raising auStat[6] by 1, which is exactly the gain the "+N" column advertises.
- The checkbox rows are cleared, not labelled. Both label sources, unk_EEE8A and unk_EEF57, sit above
  0xAC800 inside .data's zero-filled span, so each copy writes a single NUL; the state lives in
  anLineAux.
- The assigned counter compares anLineAux against 1 exactly (0x71314), so a row holding any other value
  is not counted against the capacity gate.
- ApplyAssignments closes the screen. Its tail call at 0x72394 reaches BuildPanels while
  g_bPsiPanelOpen is still set, so it takes the release arm: pressing Apply commits and dismisses.
- Hex-Rays renders PsiScreen_Init as returning an uninitialised value. 0x72C74 / 0x72C78 is
  `POP {R4-R7,LR}` followed by `B PsiScreen_BuildPanels` -- a real tail call with no return value.

### 1 original bug found, reproduced and pinned

0x72370. Base_UpdatePsiLabNeeded takes its budget as its third argument, and its two other call sites
load Base_CountPsiSoldiers into R2 first (Geoscape_CloseUI 0x8BA4C, Game_StartNew 0x953CC). This call
site never writes R2: the last write is the inner loop's `ADD R2, R2, #1` at 0x7235C, so the budget is
the loop's exit value -- the base's whole soldier row count, or 0 when the panel is empty. A base with
twelve soldiers and one assigned gets a psi-lab budget of 12/10+1 = 2 instead of 1/10+1 = 1, and marks a
second lab cell as needed. Reproduced; ledger row added.

### Deviations, recorded

- The original stores UiPanel_ctor's result into the global and writes through it without testing
  (0x717F8 and the three that follow); the port guards all four.
- Both roster passes dereference Map.apSoldiers[i] with no null test, and 0x722DC indexes it with the
  row's aux value unguarded; the port skips nulls and bounds the index.
- The stat and delta strings are built with j_itoa plus unbounded strcat into a 104-byte stack buffer
  and copied into 50-byte rows with strcpy; the port bounds both.
- 0x712EC indexes anLineAux with the panel's nUnk3032 cursor unguarded; the port bounds it.
- UiPanel_ctor clamps to 500 lines where the original does not, so the port bounds the row cursor.
- SelectListed returns either a pointer to a stack copy of the (empty) label or &dword_1870B4, neither
  of which any caller reads; the port returns a bool.

### IDB

- unk_15EED0 -> g_apPsiNamePanel, unk_15EE58 -> g_apPsiCheckPanel, unk_15EE78 -> g_pPsiScreenPad,
  byte_15EE84 -> g_bPsiRowSel, byte_15EEF0 -> g_bPsiPanelOpen, unk_ABB08 -> aPsiDeltaFull ("+1"),
  unk_186BA4 -> pGeoscapeCtlConfirm, unk_186BAC -> pGeoscapeCtlApply, and new symbols
  g_pPsiScrollPrevCtl (0x15EE7C), g_pPsiScrollNextCtl (0x15EE80), g_apPsiStatPanel (0x15EE88),
  g_apPsiDeltaPanel (0x15EEA8), g_nPsiScratchRow (0x15EEC8). 466 -> 476 renames on record.
- The Soldier struct's three psi members renamed to match the port: bUnk149 -> bPsiAssigned (+0x95),
  bUnk422 -> bPsiActive (+0x1A6), bUnk423 -> nPsiTrainDays (+0x1A7). The port's own copies follow.
- Function comments at 0x716d4, 0x71298, 0x72250 and 0x72b40; line comments at 0x71C6C (the aux is the
  apSoldiers index), 0x71D00 (assigning sets bPsiActive), 0x71F7C and 0x72090 (the 30% training total),
  0x71F98 (the "+1" literal), 0x7209C (one day even at full energy), 0x72370 (the R2 residue), 0x71314
  (the exact 1), 0x71334 (the capacity gate), 0x72C70 (the row-selected flag), 0xABAC8 (the two scroll
  descriptors) and 0x15EE84 (the block layout).
- One new ledger row (228), 90 ORIGINAL BUG markers unchanged: this unit reproduces its finding rather
  than deviating from it.

121 new checks in tests/test_baseui.c. Fourteen mutations confirm they are not self-satisfying: letting
the counting pass ignore nKind turns 8 red, storing the row instead of the soldier index in the name
aux turns 6 red, reading bPsiActive where the original reads bPsiAssigned turns 11 red, the reverse swap
turns 3 red, 10% instead of 30% turns 4 red, dropping the one training day at full energy turns 1 red,
not setting bPsiActive turns 5 red, using the free colour for an assigned row turns 4 red, dropping the
+1 from the capacity gate turns 5 red, counting any non-zero aux instead of 1 turns 2 red, a constant
budget of 1 turns 1 red, swapping the apply branches turns 6 red, applying the two scroll descriptors in
reverse turns 4 red, and skipping the scroll-control release turns 1 red. Two mutations were tried that
the tests cannot see and are not counted: an equivalent rewrite of the capacity comparison
(`cap < n+1` to `cap <= n`), and dropping the free() while still nulling the pad pointer.

## Unit 91 -- PsiScreen_Draw @ 0x72398 (1,960 B)

The psi screen's frame. The whole body sits behind g_bPsiPanelOpen @ 0x15EEF0 (0x723B8), the same byte the
build/release toggle uses, so a closed screen draws nothing at all: not the rails, not the controls, not
the tail.

The rails are the shared BaseUi_DrawFrameRails (0x723C8..0x72558): 24 side blocks 7 tall climbing
100..215 and falling 230..115, 24 top and bottom blocks 5 wide climbing to 215 and falling 250..135.
TransferScreen_Draw, ManufScreen_DrawFrame and ResearchScreen_Draw each carry the identical block, so the
port calls one helper for all four.

Four captions, and an earlier note on this function was wrong about them. It called them scratch buffers
nothing writes; the shipped lang.dat has text in every one, and all four are TEXTS records at
aTextRecs @ 0xB38D0:
  TEXTS[1188] "Èìÿ: Ïñè íàâûê/ñèëà: Äîá.íàâûê: Îáó÷" at (7, 54) -- the column captions (0x726A0)
  TEXTS[1189] "Âûáåðåòå áàçó" centred at (60, 300) (0x726F8)
  TEXTS[1127] "ÎÊ" centred at (180, 300) (0x7274C) -- the same record the manuf, research and buy-sell
  frames use, which is why IDA already had aTextOk at 0xEBF4B
  TEXTS[1190] "Íåò ìåñòà â Ïñè-ëàáîðàòîðèÿõ" centred at (120, 158) -- the shortfall caption (0x72B2C)
unk_EF024, unk_EF0F1 and unk_EF1BE are now aTextPsiColumnCaptions, aTextSelectBase and aTextNoPsiRoom,
each char[205].

Centring is x = centre - (width >> 1). 0x7290C is ADDMI R1,R1,#1 with the flags from MOVS on a positive
width, so the add never fires and the ASR #1 at 0x72910 is a plain floor; 0x72B1C is the same shape. The
title is centred on 120 (0x725F0), the overlay row names on 110 (0x72918, RSB from 0x6E).

Three colour pairs are packed: (44,F4,FC)/(4,46,4B) at 0x7258C and again at 0x7265C, and the tail's
(DC,50,50)/(1E,32,50) at 0x72A94. Only the second half matters for text -- Gfx_PackRgb565Pair writes it to
unk_147B3C, palette slot 2 entry 27, and the font glyphs take their main colour from entry 27. The tail
pair is packed whenever the panel branch is reached, before dwActionFail is even read, which is what makes
that branch observable.

Overlay (byte_1870F8). With it clear the draw jumps from 0x72760 straight to the tail at 0x72A70. With it
set: the full-screen blend (0x72790), a 32-wide erase strip at x 208 of height 28*nBaseCount + 4
(0x727CC), Base_DrawFacilityIconStrip with the mark argument -1 (0x727D8) so the drawer paints no chevron
of its own, the 210-wide panel (0x72810), then one bevelled row per base -- 205x26 at 0x46/A0/B3, 204x24
at 00/6E/77, 201x22 at 04/46/4B -- with the base name centred at (110, 28*i + 7). The row count is the
signed byte at abFacilityGrid + 0x618 (nBaseCount @ 0x159D80), read by LDRSB at 0x7281C and compared
against 0, so a negative value draws no rows.

A base whose Base_CalcPsiLabCap is 0 gets a 23-step white bracket: 23 2x2 blocks down-right from
(212, 28*base + 4) and 23 up-right from (212, 28*base + 26), meeting at x 234 (0x72968 / 0x72994). It is
the same bracket Base_DrawFacilityIconStrip paints for a marked base -- here it marks the ABSENCE of a psi
lab, which is exactly what the screen is telling the player about.

Tail. byte_158834 against byte_1870F4, both read signed (0x72A08). Equal, or the overlay closed: pack the
tail pair and, when dwActionFail == 1 and dword_1870B4[0] == 0, run Ui_AnimExpandBlit_IfEnabled(grid, 20,
130, 200, 70, 1) and the TEXTS[1190] caption. Different: Base_CalcPsiLabCap(byte_158834) decides -- non-zero
adopts that base into byte_1870F4 and clears byte_1870F8 (0x72A28 / 0x72A2C), zero does nothing at all, not
even the colour pair. The 70 in the panel call is R7, the same register the outer bevel used as its colour
index at 0x72868 (0x46 = 70).

Tests: 82 new checks. Thirty-two mutations turn at least one red: dropping the pad blit, the rails, the base
title, the panel loop, either control, or the open gate; swapping any two of the four caption records;
forcing the overlay open; giving the strip drawer a real mark instead of -1; inverting the bracket
condition; 22 steps instead of 23; shifting either bracket arm by one; letting the row loop run one base
too far; reading nBaseCount unsigned; flipping the tail compare; adopting a base with no capacity;
comparing dwActionFail against non-zero; moving the shortfall panel by one pixel; swapping the outer and
the middle bevel colours; moving the title by 20 in x or 10 in y; moving the row name by 20 in x or 10 in
y; shrinking the erase strip by one row; and shrinking the blend in x or in y. One mutation was tried that
no test can see and is not counted: the 210-wide panel rect narrowed from 210 to 200 -- the 32-wide erase
strip at x 208..239 covers exactly the difference, so both versions leave the same pixels.

Deviations, recorded: the port reads the four captions through a pTextRecs pointer and the base names
through a BaseSiteRec array instead of the original's fixed globals; it bounds the base index the title
uses; it takes the strip drawer and the two control blits as seams; it keeps the working base index and the
drawn base index as two env fields where the original has one global and one argument; and it guards the
pad pointer, the panel list, the base-count pointer and the strip hook that the original reaches unguarded.
## Unit 92 - the base-info screen's panels (BaseInfoScreen_Init @ 0x57688, BaseInfoScreen_BuildPanels @ 0x557f4)

Ported: BaseInfoScreen_Init (312 B) and BaseInfoScreen_BuildPanels (6,084 B) in src/pufo/game/pufo_baseui.c,
declared in pufo_baseui.h as BaseInfoScreenInitEnv / BaseInfoBuildEnv. Tests: TestBaseInfoBuildPanels and
TestBaseInfoInit in tests/test_baseui.c, 135 checks.

Init @ 0x57688 takes the address of the three-slot block at 0x158828. Slot 0 is the screen pad: operator
new(0x14), PadImage_ctor, PadImage_Load("baseinfo", 14) (aBaseinfo @ 0xAB20C), then both origins are set to 0.
Slots 1 and 2 are controls: two rounds of operator new(0x20) plus UiControl_ctor, then slot 1 gets
BaseInfoScreen_OnOk @ 0x557c8 and slot 2 gets BaseInfoScreen_TogglePanelMode @ 0x55754 through +0x0C. The shared
close control g_pUiCloseCtl is moved to (224, 1) and given BaseInfoScreen_CloseThunk @ 0x557bc. Both controls then
run UiControl_Setup(ctl, 0, 0, stru_AB198[i]) - the descriptors are {1, 300, "emptyb", "cemptyb", "", 0} and
{120, 300, ...}, so the OK button lands at (1, 300) and the toggle at (120, 300), both in mode 0. The tail is
byte_1870F4 = nSelectedBaseIdx, byte_1870F8 = 0, then BaseInfoScreen_BuildPanels() as a tail call.

BuildPanels @ 0x557f4 has two arms off bBaseInfoPanelsBuilt @ 0x15883C. The release arm (0x56F0C..0x56F90)
clears the flag, UiPanel_FreeLines plus operator delete on pBaseInfoPanelNames, pBaseInfoPanelFree and
pBaseInfoPanelTotals, then UiControl_FreePads plus delete on the two slots after pBaseInfoPad - that is
0x15882C and 0x158830. It does NOT free pBaseInfoPad itself; Geoscape_CloseUI @ 0x8BE00 does that.
The build arm sets the flag, sets bBaseInfoPanelMode @ 0xAB190 to 1, and builds three UiPanel(42).

Panel geometry, shared except for x, the click-rect left and the view width: nStyle 16, nFont 16, pfnClick null,
nPosY 40, nUnk7056 70, SetBytes0to2(B4, B4, B4), SetBytes6to11(F0, F0, F0, 14, 14, 14), bFlag7073 and bFlag7072
cleared. The name column is x 10, nUnk7052 5, nViewW 200 and never touches nUnk7076; the free column is x 130,
nUnk7052 210, nViewW 10, nUnk7076 1; the total column is x 190 with the same narrow settings.

Every label on this screen is a clear, not a string. The 42-row loop at 0x559B4 copies from 0x10DA38 into all
three panels, and the per-row label copies at 0x55A90..0x55C58 (name rows 0..16), 0x55FE4..0x56178 (name rows
nShips+18..nShips+25) and 0x56D8C..0x56DCC (total rows 14 and 15) copy from 0x104C7B, 0x104D48, ... 0x105C7F,
0x105D4C and 0x105E19. All of those sit above 0xAC800, past the end of the .data file image (.data is va 0xA6000,
vsz 0xE2D70, rsz only 0x6800), and none of them has a write xref anywhere in the binary: they are zero-filled
scratch, so each copy writes an empty string. The port reproduces them as clears.

Craft list, 0x55E28..0x55F20. Map_nCraftCount @ 0x114B4C is read unsigned (ANDS R3, R0, #0xFF then CMP #0 / BLS),
byte_1870F4 signed (LDRSB at 0x55E6C) and Ship.bHomeBase unsigned (LDRB at 0x55E70); a craft joins the list when
the two match. The name is Ship_FormatDisplayName(Ship_FindIndexById(Ship.bId)) - the display name comes from the
id lookup, while the three aux writes come from the roster slot: name aux = Ship.bCraftType, free aux = Ship.bId,
total aux = 1 as the run marker. Rows start at 17 and the counter only advances on a match.

Row map. Free column: 1 soldiers aboard, 2 engineers free, 3 scientists free, 6..10 the capacity deltas
(living quarters minus Base_CalcOccupiedSpace, stores minus Base_CalcStorageUsed, labs minus
Base_CountActiveResearch, workshops minus Base_CountActiveManuf, hangar minus Base_CountInboundTransfers(-1, scan
ON) minus Base_CountShipsAtBase), 17.. the craft cost labels, nShips+19/20/21 the fixed unit prices 20000$,
20000$ and 30000$, nShips+23 the facility total and nShips+25 the grand total. Total column: 1, 2, 3 the crew
counts, 6..10 the five capacities, 13 Base_CountBuiltFacilities, nShips+19/20/21 the money breakdown
20000*soldiers$, 20000*engineers$ and 30000*scientists$. Name column: SetLineMeta(200, 150, -106, 50, 10, 10) on
rows 0, 5, 12, 16 and on nShips+18, nShips+23, nShips+25.

The soldiers-aboard loop (0x56364) runs while the TOTAL column's aux is 1 and passes the FREE column's aux, which
is Ship.bId. This is the only Craft_CountSoldiersAboard @ 0x6649c call site in the binary that passes a craft id
rather than the roster index; every other caller passes the index. Recorded as a comment on the function.

The craft cost loop (0x566A4..0x5685C) is where Hex-Rays misleads. It renders the aux-0 case as a break out of
the loop, but the break only leaves the switch: 0x56810 writes "500000$" and 0x56838 adds 500000, and the loop
test at 0x56858 then continues. So aux 0 is priced like aux 1 and the run keeps going; only the total column's
marker ceasing to be 1 ends it. A type outside 0..4 takes the switch default: no label, no cost, run continues.

The money total (0x56958) is 20000 * (Base_CountSoldiers + engineers held here) + 30000 * scientists held here +
the craft sum. The facility part (0x56A74..0x56AE0) walks grid + 144*base + 108 + k, reading [R1+372] and
advancing R1 by 6, which is the same 36 cells as grid + 480 + 144*base that every capacity pass walks; each cell
whose type byte is not 0xFF adds 50000, built or not. The final scan (0x56DD4..0x56ED4) re-clears total rows 14
and 15 for every cell of kind 4 or kind 5 - both sources are zero-filled scratch, so it has no visible effect.

Deviations. The port nulls the three panel slots and the two control slots after freeing them; the original
leaves them dangling (nothing reads them before the next build). The port refuses a null environment, guards the
three panel pointers after allocation and bounds every row index, where the original dereferences and indexes
blindly. snprintf("%d") stands in for j_itoa @ 0x9e9f0. The original frees no pad in the release arm and the port
matches that.

Unobservable by construction, so no test can pin them: the clear of name row nShips+17, the eight-row clear count
at 0x55FE4, the 42-row clear count and the kind-4/kind-5 re-clear all write empty strings over rows that are
already empty. Four mutations in exactly those places stay green, as expected.

IDB: unk_158824 -> pBaseInfoPanelNames, unk_158820 -> pBaseInfoPanelFree, unk_158838 -> pBaseInfoPanelTotals
(all typed UiPanel *), byte_AB190 -> bBaseInfoPanelMode, asc_AB1D8 -> aDollarSign. Comments added at 0x557f4 (the
row map and the zero-filled-scratch finding), 0x56810 (the aux-0 continuation that Hex-Rays renders as a break),

## Unit 93 - the base-info screen's frame (BaseInfoScreen_Draw @ 0x56fb8)

Ported: BaseInfoScreen_Draw (1,744 B) in src/pufo/game/pufo_baseui.c, declared with BaseInfoDrawEnv in
pufo_baseui.h. Test: TestBaseInfoDraw in tests/test_baseui.c, 58 checks.

Everything sits behind bBaseInfoPanelsBuilt @ 0x15883C: with the flag clear the screen draws nothing at all.

The grey ramp (0x56FE8..0x57210) is 24 steps of 5 pixels, x 0..115. Each step draws a 5x1 block at x+1 in the
triple (5*(step+20), same, same) and another at x+119 in (-6-5*step, same, same). Both are BYTES, so the right
one wraps: 250, 245, ... 135 while the left climbs 100, 105, ... 215. Three y bands. With bBaseInfoPanelMode
set they are fixed at 35, 113 and 225; with it clear they are 35, 18*shipsAtBase+59 and 18*shipsAtBase+169,
where shipsAtBase is Base_CountShipsAtBase for byte_1870F4 -- the original re-reads it on all four calls
(0x57118, 0x57158, 0x57198, 0x571D8) of every step, with identical arguments.

The two halves of the ramp OVERLAP. The left one reaches x 120 and the right one starts at x 119, and the left
block of a step is drawn before that step's right block but the steps run in order, so the left ramp's last
block (x 116..120) overdraws the right ramp's first block at x 119 and 120. Only 3 of its 5 pixels survive per
band, which is what the pixel counts pin: 250 appears 9 times in the frame, not 15. The byte arithmetic also
makes the two halves share colours -- -6-5*7 = -41 = 215 as a byte, and 5*(7+20) = 135 -- so 215 and 135 each
appear 30 times rather than 15.

UiPanelMsg_Draw runs on the three columns in build order (0x57218..0x57230). Only the name column's rows 0, 5,
12 and 16 carry a meta colour from BuildPanels; every other row keeps the zeroed meta and draws in black, so
the test puts text on a meta row to prove the columns really reach the surface.

The base name is copied from the site record at byte_186C24 + 64*base + 54 into a 60-byte local and centred at
(120, 13) at 0x57284 -- BEFORE Gfx_PackRgb565Pair(68, 244, 252, 4, 70, 75) runs at 0x5729C. The name is
therefore drawn in whatever colour the palette already held, not in the pair this function packs. TEXTS[1112]
then goes centred at (60, 300), and the toggle label at (180, 300) is TEXTS[1113] while the mode flag is set
and TEXTS[1114] while it is clear. All three are real lang.dat records, not the zero-filled scratch the panel
labels use: 1112 "Âûáîð áàçû", 1113 "Ìåñÿ÷íûé ðàñõîä", 1114 "Áàçà". They are now aTextBaseInfoSelect,
aTextBaseInfoMonthly and aTextBaseInfoBase, each char[205].

Overlay (byte_1870F8): a 32-wide erase strip at x 208 of height 28*nBaseCount + 4, Base_DrawFacilityIconStrip
with the mark -1 so it paints no chevron of its own, the 210-wide rect, then one row per base with 205/204/201
wide bevels at (3, 28*i+3), (3, 28*i+4) and (5, 28*i+5) and its name centred at (110, 28*i+7). The two erase
rects together cover x 0..239 of that band, and the test pins each rect's own extent with a pre-painted pixel
at x 207 (only the 210-wide rect reaches it) and x 235 (only the 32-wide strip reaches it). Unlike the psi
frame there is no bracket on a base with no psi lab.

The adopt arm (0x57500..0x57570) is INSIDE the overlay arm. When byte_158834 differs from byte_1870F4 the draw
itself copies it, clears byte_1870F8 and bBaseInfoPanelsBuilt, frees the three panels with UiPanel_FreeLines
plus delete and calls BaseInfoScreen_BuildPanels again. So a base the geoscape moved to is picked up on the
next draw, not on a click -- and with the overlay closed a differing base is left alone entirely.

Deviations. The port refuses a null environment, guards the panel list and each panel pointer, bounds the site
record index against the eight slots, bounds the name copy to the 60-byte local (the original's copy at
0x57250..0x57264 is unbounded), and computes Base_CountShipsAtBase once per step instead of four times.

58 new checks; all 35 mutations turn at least one red, so nothing in this function is left unpinned.

IDB: unk_EB348 -> aTextBaseInfoSelect, unk_EB415 -> aTextBaseInfoMonthly, unk_EB4E2 -> aTextBaseInfoBase (all
char[205]); a function comment at 0x56fb8 covering the ramp, the overlap and the adopt arm, and a line comment
at 0x57118 recording the four identical Base_CountShipsAtBase calls.
## Unit 94 - the base-attack screen (BaseAtScreen_Update @ 0x57808, BaseAtScreen_Draw @ 0x58728, BaseAtScreen_CloseThunk @ 0x577c0)

Ported: BaseAtScreen_Update (3,872 B), BaseAtScreen_Draw (420 B) and BaseAtScreen_CloseThunk (72 B) in
src/pufo/game/pufo_baseui.c, declared with BaseAtUpdateEnv, BaseAtDrawEnv and BaseAtCloseEnv in
pufo_baseui.h. Tests: TestBaseAtUpdate, TestBaseAtDraw and TestBaseAtCloseThunk in tests/test_baseui.c.

This is the report a base gets when a mission site lands on it. Geoscape_SpawnMissionSite fills the block
at 0x158840..0x158849 from the strateg item (0x7EF50..0x7EF70): nBaseAtClass = bCraftClass (+2, read
SIGNED), nBaseAtStrategIdx = the item's creation serial at +0x34, byte_158848 = nTargetIdx (+0x84),
nAssaultBaseRace = bRace (+0x70); it pauses the game, writes the screen id 20 to 0x186BC4, and tail-calls
BaseAtScreen_Open with the base index read SIGNED from the same +0x84. Geoscape_CloseUI case 20 (0x8BAF8)
is the teardown: the same opener with nMode -1, which now takes the release arm. The port's
Geoscape_SpawnMissionSite has NOT reproduced that assault branch yet - it routes the screen through
SpawnMissionHooks.pfnContactScreen. Recorded as a separate issue.

THE OUTER LOOP IS THE BARRAGE, NOT THE GRAVITY PAIR. Hex-Rays renders 0x57BEC..0x583F0 as a while(1) with
a break into a second while(1), which hides what the ARM says: 0x583F0 is `BLT loc_57BE8` and 0x57BEC is
`STR R10, [SP, #var_B8]`, so the per-kind pair counters are reset at the top of the round loop and the
defence pairs are re-emitted in every one of the (gravity + 1) rounds. The capacity at 0x57A94,
2*(defenceCells*(gravity + 1) + gravity) + 3, is exactly the row count that structure produces - that is
what proves it. With one missile cell and two gravity cells the log is 13 rows: defence pair, gravity
pair, defence pair, gravity pair, defence pair, then the tail.

The budget comes from switch((char)nBaseAtClass) at 0x5784C: 50, 200, 250, 500, 500, 1200, 2200, 3000 for
class 0..7 - the ARM builds the last two as 2192|8 and 2992|8 - and 0 for anything else, which makes even
an out-of-range class lose on the first pair. A pair is rolled with Game_RandU16(100): below the kind's
threshold the defence HITS (green meta 50,255,50 / 0,20,0, TEXTS[1116], budget -= damage), at or above it
the defence MISSES (red meta 255,50,50 / 20,0,0, TEXTS[1117]). Thresholds 50/60/70/80 and damages
500/600/900/1500 for kind 13/14/15/16, so the better the defence the more often it misses and the harder
it hits. Each threshold is pinned by a seed whose roll falls in the band below the next kind's threshold:
the same roll of 50..59 is a missile miss and a laser hit, 60..69 a laser miss and a plasma hit, 70..79 a
plasma miss and a fusion hit. Each damage is pinned by how far the budget reaches: 1200 burns over three
missile hits but over two laser hits, 2200 over three plasma hits, 3000 over two fusion hits.

ORIGINAL BUG, not reproduced: the emitted row count is 2*(D*(G+1)+G)+3 with D+G <= 36, which peaks at 723
for 18 gravity and 18 defence cells - past the 500 line buffers a UiPanel holds, so the writes run through
apLines[500] at +0xBE4 into anLineAux[500] at +0x13B4 and then past the 0x1BB4 block. UiPanel_ctor's clamp
and the line setters' bounds stop that in the port.

UNPINNABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: the budget is tested only after a pair is emitted and every damage is at least
500, so the budgets 50, 200, 250, 500 and 500 all die on the first hit. No observable behaviour separates
classes 0..4 from each other; only 1200, 2200 and 3000 can be told apart.

The grid scan (0x57914..0x57A38) reads the type byte at 36*(4*base+3)+372+cell, which is 480+144*base+cell
- the same type layer the base-info screen uses - and the days byte at 36*base+cell, both with the cell
index 6*row + col. Hex-Rays renders both through the buildDays array type, which is why the strides look
different for one cell. Every kind test also requires the cell to be free, so a cell under construction is
not a defence, and a hangar is not one either.

The tail is three rows with aux 0. The first is the EMPTY label: 0x58464 is `LDR R0, =0x10DA38`, a pointer
into zero-filled .data, not a TEXTS record. Then either TEXTS[1125] "ÍËÎ âûñàäèëîñü ðÿäîì ñ áàçîé" and
TEXTS[1126] "Ïîäãîòîâêà ê çàùèòå" with bBaseAtMissionFollows = 1 - the budget survived and the ground
mission follows - or TEXTS[1123] "ÍËÎ óíè÷òîæåí" and TEXTS[1124] "Óãðîçà çàõâàòà ñíÿòà" with the flag
clear. nBaseAtLineLimit is the row count, nRadarCooldownR goes to 255 and nLineCount to 0, so the reveal
starts again from row 0.

Draw reveals one row per cooldown: with nRadarCooldownR at 255 and rows still hidden it parks the cooldown
at 255 - aux of the row about to be shown (20 for a defence row, 10 for the gravity pair's second row, 0
for a tail row, which the geoscape's saturating counter reaches at once), shows that row, and scrolls once
the shown count passes nStyle (15). When every row is shown the shared confirm control goes to
x = 120 - (uWidth >> 1), y 290, bBaseAtConfirmShown is set - the byte Geoscape_OnPointer (0x89414) and
Geoscape_OnPointerUp (0x8AF70) gate on - its pad is blitted, and TEXTS[1127] "ÎÊ" is drawn centred at
(120, 290) in the same caption colour pair the base-info and psi frames pack. The "baseat" pad (mode 30,
240x320) paints 143 pixels of the cleared frame, which is what pins the pad identity.

CloseThunk: with bBaseAtMissionFollows clear the contact is over, so StrategList_RemoveAt drops the item
(nBaseAtStrategIdx is the index) and 0x15961C - GameTime.bPaused - is cleared. Either way it tail-calls
Geoscape_CloseUI, whose case 20 runs Update's release arm. The release arm restores nLineCount from
nBaseAtLineCap BEFORE freeing, so UiPanel_FreeLines reaches every line buffer: the draw had left nLineCount
at the revealed row count, which is smaller.

Deviations. A null environment, panel, pad or counter is refused; the base index is bounded to the eight
grid blocks (the original's -1 call would read grid - 36 and grid + 336 if it reached the build arm); the
original writes nLineCount from the capacity before testing the panel for null and blits the pad and calls
UiPanelMsg_Draw untested; the freed slots are nulled; and the labels go straight to UiPanel_SetLineText
instead of through the original's 152-byte stack buffer.

A 78-mutation sweep over the three functions turned 73 of them red. The five that stayed green are equivalences, not gaps: the (i8) craft-class cast cannot differ from (u8) because class bytes are 0..7; the nGravity > 0 conjunct is dead because the round loop already breaks at nRound >= nGravity; SetBytes3to5 and SetBytes6to11 write disjoint byte ranges so their order is irrelevant; an un-freed pad is a leak with no observable effect; and the scroll gate > against >= is masked by UiPanel_ScrollNext's own nUnk3028 < nLineCount - nStyle guard. The sweep also found two defects in the tests themselves: a static StrategItem handed to PtrArray_DeleteAt, which free()s its element, aborted the suite with 0xC0000409 and silently truncated the run before it, and a claimed 143 painted pixels that turned out to be the panel's own row text -- the pad blit paints nothing until a palette is loaded for its index slot.

## Unit 95 - the hangar's stores-transfer panel set (BasePlaneScreen_BuildControls @ 0x7b014, 2,788 B)

Ported in src/pufo/game/pufo_plane.c as BasePlaneScreen_BuildControls(PlaneStorePanels *out, const
PlaneStoreBuildEnv *env). The original takes no arguments -- the decompiler's
`__fastcall BasePlaneScreen_BuildControls(struct BasePlaneScreen *pScr)` is invented (0x7B014 is
`PUSH {R4-R11,LR}` straight into a global load), and the same is true of BasePlaneScreen_Draw at
0x7D374. Both signatures are corrected in the IDB.

**bPlaneStoresCommitted @ 0x161F28 picks the arm**, and the IDB had it as a 12-byte object although every
access to it in the binary is LDRB or STRB; it is one byte now. The teardown clears it FIRST (0x7BA18),
before releasing anything, then walks the two store-nav control slots at the object block's +0x64 / +0x68
(0x161AAC, 0x161AB0 -- `ADD R4,R4,#4` twice from pPlaneBackdropPad) through UiControl_FreePads and
operator delete, then the five panels in the order slot (0x7BA48), sel-row (0x7BA68), avail, commit-row,
taken. The original frees through the globals and never nulls them.

**The build raises the flag before a single row exists** (0x7B12C). The flag means "this panel set is
live", not "a row was committed", which is why BasePlaneScreen_Close tests it the same way
CommitStores sets it, and why a teardown is reachable even when the build listed nothing.

**The crew quota is seeded from the craft rather than zeroed** (0x7B05C..0x7B09C): it is
apObjects[31..35]->aItemQty[nSelectedCraftIdx], and the loop reaches slot 31 as the context base 0x1139B8
plus 0x184, which is apObjects + 0x7C. The running total is stored on every step (0x7B070), not once at
the end.

**The row filter is three ARM compares** -- 0x7B190 `CMP #0x19 / BLT keep`, 0x7B198 `CMP #0x1E / BLE
skip`, 0x7B1A0 `CMP #0x34 / BGE skip` -- so a slot gets a row when `slot < 25 || (slot > 30 && slot < 52)`.
The refused band 25..30 is the six weapon slots the hangar draws through its own weapon columns (the
SelectWeapon25..30 handlers), and 52 is ObjectRecFull.aItemQty's own length.

**Each admitted slot then needs the base to stock it or the craft to carry it** (0x7B1B8
`LDRH [obj,#0x2A]` = auPerBaseVal[base], 0x7B1C8 `LDRH [obj,#0x3A]` = aItemQty[craft]) **and its
unlocking research topic to be unlocked**: `aResearchTopics[g_abSlotTopicGate[slot]].bUnlocked`, ARM
0x7B1D4 `LDRB [slot, table]`, `MUL #0x22` (34 = sizeof ResearchTopicLive), 0x7B1E4 `LDRB [#0xD]`. The
pair and the row counter are all under the same STRNE (0x7B1F0, 0x7B1FC, 0x7B204), so a slot the topic
gate refuses leaves a cleared pair behind rather than an uninitialised one -- which is what makes the row
pass's re-test of the pair well-defined.

**byte_AA968 is a 156-byte slot-to-topic table**, now g_abSlotTopicGate in the IDB (it runs to the next
global at 0xAAA04). Slots 0..24 map to topics 0,1,6,9,2,7,10,4,3,8,5,11,13,12,18,23,24,22,21,25,14,15,17,
20,16; slots 31..35 to topics 97..101; 37 to 113, 39 to 114, 40..47 to 1, and 48..50 to 115, 117, 116.

**Five panels, one shared style, five geometries.** All five are operator new 0x1BB4 with
UiPanel_ctor(row count), nStyle 14, nFont 16, nPosY 70, nUnk7056 70, gap_0[0..2] B4,B4,B4 and gap_0[6..11]
F0,F0,F0,14,14,14. They differ as: slot (0x161AC8) x 10, band left 5, width 125, click
Cache_ObjPlus0xBD8_To_dword_186BE8, bFlag7073 1, bUnk7088 0x96; avail (0x161A40) x 164, band left 130,
width 50, no click, bFlag7073 0, bFlag7074 1, nUnk7076 2; sel-row (0x161F00) x 170, band left 166, width
15, click BasePlaneScreen_AdjustSelectedQty, bFlag7073 1, gap_0[3..5] 32,32,FA, nUnk7084 5, bUnk7088 0x96;
commit-row (0x161EEC) x 186, band left 182, width 15, click BasePlaneScreen_CommitStores, same extras;
taken (0x161EF4) x 232, band left 190, width 45, no click, bFlag7073 0, bFlag7074 1, nUnk7076 2. The two
count columns keep UiPanel_ctor's bUnk7088 0xFF -- BuildControls only writes that byte where it also
writes bFlag7073. nUnk7084 5 on the two 15-wide quantity columns is UiPanel_ClickRow's auto-repeat count,
so holding the "<" or ">" row repeats the quantity change every fifth click.

**The row pass** (0x7B7D0..0x7B930) re-tests the stored pair, copies apObjects[slot]->szName through a
112-byte stack buffer cut to 17 characters when strlen is above 0x11 (0x7B838 `CMP R3, #0x11`, so an
18-character name is already cut and a 17-character one is not), writes the SLOT id into the slot panel's
aux column (0x7B8A0), "<" (aRowQtyDec @ 0xABC24) into the sel-row line and ">" (aRowQtyInc @ 0xABC20)
into the commit-row line, and puts the two counts into the avail and taken panels' aux columns -- the
decompiler renders those stores as `gap_0[row*4+5044]`, and 5044 is anLineAux at +0x13B4. The row index
advances only for kept slots while the slot counter advances for all of them, which is what makes the aux
column a slot id rather than a row index.

**The sort walks nObjectCount-1 order entries, not the table's 148** (0x7B9F4 `CMP R11, R3,LSR#16` on the
u16 Map_nObjectCount read with LDRH at 0x7B9D0), and it swaps THREE panels -- slot, avail, taken -- where
the buy/sell builders swap five. With the shipped 149 objects the two bounds coincide, so the shorter walk
is invisible in the shipped game; with 60 objects it is not, and the test pins the difference: slots 1,
24, 31, 32, 34, 35 and 51 come out as 1, 51, 24, 31, 34, 35, 32 because 32, 34 and 35 sit at table
indices 60, 63 and 64, past the walk.

128 new checks in test_plane. A 46-mutation sweep -- the reduced form, behaviour-bearing values only -- turned all 46 red. Four were unpinned on the first run and all four turned out to be defects in the tests rather than equivalences: three compared a value against the very macro the mutation moves (the 256-slot carry clear, the two row labels), so shrinking the macro shrank the expectation with it; and the fourth swapped the two nav clicks between fixture handlers that were empty functions, which the linker's identical-code folding (MSVC /OPT:ICF, on by default in Release) merges into a single address, making every pointer-identity check between them vacuous. The fixtures now write distinct values into a volatile global so their bodies differ, and the same fix was applied to the thirteen empty handlers in the older TestPlaneInit, whose 'clicks are the four handlers in order' and 'clicks are Rearm plus the six weapon slots' checks were vacuous for exactly the same reason.

Deviations: the original dereferences each freshly allocated panel straight after its ctor (0x7B218 writes
nStyle with no test) and writes the two control clicks through the globals with no test either, so an
allocation failure faults; the port skips a failed allocation. The scan buffer is the 2032-byte stack
block at 0x7B018, 254 pairs, and the scan writes one pair per slot with no bound -- the shipped 149
objects fit, a Map_nObjectCount above 255 would not, and the port bounds at 254 pairs. The original also
indexes auPerBaseVal with the unbounded signed base byte and aItemQty with the unbounded craft dword
index; the port resolves both to zero out of range. The port nulls the seven freed slots, which makes a
second teardown harmless.
