## Unit 96 - the hangar frame, the craft readout and the rails (BasePlaneScreen_Draw @ 0x7d374, 1,648 B)

Ported in src/pufo/game/pufo_plane.c as BasePlaneScreen_Draw(const PlaneDrawEnv *env). The original
takes no arguments (0x7D374 is `PUSH {R4-R11,LR}` straight into a global load), which unit 95 already
corrected in the IDB.

**Three gates, and they do not gate the same amount of the screen.** bPlaneShowCraftDetail @ 0x161F20
(0x7D37C) sends the whole call into BasePlaneScreen_DrawCraftDetail and returns its value. Otherwise
bPlanePanelsBuilt @ 0x161F08 (0x7D398) decides whether the two list panels and the craft readout run -
but both `BEQ`s land on loc_7D640, the second colour pair, so the two captions and all four rail loops
run whatever the flags say: a hangar whose panels were never built still paints the frame and still
draws "Êîðàáëü: " and "Ñòàòóñ".

**The readout is gated by a geoscape flag and the pointer row.** bBaseFacPreviewActive @ 0x18652C has
six xrefs in the whole binary - four in BaseFacScreen_DrawPlacementOverlay, one in Geoscape_InitUI and
this one - and the band test is `nPosY < nSmapCursorY < nPosY + 16 * nLineCount` (0x7D3E0 reads nPosY at
+0x1B88 through `MOV R3,#0x1B80 / ORR R3,#8`, 0x7D3FC reads nLineCount at +0xBDC, 0x7D408
`ADD R3,R2,R3,LSL#4`, and `BLE` / `BGE` both skip). nSmapCursorY @ 0x186BD4 is read LDRSH and written
STRH (Geoscape_OnPointer 0x872F8), so it is the signed 16-bit pointer row the pointer dispatcher keeps
live for whichever screen owns the pointer. Unlike the transfer, manuf and research frames, this band
has no nStyle cap.

**The three sums all index aItemQty with nPlaneSelCraftIdx @ 0x161F04** - the draw uses that global,
not the nSelectedCraftIdx @ 0x161AC4 the stores builder uses - and each walk runs 0..Map_nObjectCount-1
(LDRH at 0x7D41C), skipping a slot whose aItemQty is zero before the band test. Armament is slots 25..30
(0x7D45C `CMP #0x18 / BLE`, 0x7D464 `CMP #0x1F / ADDLT`), the six weapon slots the SelectWeapon25..30
handlers cover; crew quantity is slots 31..35 (0x7D4A4 `CMP #0x1E / BLE`, 0x7D4AC `CMP #0x24 / ADDLT`),
the same five crew slots the crew quota sums; crew aboard is the soldiers whose Soldier.bUnk183 @ +0xB7
equals the craft index (0x7D4C4..0x7D500, nSoldierCount read LDRH, the pointer array at the context's
+0x1198). The compare is `CMP R3,R5` with R3 the zero-extended byte and R5 the dword index, so a craft
index above 255 matches nothing.

**The armament value is a pair, not a number**: itoa(v3), then strcat with the single backslash at
aQtyPairSep @ 0xAB9F0 (0x7D5A8 / 0x7D5B0), then strcat with itoa(apCraft[nPlaneSelCraftIdx]
->bCrewSlots @ +0x14) (0x7D5D0 / 0x7D5E0). The five captions are real lang.dat records - the IDB's own
TEXTS region is zero-filled because the text loads at runtime - read out of lang.dat at 0x102 + 200*n.
TEXTS[146] "Âîîðóæåíèå" at (25,23), TEXTS[147] "Ýêèïàæ" at (25,43), TEXTS[148] "ÒÎÏ êîë-âî" at (25,63),
the three values at (190,23), (195,43), (195,63); then TEXTS[124] "Êîðàáëü: " at (25,90) and TEXTS[153]
"Ñòàòóñ" at (165,90). Two colour pairs: (250,250,250 / 20,25,20) at 0x7D504 before the readout and
(250,250,250 / 10,10,25) at 0x7D640 before the captions.

**Four rail loops, and the two inner ones test their bound AFTER the step.** Rails A and B are the
shared screen rails - 24 steps of 7 on the sides and 24 steps of 5 on the top and bottom, the same
constants and the same 5*(k+20) / 230-5k / 250-5k ramps the transfer, manuf and research frames carry -
so the port calls BaseUi_DrawFrameRails, which is now shared across four screens rather than three.
Rail C (0x7D840..0x7D8FC) runs a climbing x from 15 against a descending x from 220, both stepping 5
while the descending one stays above 115; the test comes after the step, so the body at x2 = 120 runs
too - 21 bodies, colour 5*(n+20) with n 0..20, 5x1 at y 15 and 85. Rail D (0x7D8FC..0x7D9B4) runs m from
0 down in steps of 2 with the same shape, so m = -34 / v = 17 draws too - 18 bodies, colour 100..185,
1x2 at x 15 and 224, y 2v+15 and m+83. The two x runs 15..119 and 120..224 are continuous, and the two
y halves meet at 49..50 rather than leaving a gap: together they close a rectangle from (15,15) to
(224,85) around the readout. The rails run AFTER the text, so they paint over it where they overlap.

61 new checks in test_baseui, drawn into a real 240x320 surface with the real font. The readout window
(x 14..229, y 14..99) is compared against a hand-painted frame - the labels, the three value strings,
the shared rails and the inner rails painted from the ARM with literals rather than the port's macros -
so the exact strings "16\9", "3" and "13", their positions and the inner frame's geometry are all pinned
at once; separate probes then move one input at a time (a decoy quantity outside each band, a quantity
inside it, Ship.bCrewSlots, nSoldierCount, a craft index past the array) and re-compare. A 47-mutation sweep -- behaviour-bearing values only -- turned all 47 red. Two were unpinned on the first run and both were the macro-aliasing defect again: the fixture placed its caption text with the same record macro the port reads, so moving the macro moved the expectation with it, and the fixtures now use literal record numbers. The third was a pattern that matched two loops in the file rather than a gap in the tests.

Deviations: the original dereferences both panel pointers, every apObjects and apSoldiers entry it walks
and the craft pointer at apCraft[nPlaneSelCraftIdx] with no null test, and indexes aItemQty with the
unbounded dword craft index; the port skips a null entry and resolves an out-of-range craft index to
zero / no craft. The value string is built by itoa into the 52-byte var_34 @ sp+0x48, an unbounded
byte-copy loop into the 56-byte psz @ sp+0x10 (0x7D590) and two unbounded strcat; the port builds the
same string in one bounded snprintf. BasePlaneScreen_DrawCraftDetail is not ported and enters as a hook.

IDB: 6 renames (unk_BADBA to aTextRec146_ArmamentCap, unk_BAE87 to aTextRec147_CrewCap, unk_BAF54 to
aTextRec148_CrewQtyCap, unk_B9C1C to aTextRec124_CraftCaption, unk_BB355 to aTextRec153_StatusCaption,
asc_AB9F0 to aQtyPairSep); a function comment at 0x7d374 and line comments at 0x7D38C, 0x7D3E0, 0x7D408,
0x7D41C, 0x7D45C, 0x7D464, 0x7D4A4, 0x7D4AC, 0x7D4F0, 0x7D5A8, 0x7D5D0, 0x7D640, 0x7D6AC, 0x7D770,
0x7D840 and 0x7D8FC. BaseUi_DrawFrameRails is no longer file-local, since the hangar draws the same

## Unit 97 - the hangar's other face (BasePlaneScreen_DrawCraftDetail @ 0x7baf8, 3,824 B)

Ported in src/pufo/game/pufo_plane.c as BasePlaneScreen_DrawCraftDetail(const PlaneDetailEnv *env).
BasePlaneScreen_Draw enters it straight away when bPlaneShowCraftDetail @ 0x161F20 is set (0x7D37C) and
returns its value, so the hook unit 96 carried for it is gone: the draw env now carries the detail env.

**Two gates, and the first one short-circuits everything.** Rails A and B are byte-for-byte the shared
screen rails, so the port calls BaseUi_DrawFrameRails. Then Ship_FormatDisplayName is byte-copied into
psz @ sp+0x88 (52 B) and measured, and the width stays in a register four separate exits reuse. The
craft index is worth naming: this screen reads nSelectedCraftIdx @ 0x161AC4 where BasePlaneScreen_Draw
reads nPlaneSelCraftIdx @ 0x161F04 (0x7BCAC). bPlaneListPanelsBuilt @ 0x161F24 set draws the crew pair
(pPlaneCrewPanel @ 0x161EDC, pPlaneCrewStatusPanel @ 0x161A3C), packs (200,200,200 / 10,25,10), puts the
name at (120 - w/2, 30) and returns -- both the stores panel set and the craft read-out are skipped.

**STORES ARM (0x7BD70..0x7C228).** dwActionFail @ 0x1870C8 read as a dword decides the two row panels'
bFlag7073: exactly 1 clears it on pPlaneSelRowPanel @ 0x161F00 and pPlaneCommitRowPanel @ 0x161EEC,
anything else sets it to 1 -- and the 1 is the leftover R11 from the rail loop's nRectH (0x7BDA4..
0x7BDC4), not a constant the reader can see. Then (150,150,255 / 20,20,20), TEXTS[89] "Êîðàáëü" centred
on 210 and TEXTS[155] "Áàçà" centred on 147 at y 54. bPanelFlagScratch @ 0x161F0C is copied into both
row panels' bUnk7080 and cleared: a one-shot flag a row click sets and this draw consumes. The band is
16 * min(nLineCount, nStyle) of the SELECT-ROW panel (0x7BE7C..0x7BEAC, `MOVGE R3,R0,LSL#4`), every
separator is 1 x (band + 2) at y 69 in palette index 0xB4, and the order is separator 130, avail,
separator 166, sel-row, separator 181, commit-row, separator 196, taken -- so the avail panel paints
over the separator at 166 rather than the other way round.

**The bottom line splits on a flag that looks like the one unit 96 used but is not.** bBaseFacPreviewOk
@ 0x18652D is one byte away from the bBaseFacPreviewActive @ 0x18652C the craft read-out gates on, in
the same control block, and the band is 75 < nSmapCursorY < band + 75 with both ends exclusive. Armed,
it packs (150,150,255 / 20,20,55) and draws the hovered row's object name at (10, 297) -- the pointer it

(200,200,200 / 10,25,10) and the name at (120 - w/2, 30), then (220,80,80 / 50,30,30) and -- only when
dwActionFail is exactly 1 -- the refusal panel: Ui_AnimExpandBlit_IfEnabled over (20, 130, 200, 70) plus
TEXTS[410] "Íåò ìåñòà íà êîðàáëå" for dwActionFailReason @ 0x1870B4 == 0, TEXTS[408] "Íåò ñâîáîäíûõ
õðàíèëèù" for 1 and TEXTS[409] "Íåò áîåïðèïàñîâ äëÿ ÒÎÏ" for 2, centred at (120 - w/2, 158). Any other
reason returns with the red pair packed and nothing drawn. The map is a switch, not the buy/sell
screen's 405 + reason: the two screens read one dword and pick different records out of the same six.

**DETAIL ARM (0x7C22C..0x7C9DC).** (200,200,200 / 10,25,10) and the name at (120 - w/2, 10); then
(100,150,250 / 10,25,10) and the two percentage lines. "Òîïëèâî " (TEXTS[144]) gets

Then the art. Ship.bCraftType picks the craft pad out of the object block's five (now pPlaneCraftPad0..4

Tail, 0x7C964..0x7C9DC: (100,150,250 / 10,10,25), then bStatPanelAOpen @ 0x161F18 picks

71 new checks in test_baseui, on a real 240x320 surface with the real font. Both arms are compared
against a hand-painted reference frame built from the ARM with literals -- the two captions, the five
panels and four separators in the original's interleaved order, the bottom line, the name, the refusal
panel and its reason string; and for the detail arm the name, the two percentage strings, the three pad
blits, the two glyph-and-count lines and the two hold strings. The pads are real 2x1 glyphs whose index
bytes are 27 (the palette entry Gfx_PackRgb565Pair writes) and 0xFE (the key every PadImage_BlitEx here
passes), so each pad blits exactly one visible pixel and the key is pinned by the second staying blank;
the craft pads keep the nOriginX the fixture gives them and the weapon pads get theirs overwritten, so
the blit position identifies which pad ran. Separate probes then move one input at a time: the two
percentage sources, a zero divisor, bCraftType 4 and 5, the mount byte 24 and 31, the four counters,
nSoldierCount 0, bCanDogfight clear, the hold cap, and the three refusal reasons.

Deviations: the original dereferences the craft pointer at apCraft[nSelectedCraftIdx] four times, every
apSoldiers and apObjects entry it walks, all seven panels, the slot panel's anLineAux at the unbounded
row cursor and the object pointer it hands Text_DrawString, with no null test; the port skips what is
missing and bounds the row cursor and the slot index. Both percentage divisions go through _rt_sdiv with
no zero test -- uRangeMax or uFuelMax of 0 is a division by zero there -- and the port reads 0 percent
/ 100 percent for that case. The name is byte-copied from the 108-byte shared scratch into the 52-byte
psz with no bound and the four scratch strings are built with unbounded strcat; the port uses bounded
copies over the same 52 / 56-byte buffers. The cargo sum here reaches slots 31..35 through the cached
pointers with no object-count bound, while the port reuses Craft_CountWeaponSlotsCarried, which bounds
the walk by Map_nObjectCount. The original returns whatever R0 holds at the exit (`POP {R4-R11,PC}`
straight after `ADD SP`); nothing reads it, and the port returns 0.

IDB: 17 renames -- the four counters (dword_161AB8 to nPlaneSoldiersAboard, unk_161EE4 to
nPlaneSoldiersAtBase, unk_161AB4 to nPlaneSoldiersUnassigned, dword_161AC0 to nPlaneCrewCarried),
unk_186BE8 to nPanelRowCursor, dword_1870B4 to dwActionFailReason, and the eleven pads in the object
block at 0x161A48 (unk_161A4C..unk_161A5C to pPlaneCraftPad0..4, unk_161A60 / dword_161A64..dword_161A70
/ unk_161A74 to pPlaneWeaponPad0..5). A function comment at 0x7baf8 and 16 line comments.
Test fixture note. The first unit-97 mutation sweep left five values unpinned and the cause was the
fixture, not the port. Font_DrawGlyph with nPal 0 reads palette slot 0, which the fixture left zeroed, so
the soldier and crew icon ids 38 and 40 blitted as colour 0 and were invisible on a zeroed surface: 38 -> 1,
38 -> 100 and 40 -> 39 all passed. The refusal-reason-0 check only counted ink inside the panel window, so
the record number 410 was free to change to 408. The pad key 0xFE was free to change to 0xFD because the
keyed index maps through palette slot 2 entry 254, which is zero unless the fixture colours it. Filling slot
0 entries 1..255 with distinct colours (entry 0 stays 0 because Font_BlitGlyph treats index 0 as transparency,
the ARM at 0xa4288 tests *v5 != 0), giving slot 2 entry 254 its own colour, and turning the reason-0 case
into a full-frame compare made every one of them observable. The sweep now catches 52 of 52 applied
mutations; a reason-3 full-frame compare also pins the switch's fall-through return.
## Unit 98 - the transfer error dump (Transfer_WriteErrorDump @ 0x996e4, 3,824 B)

Ported in src/pufo/game/pufo_baseui.c as Transfer_WriteErrorDump(const TransferDumpEnv *env), and both
call sites now call it: TransferScreen_CommitTransfer at 0x97EE4 and Smap_GrantSiteRecovery at 0x99038,
each when some base's per-object column passes 60000 (0xEA60). The pfnShowTError seam the commit env
carried while the dump was unported is gone, and both envs gained pszAppDir instead.

**It is a debug dump writer, not a UI display, and it changes no game state.** The name is
szAppDir @ 0x1883B0 + "t_error" + itoa(Game_RandU16(0xE100)) (0..57599) + ".txt", opened "wb"
(0x996EC..0x9977C). Two original defects sit in those 20 instructions: the strcpy of szAppDir into the
40-byte stack buffer at sp+0x1A0 has no bound, and fopen's result is never tested, so a failed open
sends the NULL FILE * to every fwrite and to the fclose at 0x99F4C. The binary imports no remove,
unlink or DeleteFile at all, so nothing ever deletes a dump either - a long game with an overfull base
accumulates one file per report.

**Every line ends with the 2-byte value 2573 written at 0x99784**, which is 0x0D 0x0A on the wire:
CRLF, written by `fwrite(&var_358, 2, 1, f)` rather than as part of the label.

**The header block** (0x99780..0x99954) is TRANSFERS, count= with nSmapSiteCount,
(basenumber)current base= with the second argument, and problem with obj= with the third. The base
index is sign-extended from a byte at 0x99890 (`MOV R3,R5,LSL#24 / MOV R5,R3,ASR#24`), so a base index
of 0x80 or more prints negative.

**One block per site** (0x99960..0x99F44), skipped entirely when nSmapSiteCount is not positive, and
each block opens with a bare CRLF at 0x999E0, so blocks are separated by a blank line. The nine site
values do not agree on signedness: bFlag1 (0x99A9C), bFlag0 (0x99B68), bUnk518 (0x99BEC),
bRecoveredCraftCount (0x99CF4) and bRecoveredSoldierAssign (0x99D74) are LDRSB and print signed, so a
byte of 0x80 or more prints negative, while uRecoveredSoldiers (0x99C70, LDRH) and bHasLoot (0x99DF0,
LDRB) print unsigned. Two labels carry a trailing space the reader has to keep: "transfer N " and
"add_new_ship= ". "(incoming transfer)" is appended to the SAME line as the destination base, before
its CRLF (0x99AD8..0x99B14), when the destination byte resolves through the base lookup to the very
index the dump was called with. Then "objN=<auItemQty[N]>" for N in 0..Map_nObjectCount-1.

**The site walk keeps a half-stride counter.** var_350 adds 371 (0x173) per site and is divided back
by 0x173 at 0x99EB4 to index auItemQty, while the site pointer itself advances by 742 - `MOV R3,#0x2E4
/ ORR R3,#2` at 0x99F1C. 371 is half the 742-byte SmapSite, so the counter is residue, not a second
stride; the port uses the index directly.

**Deviations.** The port bounds the 40-byte path copy, refuses a failed open with -1 instead of writing
through NULL, and writes through CreateFileA / WriteFile because the MSVC CRT deprecates the whole
fopen family and the project keeps /WX on project-wide (the same reason util/pufo_str.h exists); the
bytes on disk are identical. The original's site-id lookup is Base_FindIndexBySiteId @ 0x5a8d0, which
compares the sign-extended byte against the LDRSB field, so a site id of 0x80 or more would match a
base whose bUnk4 is the same negative byte; the port's shared Base_FindIndexByTypeByte takes a u8 and
answers -1 there. Base ids are 0..25 in the shipped data, so that case is unreachable in play.

Tests: 27 new checks in test_baseui (3682 there), the main one a byte-for-byte compare of the whole
dump file against expected text built in the test from the ARM's own labels and the fixture's own
values, plus the commit and delivery paths checked through the file they now write. A 30-mutation sweep
turned all 30 red - every label, both trailing spaces, the CRLF value, all six signedness casts, the
incoming test, the lookup bound, the object-count bound, the random maximum, both name fragments, the
block-opening CRLF and all three call-site arguments. One mutation is a true equivalence and is not
counted: `nSiteCount > 0` to `>= 0` cannot change the output, because the site loop runs zero
iterations at a count of 0 either way.

IDB: 10 line comments (0x9972C, 0x99784, 0x99890, 0x999E0, 0x99A9C, 0x99B14, 0x99C70, 0x99DF0, 0x99EB4,
0x99F1C), function comments on 0x996e4 and 0x5a8d0, no renames - szAppDir @ 0x1883B0 was already named.
Three new ledger rows: the unbounded path copy, the untested FILE *, and the dump files nothing removes.
## Unit 99 - the base facility grid's names, build icons and craft (BaseFacScreen_DrawNameGrid @ 0x61c8c, 1,840 B)

The last strat-ui function. It draws one base's 6x6 facility grid on the geoscape's logical surface,
straight out of abFacilityGrid @ 0x159768, and it is the only place the grid's four layers are read
together: buildDays (the remaining build days), tileA (the tile stamp), tileB (the facility name) and
layer2 (the craft standing in the cell).

Structure, from the ARM:

- 0x61CA4..0x61CE4: a 6x6 backdrop of the blank basebits tile, at (32*col + nSmapOriginX,
  36 + 32*row + nSmapOriginY), glyph id nBaseBitsSprBase with nPal 0. The loop bounds are 0xC0 on
  both axes, so the grid spans x 0..191 and y 36..227 - 32 px cells, six of them per axis.
- 0x61CEC..0x620E8: two passes over the cells, the first over tileB (+36) and the second over
  layer2 (+72). A zero byte skips the cell outright (0x61D58). Otherwise the sprite is the name
  tile EXCEPT for a cell that is still building in the first pass, which gets the blank tile
  (0x61D74 tests buildDays, 0x61D84 tests the pass counter left in var_18).
- buildDays == 0 stops the cell there (0x61DDC). Otherwise tileA (+0) is the stamp and 0x61E04..0x61E38
  is a seven-way compare: 1, 2, 3 draw the build icon at sprite +4, +5, +6 and the days label centred
  at (x - w/2 + 16, y + 7); 9, 10, 11 draw the icon at +13, +14, +15 and NO days label; 12 draws the
  icon at +16 with the days label at (x - w/2, y - 8); anything else draws nothing further.
- The label colour is packed at 0x61E60..0x61E84 as r1=g1=0x96, b1=0xFF, r2=g2=0, b2=0xFF, and the
  number goes through j_itoa with radix 0xA into the 4-byte var_1C - exactly enough for "255", which
  is the largest buildDays byte. itoa is called twice for the same value (the width pass and the draw).
- 0x620F0..0x623B0: the craft pass. A cell only carries a craft when tileA == 12, the hangar's
  bottom-right quadrant (0x62134). Map_nCraftCount @ 0x114B4C is read as a byte and `BLS` at 0x62154
  leaves the whole pass at zero. apCraft @ 0x114A64 is reached as Map + 0x10AC (0x1080 | 0x2C at
  0x6215C..0x62164). The craft must match the cell: bHangarX == column, bHangarY == row (0x6216C,
  0x6217C), bAtBase non-zero and bHomeBase == the base. The sprite id is layer2 + nBaseBitsSprBase -
  33..37, the five craft glyphs - and the same byte picks the vertical nudge: 33 and 35 draw 1 px HIGH
  (0x62278 falls through to the SUB #1 at 0x622B0), 34 1 px LOW, 36 unshifted, 37 2 px HIGH (SUB #2 at
  0x6221C); any other value draws nothing (0x621E0). The craft sprite sits 16 px LEFT of the cell
  origin (R9 = -0x10 at 0x62124) and 17 px above it (R10 starts at 19, bounded by 0xD3 at 0x623AC).

Deviation: the original reaches the layer2 byte through the name pass's leftover counter - var_18 is 2
by the time the craft pass runs, and 6 * 12 = 72 lands exactly on layer2 - so the addressing looks like
a row index of 12 rather than a layer offset. The port reads layer2 directly. The original bounds
nothing: nBase indexes the eight fac blocks and the eight buildDays blocks unchecked, and the craft
array is walked without a null test. The port bounds the base at 8 and skips null craft. The return
value is register residue and no caller reads it, so the port returns void.

Tests: 15 new checks in test_baseui (3697 there), the main one a whole-frame compare. A reference frame
is painted in the test from the ARM's own coordinates and sprite offsets - 36, 32, 19, -16, +7, +16, -8,
sprites +4/+5/+6/+13/+14/+15/+16, layer2 33..37 - and compared pixel-for-pixel against what the port
drew. The fixture loads the "basebits" group the way Geoscape_InitUI @ 0x85F64..0x85F80 does, because
every sprite this grid draws is a basebits sprite and fontSys_nBaseBitsSprBase is the group base; with
only "font" loaded the whole grid would have drawn sprite 0 and the compare would have proved nothing.
The empty-grid case pins the backdrop as exactly 36 full 32x32 sprites and pins the grid extent to
x 0..191 / y 36..227. Craft cases cover a craft homed to another base, a craft not at the base, the
36 nudge (unshifted), the 35 nudge, a layer2 byte outside 33..37, and a count of 0; the craft at
column 5 row 3 is deliberately off the diagonal so a port that compares bHangarX against the row cannot
pass. Base index 8, -1 and 7 pin the eight-block bound.

A 42-mutation sweep turned 41 red: every grid constant, all seven build-sprite offsets, all five craft
nudges, the nudge sign, both layer offsets in the two craft reads, the pass-layer swap, the zero-cell
skip, the zero-days skip, the unknown-stamp skip, the 9..11 upper bound, the stamp-12 test, the
pass-1 name test, the +16 centring, both packed colours, the bAtBase / bHomeBase / bHangarX / bHangarY
tests, and all six grid layout macros in pufo_geoscape.h. Three mutations are true equivalences and are
not counted: `nCraftCount <= 0` to `< 0` (the count is a byte, so at 0 both bounds leave a pass that
would run zero iterations); the days colour 255 to 250 in the blue channel (both divide by the 0.7 scale
and clamp to the same 5-bit blue 31); and `%u` to `%d` on buildDays (a byte never exceeds 127 in the
printed sense - 255 renders identically either way).

IDB: 26 line comments (0x61CA4, 0x61CB4, 0x61CD4, 0x61CE0, 0x61D58, 0x61D70, 0x61D74, 0x61D84, 0x61E00,
0x61E38, 0x61E44, 0x61E60, 0x61E88, 0x62124, 0x62134, 0x6214C, 0x62154, 0x62164, 0x6216C, 0x6217C,
0x621E0, 0x621E4, 0x62230, 0x62278, 0x622C4) plus a function comment on 0x61c8c and one on 0x85F78,
where fontSys_nBaseBitsSprBase @ 0x158294 is written with the frame count BEFORE the "basebits" load -
the fact that makes every facility tile a basebits sprite. Three new ledger rows: the unbounded base
index, the blind craft-array deref, and the residue return.

## Unit 100 - shutting the credits and the ending down (Titles_Shutdown @ 0x3826c, Titles_dtor @ 0x46fa4, EndScreen_Shutdown @ 0x389f8)

Three small release functions that complete the `titles` subsystem (13/13). They are the screen-16 and
screen-18 arms of Input_OnPointerUp @ 0x14924, and until now both were seams the shell never filled.

Titles_Shutdown (100 B), in order: Sound_Shutdown (0x38270), KillTimers_C (0x38274), Font_Free on
fontSys @ 0x158268 (0x3827C), then five operator delete over 0x1571A0..0x1571B0 (0x38280..0x3828C) --
the five titlesN.pad glyph blobs Titles_Init allocated at 0x381B8..0x381F8 -- and finally, only when
g_pTitlesState @ 0x158804 is non-null (0x382AC), Titles_dtor (0x382B4) followed by a delete of the
0x154C0 state block itself (0x382BC). **Nothing is nulled afterwards**: 0x1571A0..0x1571B0 and
g_pTitlesState keep pointing at freed memory, so a second shutdown frees them again.

Titles_dtor (60 B) writes Map_nUiScreen (Map+0x3A) with **22** (0x46FB0) -- not the 16 the credits
screen ran under -- unconditionally, and only then, when g_pTitlesSurface @ 0x158808 is non-null
(0x46FC0), runs SoftSurf_dtor (0x46FC8) and the delete (0x46FD0). The 22 is never seen on screen:
Titles_Shutdown's caller runs GameUI_InitStartup straight after, which writes 17.

EndScreen_Shutdown (48 B): Sound_Shutdown (0x389FC), KillTimers_A (0x38A00), Font_Free (0x38A08), an
UNGUARDED operator delete of the ending backdrop at 0x1571C0 (0x38A0C..0x38A14), and a **tail call**
into GameUI_InitStartup @ 0x38a28 (0x38A20). The ending does not exit -- it goes back to the start
menu, and that call re-loads the font the shutdown just freed, which is why Font_Free is not the last
word on fontSys.

A shipped-data finding fell out of the test fixture: EndScreen_Init @ 0x38920 asks the archive for the
"z" sample set, but main.dat carries no Z*.WAV at all -- only TACT0..N.WAV and BACK0..4.IT -- so the
scan stops at index 0 and every ending loads zero samples.

Deviation: the port frees through the same owner Titles_Init / EndScreen_Init allocated with (malloc)
and nulls every pointer it releases, which the original does not; it bounds the glyph array and the
screen-id pointer instead of dereferencing them blindly; and the original's delete of the 0x154C0 state
block has no counterpart because the port keeps that block in the shell's static storage. The shell now
wires the screen-16 arm for real (App_TitlesToStartup: Titles_Shutdown then App_InitStartupUi); the
screen-18 arm stays a seam because the shell has no ending flow yet.

Tests: 26 new checks in test_titles (136 there). Sound_Shutdown's presence is pinned through the fake
audio backend's sample-free and music-free counters after a real Sound_InitAndLoadSamples("tact") and
Sound_LoadAndPlayMusic; the timers through the timer backend's kill log (two kills, 0xC351 then
0xC352); Font_Free through the font's sprite index going null; the glyph blobs through all five
pointers; the state gate by showing that a null state block leaves both the screen id and the surface
untouched; Titles_dtor's unconditional screen-id write by running it with no surface at all; and the
tail call by showing the start menu comes up at 17 with a startup env and stays at 18 without one.

A 14-mutation sweep turned 12 red (the 22, four-not-five blobs, both KillTimers_* swapped to D, the
state gate, both Sound_Shutdown calls, both Font_Free calls, both dangling-pointer fixes, the tail
call). Two are true equivalences and are not counted: KillTimers_A/B/C are byte-identical in the
binary (0x9e6a4 / 0x9e754 / 0x9e7c4), so swapping A or C for B kills the same two ids.

IDB: 3 function comments (0x3826c, 0x46fa4, 0x389f8) and 7 line comments (0x38280, 0x382AC, 0x46FB0,
0x46FC0, 0x38A14, 0x38A20, 0x38920), no renames. Three new ledger rows (261): the dangling glyph blobs
and state block, the unguarded backdrop delete, and the ending's empty sample set.

## Unit 101 - the soldier readout and its two armour panels (SoldierScreen_DrawDetail
@ 0x632cc, 6,096 B; SoldierScreen_DrawEquipPanels @ 0x62d78, 960 B)

The two functions behind SCREEN 5, 7,056 bytes, the biggest pair left in the strat-ui
cluster. Coverage moves to 549,876 / 598,792 code bytes (91.8 %).

The IDB called 0x632cc Ui_TextInputDialog. That name describes only the keyboard block
in the function's last ~1,100 bytes; the body is the whole selected-soldier readout -
header, rank icon, class insignia, armour, the record block, nine stat bars, the two
armour panels and the transfer panels. The port names it SoldierScreen_DrawDetail and
the IDB follows.

SoldierScreen_DrawEquipPanels (0x62d78) draws the pair of panels on the right of the
readout. The row count comes from nEquipRowCount @ 0xab710, which the function resets
to 1 at 0x62DB8 and then raises once per armour object that has stock in the selected
base: apObjects[122..124] (the IDB globals Map_apObjects122/123/124 at 0x113CA8 /
0x113CAC / 0x113CB0), whose auPerBaseVal[nSelectedBaseIdx] it caches into
nSolStockArmour1/2/3 at 0x159D84 / 0x159D88 / 0x159D8C. Row 0 is TEXTS[93] "None" on
the equip panel and the shared empty string at 0x10DA38 on the stores panel; rows 1..3
carry the armour caption (TEXTS 94/95/96) and the quantity, and each row records its
armour index + 1 in the panel's aux slot, which is what EquipSelected (0x62f98)
switches on. The frame is three nested rects - (45,75) 170 x (18*rows+29) in
0x6E/0x77, (46,76) 168 x (18*rows+27) in 0x30/0xE0/0xE8, (47,77) 166 x (18*rows+25) -
and the height multiplies the SIGNED BYTE of the row count, so the original would wrap
past 14 rows; the shipped data never gets there.

SoldierScreen_DrawDetail (0x632cc) opens by storing the cursor into
nSoldierDetailCursor @ 0x159760 (0x632F4) before any bounds check, then draws: a
24-step header ramp in two halves with 1x27 edges at x 3 and 235; the rank name and
rank icon at bRankType + g_fontSys.nBaseBitsBase + 42; the class insignia as a pair of
basebits pads at x 33 and 67, y 2, chosen by a six-entry table keyed on nClass (0/0,
1/1, 2/2, 0/1, 1/2, 0/2) and only for a soldier with more than 3 missions; the armour
row, gated on nUnitType <= 3 so aliens have no armour; the record block - a 10-step
ramp falling 0xB4-8*k, then Craft / Missions / Kills / Time and Wound Recovery only
when bUnk183 == 254; nine stat bars whose labels are TEXTS 127..136; the panel frame
ramps at y 134..310 step 22 with side rails at x 5 and 232, y 58..204 step 6; the two
transfer panels behind the bTransferFlag byte; and the name-edit keyboard - a 16x16
grid of characters from 32, 13 tall and 14 wide from (12,80), opened through
Ui_AnimExpandBlit(0, 70, 236, 250, 4, 0x46, 0x4B, 0xC8, 3), with the BackSpace and
Accept pads and the three plain .data captions.

The stat-bar labels are the second independent statement of what auStat[] holds (the
first is Unit 74's training screen), so the port now has a SoldierStat enum in
pufo_unit.h naming all ten slots. Separately reported, not fixed: pufo_ballist.h calls
auStat[8] nStatThrow and auStat[9] nStatStrength, which contradicts those captions.

Deviation: the original writes the panel rows and only then stores the row count into
the panel, while the port goes through UiPanel_SetLineText, which also bounds by
nLineCount - so the port stores nLineCount before the rows instead of after them. The
two orders differ only for a row index beyond the panel's line count, and the port
allocates 8 lines for a maximum of 4 rows. The stock capture's != 0 and the row
emission's > 0 can only differ for a negative quantity, and auPerBaseVal is a u16, so
in the shipped data they always agree. Two further deviations are the original's own:
bCraftType 3 and 4 read a 140-byte buffer that this function never fills (the port
names the default TEXTS[93] "None" and the buffer is in the ledger), and the function
returns 1 from its keyboard tail; the port's Text_DrawString is void, so the port
returns 1 directly.

Tests: 111 new checks in test_baseui (3,808 in that suite, 15,547 across all suites,
no failures). Phase A runs with the font freed so every assertion is a rect blit with
an exact 565 value - the three frame rects and their row-count-dependent heights, the
header ramp's left/right overpaint boundary at x 122, the insignia pads' own origins,
the bar widths from the auStat values, the side rails' contiguous tiling, the transfer
gate, the keyboard gate on animation progress, the pad blit order, and the space-key
box colour switch. Phase B loads the real font from lang.dat/main.dat and checks ink
bands: the rank icon and name band, the armour row present for type 1 and absent for
type 5, Wound Recovery present for 254 and absent for 255, and the keyboard's first
and last grid rows. The last two assert the exact glyph colour the pair writes, not
mere ink presence, because Ui_AnimExpandBlit blends every pixel inside the keyboard
region and "some ink there" proves nothing.

Mutations: 22 caught, 2 recorded equivalences (the u16 != 0 versus > 0 capture, and
the armour gate widened to <= 255, which only changes behaviour for a unit type the
array cannot hold and indexes the label table out of bounds).

IDB: 1 function rename (Ui_TextInputDialog -> SoldierScreen_DrawDetail), 13 global
renames (nSoldierDetailCursor, nNameEditChar, bNameEditActive, pszItoaScratch,
pCtlNameEditBackspace, pCtlNameEditAccept, nSolStockArmour1/2/3, pPadCs0/1/2,
szEmptyString, aTextRec94/95/96), pSolPanelEquip typed UiPanel *, 18 comments
(function comments at 0x632cc and 0x62d78, line comments at 0x632F4, 0x6348C, 0x63490,
0x636C0, 0x6391C, 0x63A30, 0x64218, 0x64420, 0x64678, 0x646E0, 0x647F0, 0x649A4,
0x64A40, 0x62E50, 0x62E8C, 0x63040, plus the pPadCs0 block comment). Two of those
renames fix earlier mistakes rather than name new findings: 0x10DA38 was called
szBaseAtResultOk although UiPanel_ctor copies it into every line buffer (0x3E774) and
none of its 72 reads has a writer, and 0x186C30/34/38 were apPadCs/apPadCs1/apPadCs2
with no type. The audit_names gate went from 2 unresolved citations to 0. Five new
ledger rows (266): the uninitialised craft-name buffer, the unchecked soldier/craft
index, the reused transfer flag, the dead colour pair at 0x64420, and the empty stores
label at 0x10DA38.

## Unit 102 - the tactical sprite loader and the font's group bases
(Font_LoadTactSprites @ 0x257c4, 752 B)

Coverage moves to 952 / 1103 functions (86.2 -> 86.3 %) and 550,628 / 598,792 bytes
(92.0 %).

Font_LoadTactSprites is the only writer of the per-group sprite bases in the font
block at 0x158268, and the rule is uniform: each base is the running counter captured
immediately BEFORE that group's Font_LoadSpr, so it is the group's first frame index.
The counter is fontSys.nTotalSprFrames (+0x36) for the .spr groups and
fontSys.nTotalMc1 (+0x38) for the two slots the .ma1 templates index as fontSys + 2 *
nFlag with flags 2 and 3. Reached from Map_BuildMissionTerrain (0x22e10) at 0x22E4C
and from Save_ReadTGameData (0x44248) at 0x4444C.

The load order is not the slot order. Tanks, floorob, handob and bigobs load in that
sequence while their slots are +0x24, +0x22, +0x20 and +0x26; and urban missions load
"civm" (aXcom0 slot 17) before "civf" (slot 16), so the higher slot loads first. The
mission-terrain group takes four names from aTactTerrainSetName @ 0xA6858 (40 names of
9 = 10 mission types x 4 sets, 360 bytes ending exactly at aTactUfoSetName), the UFO
group takes four from aTactUfoSetName @ 0xA69C0 (32 names = 8 classes x 4, ending
exactly at abTactUfoClassByVariant), and the class comes from abTactUfoClassByVariant
@ 0xA6AE0 indexed 3 * (nTerrainVariant - 1) + nTerrainParam -- 16 bytes, of which only
15 are reachable, the last being the gap to g_aTerrainModuleCount. All three are read
by no other function in the binary. The craft name is aPlane[nMapLayers - 1], which is
the layer count and not the mission type the terrain builder uses for the same table.

The mc1 running total is captured once at 0x25804 and then carried: the terrain base
stored at +0x04 is that first value, the craft base at +0x06 is what the terrain loop
left, and the UFO base at +0x08 is what the craft load left. The terrain loop re-reads
the counter after every load that actually ran (0x2584C); the UFO loop does not, so
+0x08 is the value from before the UFO sets.

A defect in this port, found and fixed here. Font_GetFlagSprBase read `((const u16
*)pFont)[nFlag]`, which mirrors the original's `*(u16 *)(fontSys + 2 * nFlag)` only if
the port's PufoFont were laid out at the original offsets -- it is not, it is a model.
In the model the first five u16s are {bInited, nSlotCount} followed by
anAlienSprBase[0..3], so flags 2, 3 and 4 were really reading the alien sprite-set
bases. tests/test_terrain.c had been written around it: its fixture primed
anAlienSprBase[0..2] to make template lookups miss. PufoFont now names the five slots
as anFlagSprBase[5] (blanks, cursor, terrain, craft, UFO), the accessor reads them by
name and returns 0 for a flag the shipped templates never produce, and the terrain
fixture primes anFlagSprBase[2..4]. The alien bases keep their own field.

The seam stayed a seam. Map_BuildMissionTerrain and Save_ReadTGameData still call this
through pfnLoadTactSprites rather than calling it directly, because the load ends with
Font_BuildIndex, which frees and rebuilds the very index the terrain builder's
template and stamping passes then read. A caller that owns neither the font nor its
index cannot have the builder rebuild it underneath them -- test_terrain's font
fixture is exactly that caller. The app, which owns the real fontSys, installs
Font_LoadTactSprites(pFont, &env) built from the env's own Map scalars.

Deviation: the original indexes aTactTerrainSetName with 4 * nMissionType and
abTactUfoClassByVariant with 3 * (nTerrainVariant - 1) + nTerrainParam with no bound
at all, so a mission type above 9 or a variant above 5 reads past the end of the
table. The port bounds both and skips the group instead.

Tests: 34 new checks in test_font (66 there, 15,581 across all 60 suites). The fixture
presets nTotalSprFrames = 11 and nTotalMc1 = 7 so the two running totals are
distinguishable -- a group base that takes the wrong counter shows up as 11 where 7
was wanted. The assertions name the 19 shipped sets a culta mission loads, in order,
and every base as an exact frame count read from the archives (cursor 13, terrain 9,
craft 75, UFO 121, font 177, xcom_0..3 433 / 708 / 983 / 1266, tanks 1549, floorob
1677, handob 1750, bigobs 1878, bullets 1935, scang 1956, smoke 2410, expl 2470), plus
the urban 25-set list, the no-layers / no-variant skips, the aPlane[2] pick at three
layers, and the two out-of-range cases. A 12-mutation sweep turned all 12 red.

IDB: 12 renames (aJungle_0 -> aTactTerrainSetName, aUfo1 -> aTactUfoSetName,
byte_A6AE0 -> abTactUfoClassByVariant, and the nine unnamed fontSys base slots
fontSys_nCursorSprBase, fontSys_nTerrainSprBase, fontSys_nUfoSprBase,
fontSys_nXcom0..3SprBase, fontSys_nCivmSprBase, fontSys_nCivfSprBase), a function
comment on 0x257c4 and line comments at 0x2582C, 0x258F0, 0x2598C plus data comments
on the three tables. Three new audited tables (43 checked, 0 mismatched), dumped by
tools/gen_tact_sprite_tables.py.

## Unit 103 - the startup entry and the forcenodrag option
(Map_InitAndLoadRegistry @ 0x22648, 1,284 B)

Coverage moves to 953 / 1103 functions (86.3 -> 86.4 %) and 551,912 / 598,792 bytes (92.2 %).

The Map subsystem's startup entry is a CRT init-term record: the thunk at 0x22604 runs
Map_InitAndLoadRegistry and then tail-calls Map_RegisterAtexit. It has two halves.

0x22664..0x226C8 clears the tactical scratch and writes two constants. In the ARM's order:
Map+0x15110 (the deploy panel), +0xC4, +0x7C, +0x150E8 (anActionPhaseSave0[112]), +0x68 low
byte, +0x150F0 (pThrowTargetUnit), +0x37, +0x5C, +0x6C, +0x74..0x77 (the four edge bytes of
apUiSlotsA[5]) and +0x80 low byte all go to zero; +0xC8 takes Game_RandU16(3) and +0x70 takes
200. Slot numbering is (offset - 0x60) / 4, so +0xC4 is slot 25 and +0xC8 slot 26. Nothing
writes +0x64 -- an early draft of the port claimed slot 1, and the sentinel fixture caught it.

0x226CC..0x22AFC reads the twelve registry values. Numerics are atoi'd -- the original re-reads
the same buffer twice or three times -- against an inclusive range whose out-of-range fallback
is a constant rather than the caller's default: gamespeed 0..4 else 4, gamma 0..4 else 2,
soundvolume 1..5 else 5, musicvolume 1..5 else 5. The volume range EXCLUDES 0. Flags are
strcmp(value, "0") != 0, so any text other than "0" sets them, an empty string included; the
Reg_GetString default is "1" for menubypen, runbydblclick, scrollbypen and showborder and "0"
for musicoff, soundoff, forcenodrag and turnbypen. The port's Options_LoadFromRegistry had been
reading the flags through atoi, which disagrees on exactly those two cases; it now uses the
string test with the original's literal default strings.

The naming fix this function proves. The byte at Map+0x150E4 was Map_bInvPanelOpen in the IDB
and bInvPanelOpen in the port -- a name for what the inventory code does with it, not for what
it is. The registry name is "forcenodrag" (written by Options_SaveToRegistry @ 0x115C4, read
back at 0x22928), the options screen lights widget 88 from its INVERSE
(Options_SyncUiFromMap_GotoScreen12 @ 0x18A18), and Menu_ToggleForceNoDrag @ 0x19d94 is that
widget's click handler. In play it picks the transfer style: set means the 13 controls are press
hit-tested and a press while an item is held places it (Inv_ClearHitSlot + Inv_HandlePointer at
0x146A8, then the held byte clears); clear means a drag. TactHud_DrawInventoryScreen highlights
the hit region when it is set and draws the carried-item ghost when it is clear. It is
Map_bForceNoDrag in the IDB and bForceNoDrag in the port.

A second naming defect, found in the same reading: TactHudInventoryEnv carried the two bytes
under swapped names -- nDragActive held Map+0x150E4 and bInvPanelOpen held byte_1139F4 @
Map+0x3C. The code read them the right way round; only the names were wrong. They are now
bForceNoDrag and bItemHeld. Fixing them exposed three vacuous checks in test_tacthud: the
"no highlight" probes sat at x 98 while the leftover nHitSub0 of 1 would have painted region 0
at x 60. They are pinned to sub-column 2 now, and the mutation that had been missed is caught.

Also renamed in the IDB: unk_128AB4 -> Map_nGameSpeed (Map+0x150FC, the dword GameClock.nSpeed
already cites), unk_AD1DA -> bCtl88ForceNoDrag (pBank widget 88's nState byte, the port's
MenuPads.bForceNoDrag), and TactHud_ToggleFlag128A9C -> Menu_ToggleForceNoDrag, the name
renames.tsv already recorded for the port. docs/idb/functions.tsv and the regenerated
inventory-grouped.tsv follow the rename, and the name-based grouping moves 0x19d94 from tact-ui
to strat-ui -- the options screen is strategic UI, where its neighbours already sit.

Deviation: the original writes all fourteen scratch slots through the context base. The port
writes through MapInitEnv members and skips the ones the caller passes as NULL -- the shell runs
no tactical mission, so it owns neither the battle-ended byte nor the throw-target slot, and
clearing a field of a block that does not exist has no counterpart. test_boot drives the full
non-NULL set.

Tests: 24 new checks in test_boot (62 there) and 2 in test_audio (55 there), 15,610 across all
60 suites. The scratch fixture starts every field at 0x5A / 0x5A5A5A5A so a write that lands in
the wrong slot, or a constant read from the wrong one, fails; the roll is sampled 64 times so a
wider or narrower Game_RandU16 argument and a roll written into slot 25 both show up; and the
flag cases use "yes", "" and a 299-byte value -- the last one rejected by Reg_GetString, which
is what makes the per-flag default strings observable. A 14-mutation sweep turned all 14 red.

IDB: 4 renames (Map_bInvPanelOpen -> Map_bForceNoDrag, TactHud_ToggleFlag128A9C ->
Menu_ToggleForceNoDrag, unk_AD1DA -> bCtl88ForceNoDrag, unk_128AB4 -> Map_nGameSpeed), a
function comment on 0x22648, data comments on 0x128A9C, 0xAD1DA and 0x128AB4, a function comment
on 0x19d94 and a correction appended to the TactHud_DrawInventoryScreen comment at 0x1f58c.
## Unit 104 - the ufopaedia bring-up and its reselect (Ui_InitBaseInfo @ 0x9ddc8, 744 B)

Ui_InitBaseInfo is the tail of both base-info openers. Ui_OpenBaseInfo POPs and branches to it at
0x84BD4, Ui_OpenBaseInfoAlt at 0x84DF8, and both hand in g_pUfopaediaScreenPad @ 0x1872E0: a
UiControl* array shared with the ufopaedia. Slot 0 is the screen's own pad, slot 1 is the current
entry's pad (g_pUfopaediaPad @ 0x1872E4, owned by Ufopaedia_RefreshEntry), and slots 2..7 are the
six controls at 0x1872E8..0x1872FC that Ufopaedia_Open's teardown releases. The port wires its
UfopaediaEnv to those same eight slots, so the pad this function allocates is the pad the teardown
frees, and the test asserts that pair rather than trusting the comment.

The bring-up half is wiring. new(0x14) + PadImage_ctor into slot 0, PadImage_Load("baseinfo", 14),
then the two origins cleared at 0x9DE0C / 0x9DE14 -- the same PadImage +0/+4 pair the research
bring-up writes at 0x749EC. Six new(0x20) + UiControl_ctor stored at ppRoot + 8 stepping by 4, so
they land in slots 2..7 and slot 1 is skipped; the fixture starts slot 1 at NULL and asserts it
stays NULL. Their handlers in slot order: UiPanel_ScrollPrev (0x99f88) and UiPanel_ScrollNext
(0x99f78) on the text panel, Ufopaedia_PrevEntry (0x9a60c) and Ufopaedia_NextEntry (0x9a754), then
UiPanel_ScrollPrevSel (0x99fb4) and UiPanel_ScrollNextSel (0x99f98) on the category panel of
g_nUfopaediaCategory. Then UiControl_Setup(slot 2+i, 0, 0, aUiBaseInfoCtlDesc[i]): the ARM walks
the slots with ADD R4,R4,#4 and the descriptors with ADD R5,R5,#0x20, so each control gets its own
record, and the six records at 0xAC548 put them at (142,210), (172,210), (10,210), (40,210),
(200,18) and (200,38), all mode 0 with the third pad name empty. Then the shared close control
g_pUiCloseCtl to (224,1) with Geoscape_CloseUI_ThunkC, and Ufopaedia_Open builds the nine category
panels, the selector and the text panel.

The reselect half is what byte_18706C is for, and it runs only when that flag is set -- which is
exactly what Ui_OpenBaseInfoAlt does on the way in. First a 25-case switch on
nResearchTopicShown - 0x76 (0x9DF18): the jump table repeats five targets every five cases, so the
25 alien-encounter topics fold onto the five race topics by residue, with two exceptions the table
makes explicit -- cases 17 and 22, topics 135 and 140, go to the default arm and keep their topic.
They are the same two Muton encounters g_anRaceKnownTopics omits, so the ufopaedia and the research
screen agree about Muton's incomplete family. Topics below 118 fall out too: SUB / CMP / ADDLS is an
unsigned test. Then a linear walk of aUfopaediaCatTopics, 22 cells per category and 198 cells in
all, comparing with LDRB against the full dword, so a topic above 255 matches nothing rather than
wrapping onto a zero cell -- and zeros are ordinary cells, so topic 0 lands on row 0's first
terminator. Finally the writes: category (a STRB of the sign-extended counter), pad dirty = 1, entry
dirty = 0, entry index, entry number = anUfopaediaEntryNum[topic], topic, bUfopaediaOpen @ 0x18730C
= 1, Ufopaedia_RefreshEntry, and the pending flag cleared. 0x18730C is a different byte from the
0x187308 toggle Ufopaedia_Open runs on; the port keeps them apart.

An original bug fell out of the walk. Five research topics -- 47, 94, 95, 96 and 143 -- are in no
category row, and 135 and 140 reach the same state through the default arm. The walk breaks out with
the category counter at 9 and the index at 22, and 0x9E054 then reads aUfopaediaCatTopics[9][22],
the byte at 0xAA90C, which belongs to the table that follows. It is 0x0A, so the ufopaedia opens on
topic 10 / entry 1006 with category 9 and entry index 22. The port keeps the same counters and names
that byte as PUFO_UFOPAEDIA_MISS_TOPIC instead of reading out of bounds; the observable outcome is
identical. Listed in docs/parity/bugs.tsv.

Deviation: the original allocates the pad and the six controls with operator new and derefs every
allocation with no test. The port takes caller-owned controls, as the research, manufacturing,
buy/sell and transfer inits do, and keeps the pad port-allocated because Ufopaedia_Open's teardown
releases exactly that slot. The reselect half also needs the topic the research screen last showed;
a caller that passes no pointer for it gets the build half only.

Two stale comments went with the reading. The header called the research tail "ResearchScreen_Init
(0x615d0, not ported)" -- 0x615d0 is NewBaseScreen_Open, the tail call is B ResearchScreen_Init at
0x61778, and ResearchScreen_Init @ 0x749a8 has been ported since part 43. The four tail-call
addresses in the port's comments (0x61778, 0x84BD4, 0x84DF8, 0x84CF0) now match the ARM, and
g_pUfopaediaScreenPad is the IDB's own name for 0x1872E0.

Tests: 222 new checks in test_baseui (4030 there), 15,832 across all 60 suites. The fixture wires
the ufopaedia env to the eight-slot block and runs the real Ufopaedia_Open and Ufopaedia_RefreshEntry
against the shipped archives, so baseinfo.pad, the eight control pad names and the entry pads are all
read out of main.dat. Twenty reselect cases are pinned with literals measured off the two tables:
category, row, topic and entry number, including the four miss cases and the Sectoid family 118 /
123 / 128 / 133 / 138 all reaching entry 54. A 25-mutation sweep turned all 25 red.

One test-quality defect surfaced while doing that sweep. The first version compared each control's
pfnClick against the stub it should hold, and swapping two handlers stayed green: the linker folds
identical empty functions into one address, so a pointer comparison between two empty stubs can never
fail. The checks now CALL the installed handler and read back an id each stub records. The same
pattern already sits in the research, manufacturing and psi fixtures, where the seam stubs are empty
too; recorded as a separate issue.

IDB: stru_AC548 renamed to aUiBaseInfoCtlDesc with a data comment, a function comment on 0x9ddc8
covering the seven steps, and a comment on 0x9E054 naming the out-of-bounds read.
## Unit 105 - the small CRT and app wrappers (Font_Init_ReturnArg @ 0x46130, Font_RegisterAtexit @ 0x460d0, j_Font_Free @ 0x460dc, Bank_RegisterAtexit @ 0x11164, Bank_AtexitThunk @ 0x11170, DatFile_RegisterAtexit @ 0x3f0d0, Render_Frame_DecRef @ 0x36818, UiModal_EndThunk @ 0x12254, App_QuitFromTact @ 0x18e18, ??1CDialogTemplate@@QAA@XZ @ 0x54c48)

Unit 105 ports the last small wrappers that sit between the CRT init-term table and the
ported subsystems, plus the two app-side glue functions. Every one was re-read from the ARM
before it was written.

Font_Init_ReturnArg @ 0x46130 is `Font_Init(pFont); return pFont;` -- the font subsystem's
init entry, reached through the init-term thunk at 0x460c4, which discards the result. The port
takes the block as an argument because the port's font block is caller-owned. Test: a block
filled with 0xA5 comes back the same and cleared.

Font_RegisterAtexit @ 0x460d0 is `return atexit(j_Font_Free);`. j_Font_Free @ 0x460dc is two
instructions: `LDR R0, =fontSys` then `B Font_Free` -- a tail jump that names the global. The
port's font block is a global too (g_fontSys), so Font_AtexitThunk names it exactly as the
original does. The test plants live allocations in g_fontSys, runs the thunk, and checks every
one is released and bInited cleared; a second run is idempotent, which matters because the
registered entry runs the same thunk once more at process exit.

Bank_RegisterAtexit @ 0x11164 is `return atexit(Bank_AtexitThunk);`; Bank_AtexitThunk @ 0x11170
is `UiBank_FreeAllPads(&pBank)` on the global bank at 0xAC6D0. The port's bank is caller-owned,
so the registrar takes it and the thunk releases that one -- the same shape as
StrategList_RegisterAtexit. The test plants pads on the first and the last widget of the bank
(the thunk walks all fourteen groups in reverse) and checks both ends come loose.

DatFile_RegisterAtexit @ 0x3f0d0 is `return atexit(j_DatFile_dtor);`, and that thunk is
`DatFile_dtor(&unk_158220)` -- the dtor of the global container the save driver opens its slots
on. The port's containers are caller-owned, so the registrar takes the container. The test opens
a real CREATE-mode container, registers it, runs the thunk, and checks nMode becomes CLOSED,
the write buffer is released, and bChunkOpen is cleared.

Render_Frame_DecRef @ 0x36818 is five instructions: `LDR R3,[R0,#0x64]; SUB R3,#1;
STR R3,[R0,#0x64]; LDR R0,=&gIsoDraw; B Render_Frame`. Map+0x64 is dword_113A1C =
apUiSlotsA[1], the banner-fade tick count that Tact_EndMission @ 0x351FC seeds with 10. The only
caller is the PocketUFO_WndProc timer 0xC352 arm at 0xA09AC, taken while Map_nBannerFadeTicks > 0
and nUiScreen == 13. IDB correction: the prototype carried three int arguments; it takes one,
the Map context in R0 -- set to `void __fastcall Render_Frame_DecRef(int pMapCtx)` and the
decompiler now shows `--*(_DWORD *)(pMapCtx + 100)`. Deviation: the port hands the counter
pointer directly and guards it; the original always has the Map context. The test pins the
order at the boundary: with counter 1 the decrement must land before the frame, so the frame
takes the fade-in branch (nothing drawn on a white surface) and not the dark-blit branch --
counter 10 -> 9 alone could not tell the two orders apart.

UiModal_EndThunk @ 0x12254 is a tail call to UiModal_End @ 0x2648c, stored as the modal-end
callback in the eighteen modal tables Inv_HandlePointer dispatches. Deviation: the original
thunk is zero-argument because UiModal_End reads the modal fields out of the global context;
the port's modal state is caller-owned, so the thunk takes the state pointer. The test re-opens
the modal before ending it through the thunk, so the flag actually has to change.

App_QuitFromTact @ 0x18e18 is the YES callback of the quit dialog: `Tact_Shutdown(1)` at 0x18E20,
then `App_QuitDisplay()` at 0x18E28. Ported in pufo_menubtn.c next to Menu_OpenQuitDialog and
Menu_CancelQuitDialog, the other two members of the trio, with both halves injected because the
shutdown env and the display teardown are app state. The app wires it to the screen-8 escape
seam (TactInputHooks.pfnShutdownQuit). Deviation: the shell never runs a tactical mission, so
its shutdown half reaches Tact_Shutdown with no mission env -- the NULL guard makes the call a
no-op; the original's Tact_Shutdown(1) works on the global mission context, which only exists
during a mission. The test pins the order (shutdown, then display), the bKeepSome value 1, and
that a missing half is skipped.

??1CDialogTemplate@@QAA@XZ @ 0x54c48 is the template dtor, `if (pTemplate)
operator delete(pTemplate)`, called four times from Map_BuildMissionTerrain. MapTemplate_Free is
its port counterpart: the port's template struct is caller-owned, so the heap part the dtor
releases is the blob, not the struct. renames.tsv records the pair.

Dispositions, not ported, with reasons. App_ResizeMainWindow @ 0x9ecb8 is pure Win32 glue:
`SetWindowPos(hWndMain, HWND_BOTTOM, 0, 0, w, h, SWP_HIDEWINDOW)` with the size read from the
two globals only InitInstance writes; its only caller is MenuBtn_ResizeWindow, ported as
Menu_ResizeWindow with the resize injected, and the shell never installs that options-screen
button. Map_RegisterAtexit (0x22620) and its thunk Map_Atexit_nullsub2 (0x2262c) register a
wrapper over nullsub_2, an empty stub, so they carry no behaviour -- the same disposition as the
BaseGrid atexit trio (0x614a8, 0x614b4, 0x614c0), already recorded in pufo_baseui.h.

Test-harness defect found and fixed. test_renderframe's CheckEqI32 printed FAIL but never
incremented g_nFailures, so the suite could never exit non-zero: the first unit-105 mutation
sweep missed three counter/order mutants for that reason alone. The counter is now incremented.
The same class of hole existed in five bail-out guards (four in test_baseui.c, one in
test_geoscape.c) that printed FAIL and returned without counting; they now count. The
test_enemyai.c Ai_Rand guard prints FAIL and exits(2), which is already caught. After the fix
the sweep is 16 patterns, 16 caught.

Coverage after unit 105: 964 / 1103 functions (87.4%), 552,812 / 598,792 bytes (92.3%). The
remaining non-platform gaps are Geoscape_Draw @ 0x8c180 (33,744 B), Ui_DrawBaseInfo @ 0x9b5f4
(10,196 B), App_ResizeMainWindow @ 0x9ecb8 (84 B) and the five no-op atexit registrars (60 B),
all with dispositions recorded here or in the headers.
## Unit 106 - the ufopaedia entry draw (Ui_DrawBaseInfo @ 0x9b5f4, 10,196 B)

Unit 106 ports the screen that shows one ufopaedia entry: the entry pad, the dashed
waiting frame, the five category layouts and the four numeric layouts. Every arm was read
from the ARM listing (the Hex-Rays output for a function this size is not trustworthy), and
the port carries an address comment on every instruction it reproduces.

Four layers, in the order the ARM has them. (1) The screen pad ppScreenPad[0] is blitted
first, always. (2) When the entry is NOT dirty a dashed frame is drawn instead of the entry:
24 vertical 1x7 dashes at x 5 and 234 and 24 horizontal 5x1 dashes at y 5 and 315. (3) The
close control is blitted, then three gates in order: screen not built -> return; ufopaedia
not open -> draw the selector panel and return; entry not dirty -> the category-panel gate
(draw the selector panel when the current category panel has lines, else return). (4) Entry
dirty: BlitSrcRect(0,0,240,320, idx 0x64, mid 0x64, low 0xC8, key 0x50) fills the screen, a
solid 5 px frame is drawn, the entry number is normalised, and a dispatch draws the entry.

The dashed frame ramps on the ITERATION, not on the coordinate. 0x9B660 computes
((i + 20) * 5) for the near pair and 0x9B754 computes (230 - 5*i) / (250 - 5*i) for the far
pair, with i the loop counter of a y += 7 / x += 5 walk. The first draft used the coordinate
(0xE6 - y*5, 0xFA - x*5), which agrees for the first dash and diverges after it; the test
pins the ramp values and the overlap point where the falling pair first survives the
climbing pair (row 172 of 215).

Normalisation (0x9B8C8..0x9B964) rewrites *pnEntryNum and writes *pnSub: 54..75 -> category
3; > 0xBB7 -> category 2 with sub = n - 3000; 1001..1999 -> category 1 with sub = n - 1000;
2001..2999 -> category 26; 76..84 -> category 4. 0xBB7 is 2999 and 0xBB8 is 3000, so entry
3000 itself is category 2 with sub 0, and 2000 / 1000 / 76 / 85 / 53 / 76 are the boundary
cases the test walks (15 inputs).

Record indices. The entry blocks read TEXTS records by their literal address; the index is
(literal - 0xB38D0) / 205. The port names them: 1270..1275 headings, 1276/1277/1278 the ammo
row labels, 1279..1284 the six fire-mode labels, 1285..1287 the three stat-row labels,
1288..1291 craft labels, 1292..1296 race names, 1297..1300 and 1335..1338 the stat/number
line labels, 1357 the build-days tail, 1358 the recovery tail, 1715..1720 the six panel rows.

The fire-row chain REPLACES the string. Each mode arm ends in an inline strcpy loop over a
REPLACE chain (topic 5, 3, 4 for mode 1; topic 5, 0xC, 0xD, 3, 4 for mode 2), so a later arm
overwrites the earlier label instead of appending to it. Only the BL strcat sites append, and
they are exactly the four suffixes the port writes: "$", "%", " %" and " s" plus the itoa
result. Modes outside 0..5 keep whatever the previous arm left.

Scratch copies. 0x9C704 copies 0xD0 bytes of the object record into 0x187100 and 0x9C8FC
copies into 0x187208; the two blocks tile 0x187100..0x1872D8 exactly (the next symbol is
g_nUfopaediaEntryNum @ 0x1872D8) and both have only this function's xrefs (2 and 5). The port
keeps them as locals named item and ammo. Deviation recorded: locals instead of globals.
Deviation recorded: the original indexes apObjects[sub] / aBaseFacFlags[sub] / aFacBuildSpec
without a bound test; the port checks nObjectCount and the array sizes first.

IDB updates. Prototype set to void __fastcall Ui_DrawBaseInfo(PadImage **ppScreenPad) and the
evidence comment appended. Renames: dword_1872DC -> g_nUfopaediaEntrySub; unk_187208 ->
g_abUfopaediaAmmoScratch; unk_186B00 -> g_pUiCloseCtl. The last one is a correction of an
earlier guess: the xref list shows the same control slot re-armed by BaseInfoScreen_Init,
BaseFacScreen_*, FundingScreen_*, NewBaseScreen_Open, BasePlaneScreen_Open, the Transfer
screens and the ufopaedia, so it is the shared close control, not a ufopaedia one. New data
symbols g_abUfopaediaItemScratch @ 0x187100 and g_abUfopaediaAmmoScratch @ 0x187208, both
unsigned char[208]. The 37 comments in the port that cited the old names were updated in the
same unit (pufo_baseui.h, pufo_baseui.c, pufo_world.h, pufo_plane.h) and the 13 citations in
this file.

Tests. TestUiDrawBaseInfo drives the real draw into a 240x320 PIXMODE_16BPP surface and
asserts pixels, not call counts: the fill value 6375, the frame rails at their middle
(120,319)/(120,314) and (239,160)/(234,160), the dash ramp values, the gate behaviour (fill
absent before the dirty gate, close control blitted once before the gates and twice after),
the pad originY each category pins (facility untouched, alien 96, craft 77, stat 25, number
50), the glyph palette bases 3 and 0x22, the six panel row strings, and the item strip pinned
at x 46 (51 is the divider's own column). test_baseui is at 4,138 checks.

Mutation sweep, reduced to the values that carry behaviour: 27 patterns (the seven
normalisation boundaries and both sub bases, the dashed loop bound and both ramps, the fill
mid/low swap, the frame 0x13B and 0xEB edges, the built gate reading the wrong byte, the
facility/stat/number/alien pad Y pins, both glyph palette bases, the panel row value swap,
PANEL_1's record index, the three rail widths) - 27 caught, 0 survived. Two first-run
survivors were test weaknesses, not port bugs: a falling-pair overlap assertion that sat on a
row the climbing pair already covered, and an item-strip assertion at x 51 behind the
divider. Two mutants were dropped as equivalent before the run: 0x34 -> 0x33 (the divider
covers columns 47..51 either way) and a weapon/alien swap that makes a static function unused
under -Werror.

Coverage after unit 106: 965 / 1103 functions (87.5%), 563,008 / 598,792 bytes (94.0%). The
only remaining non-platform gap is Geoscape_Draw @ 0x8c180 (33,744 B).
## Geoscape_Draw @ 0x8c180 (33,744 B) - read, ported in parts

Unit 107 works through the last large gap in pieces. The head, the cases 0/2 arm and the
13-arm panel switch have been read from the ARM; the parts ported so far are named below and
the rest is listed by target so the next unit does not have to re-derive the map.

The shape. A 21-case switch on nGeoscapeScreen @ 0x186BC4 (`CMP R0, #0x14 / ADDLS PC, PC,
R0, LSL #2` at 0x8C1AC..0x8C1B0, table 0x8C1B4..0x8C20C): cases 0 and 2 share one arm,
1 -> 0x91DC8, 3 -> 0x93F08, 4 -> 0x92DAC, 5 -> 0x92EE4, 6 -> 0x9309C, 7 -> 0x92AF0,
8 -> 0x94114, 9 -> 0x9415C, 10 -> 0x93E5C, 11 -> 0x93DD4, 12 -> 0x93E20, 15 -> 0x94304,
16 -> 0x941AC, 17 -> 0x94288, 18 -> 0x942F4, 19 -> 0x94314, 20 -> 0x944B0, and 13/14 plus
the default go straight to the tail at 0x944B8. Every arm ends there. The tail reads
MainMenu_nListMode: 4 draws UiModal_DrawDialog with a3 0x44F, 3 draws it with a3 0x44E, and
then GX_Present(pGX) at 0x9453C. Case 20 calls BaseAtScreen_Draw and falls in.

Cases 0 and 2 (0x8C214). bRadarScreenActive @ 0x159678 picks between the radar screen (its
pad, a 13-control blit loop on dword_186B08, one SoftSurf_BlitSrcRect at 150/130/120/60 with
the 150/130/120/60 colour quad, then RadarScreen_Update) and the world map chrome.

The map chrome, 0x8C2B0..0x8C760, PORTED as Geoscape_BlitMapView and Geoscape_BlitCrosshair
in game/pufo_geoscape.c. Three findings from the read:

- The overlay drift is `_rt_sdiv` with the DIVISOR in R0: 0x8C2F4 loads -24 as R0 and the map
  pad's uWidth as R1, so nDiv = uWidth / -24, and 0x8C30C..0x8C3C8 is
  (nHour * nDiv) - (uWidth * nMinute) * (1/1440) with the literal double
  0x3F46C16C16C16C17 at 0x8C38C, truncated by _dtoi. With the shipped 240-wide pad that is
  -10 * nHour - nMinute / 6: the day/night overlay slides one map width per game day.
- The scroll wrap is asymmetric. 0x8C3F0 `BNE loc_8C478` sends every screen id except 2 to a
  copy (0x8C478..0x8C494) that clamps nScrollX and then FALLS INTO the blit block without
  clamping nScrollY; only id 2 runs the Y clamp at 0x8C418..0x8C444. Each axis moves by at
  most one map width per step, and the band test is strict: scroll + half exactly equal to
  -nMapSize is NOT wrapped.
- The map pad is blitted twice for every id except 2 and four times for id 2 (0x8C498 base,
  0x8C4D0 and 0x8C4D0's pair at y + nMapH, 0x8C548 the x + nMapW copy). The layer pad's three
  world flips are the same three offsets the radar backdrop uses and are skipped for id 2 --
  the opposite polarity from the map pad's extra copies, which is why id 2 is the vertically
  wrapped view.

Not ported yet. The 13-arm status panel switch at 0x8C844 (SUB R0, #0x20 / CMP #0xC on line
0's flag byte from the root message list @ 0x158890, with BaseFac_BuildStatusMsg called at
0x8C82C on every arm that gets there, and the flag <= 0x1E or >= 0x32 falling to the default
arm at 0x8E5A4); the block 0x8E658..0x91CEC; and the screen arms 0x91DC8..0x944B0, which are
thin wrappers over the already-ported drawers (Geoscape_DrawGlobeHover, BaseFacScreen_DrawNameGrid,
BaseFacScreen_DrawBuildDialog, SoldierScreen_Draw, BasePlaneScreen_Draw, BuySellScreen_Draw,
TransferScreen_Draw, BaseInfoScreen_Draw, ResearchScreen_Draw, ManufScreen_DrawFrame,
Ui_DrawBaseInfo, PsiScreen_Draw, Geoscape_DrawScreen, FundingScreen_Draw,
FundingScreen_DrawExtended, BaseAtScreen_Draw).

Unit 107 part 2 -- the 13-arm status panel, Geoscape_DrawStatusPanel @ 0x8C760..0x8E658

Ported in src/pufo/game/pufo_geoscape.c as Geoscape_DrawStatusPanel with the helpers
StatusPanel_DrawAt, StatusPanel_CopyRec, StatusPanel_PackColour, StatusPanel_Anim,
StatusPanel_SetControls, StatusPanel_DrawFooter, StatusPanel_DrawDefault and
StatusPanel_DrawResearch. The contract, the env and every constant are in pufo_geoscape.h.

Head, 0x8C760..0x8C780: Gfx_PackRgb565Pair(0xDC, 0x50, 0x50 | R5, 0x1E, 0x1E). The second red is
R5, still the crosshair index 50 left over from 0x8C6A0 -- the panel never re-sets it.

Gates, 0x8C78C..0x8C7B0 and 0x8C838: UiLineList_GetFlag on line 0 of the root message list
@ 0x158890 is read TWICE -- once for the range test (CMP #0x1E / BLE at 0x8C798 and CMP #0x32 /
BGE at 0x8C7AC, both to the default arm at 0x8E5A4) and once again at 0x8C838 for the switch
(SUB R0, #0x20 / CMP #0xC / ADDLS PC at 0x8C844). So 0x1F..0x31 reach the switch and 0x1F and 0x31
fall off its far side into the same default arm.

BuildStatusMsg argument mapping, CORRECTED in the IDB comment at 0x8C82C. The callee
(BaseFac_BuildStatusMsg @ 0x6A4BC, 1,520 B) has exactly ONE stack argument, a5 at its entry SP+0:
a1 = R7 = abFacilityGrid (0x8C790); a2 = R1 = the flag byte sign-extended from a byte (0x8C818,
0x8C824); a3 = R2 = R5 = line 0 colour SLOT 0 (read at 0x8C7FC, kept at 0x8C804); a4 = R3 = R8 =

facility index; the callee's own prototype names agree with the corrected mapping (nBaseIdx,
nRowOrIdx, nColOrIdx).

### Unit 108, part 3: the action-fail line and the selected contact (0x8E658..0x8F24C)

Two blocks sit at the tail of the default arm, both reached through the BEQ at 0x8E5E0 that skipped
the panel draw itself.

**0x8E658, the action-fail line.** Three gates in this order: dwActionFail @ 0x1870C8 has to be
exactly 1 (0x8E664 `CMP #1 / BNE`, so 0 and 2 both fail), the line-0 flag has to be below 0x1E
(0x8E67C `CMP #0x1E / BGE`, so 0x1E itself is not below it), and dwActionFailReason @ 0x1870B4 has
to be 0 (0x8E68C BNE). Then `Ui_AnimExpandBlit_IfEnabled` at (0x14, 0x82) with size (0xC8, R8) --
`LDRSB R0, =dwActionFail` hands the blit its index, and the value is 1 because the first gate has
just proved it -- and TEXTS[406] "Íåò äåíåã" centred at y = 0x9E. R8 is the map half-extent the map
chrome left behind at 0x8C2D0 (`nMapW / 2 - 120`), zero for the shipped 240-wide grid pad, so the
frame degenerates to its own top edge.

**0x8E708, the contact the cursor is on**, gated on the line-0 flag being 0x0A. The entry is
`PtrArray_Get(strateg PtrArray @ 0x1864F8 + 0x3C, UiLineList_GetColor(line 0, slot n))`, and the
block re-reads that colour slot at every use: slot 0 five times and slot 1 once. Both scratch
buffers are globals -- szRadarMsg @ 0x186B10 for the size and speed lines, unk_186420 for the four
hyperwave lines (now named szUiScratchStr, see renames.tsv).

Field corrections this read produced, all against the struct layout the IDB already had:
- 0x8E8DC and 0x8EE98 load `LDRSB [R0,#2]`, which is **StrategItem.bCraftClass (+0x02), not nType
  (+0x00)**. The size switch and the hyperwave type line are both keyed on the craft class; the port
  had both on nType.
- 0x8E8C0 loads `[R0,#0x14]` = bRandA of the SLOT 0 entry as the factor of 61, while the switch
  value comes from the SLOT 1 entry: two different entries in one line.
- 0x8ECAC loads `[R0,#0x64]` = bHyperDetect, and it is the third re-read of slot 0 in the same block.
- The hyperwave lines load `[R0,#0x70]` = bRace (0x8EF90) and `[R0,#0x39]` = nMissionSub (0x8F05C),
  both from the SLOT 0 entry -- while the size line two lines above used the SLOT 1 entry's class.
- UiControl+0x0C is pfnClick: confirm gets Smap_OnPointerUp (0x8EC74) and pGeoscapeCtlA gets
  Smap_ClearSelection (0x8EC8C).

### Unit 107, part 4: the order questions (0x8F250..0x8F9E0)

The default arm's flag chain continues after the contact panel. Line 0's flag is re-read at 0x8F250,

sequence of independent CMP/BNE pairs, not a switch: 0x11, 0x0F, 0x0C, 0x0E and 0x0B in that order,

What the read turned up:
- aTextOk @ 0xEBF4B is TEXTS record **1127 "ÎÊ"**, CYRILLIC Î and Ê -- not the Latin TEXTS[1193] "OK"
  at 0xEF425 that the 13-arm footer at 0x8E3C4 uses. The test pins the difference: emptying 1127 empties
  the row under the control, emptying 1193 leaves it pixel-identical.
- The record offset register R9 is loaded in the prologue of the arm test that FOLLOWS: 0x8F268 loads
  1214 for the 0x11 arm, 0x8F418 loads 1216 for the 0x0F arm, and the 0x0E arm copies from the 1216
  offset at 0x8F7AC whether or not the 0x0F arm ran. A port that set the offset per arm would look the
  same here only because 0x0E really does use 1216; the shape is worth knowing before the next arm.
- Three different ways to name a craft inside five arms: 0x0F reads the global selected index 0x187054
  (0x8F488), 0x0E uses the line-0 colour value as the index (0x8F7E0), and the 0x0B arm WRITES the
  colour value into 0x187054 at 0x8FA90 and then reads the global back.
- The base name is aSiteRecs[colour value] + 0x1A -- the colour value IS the 64-byte record index
  (0x8F2E8 `ADD R3, R1, R0,LSL#6`), with no bounds test, the same records Save_WriteBases @ 0x3F1FC
  writes to the save file.
- 0x0E is the only arm that blits its controls before installing their handlers (0x8F91C/0x8F924, then
  0x8F934/0x8F940); 0x11, 0x0F and 0x0C set pfnClick first.
- Ship_FormatDisplayName returns szRadarMsg @ 0x186B10, so the 0x0F and 0x0E arms leave the craft name
  in that 108-byte buffer as a side effect; the 0x11 and 0x0C arms never touch it.

### Unit 107, part 5: the craft-detail card (0x8F9E4..0x9021C)

The fifth arm of the default chain, flag 0x0B, is the selected craft's detail card. It sits where no
other arm of the chain sits: the pad object at 0x186BBC is re-blitted as a rectangle first
(0x8F9FC..0x8FA30), then Ui_AnimExpandBlit puts the body at (0xE, 5) with size (0xD0, 0xDC) from src
(0x28, 0x32), key 0xB4, nIdx 0, nMode 0. The box is therefore x 14..225, y 5..230, and it is a filled
body, not an outline -- SoftSurf_BlitSrcRect_Inner @ 0xa4450 paints the whole rect (pufo_panel.c:567),
which is what a row comparison has to take into account.

Findings:
- 0x8FA90 `STR R0, [0x187054]`: this arm is the only one in the chain that WRITES the selected-craft
  index. It stores line 0's colour slot 0 there and every read after it (0x8FBB0, 0x8FC38, 0x8FCF4,
  0x8FEC4) goes through the global. 0x0F reads the global (0x8F488) and 0x0E uses the colour value
  directly (0x8F7E0) -- three different ways to reach the same craft in five arms.
- The rect blit takes all four operands out of the pad object: x from [pad], y from [pad + 4], width
  from LDRH [pad + 8], height from LDRH [pad + 0xA], with nIdx 0x3C, colour mid 0x78, low 0x82 and
  key 0x96. Over a cleared surface that paints 565 value 8745 in the pad's own rectangle.
- Four value lines centred on 120: TEXTS[1216] + Ship_FormatDisplayName at y 15, TEXTS[1214] +
  aSiteRecs[Ship.bHomeBase].abName (+0x1A) at 30, TEXTS[1222] + itoa(LDRH [Ship,#0x10], uFuelCap) at
  45, TEXTS[1223] + the fuel percent + '%' at 60. The percent multiplies by 100 BEFORE the divide
  (0x8FC50 `MUL R1, R3, R2` with R2 = 0x64) and then uses _rt_sdiv with the divisor uRangeMax in R0
  and the dividend in R1 (0x8FC54..0x8FC60). `MOV R11, #0xA` at 0x8FC34 is the itoa base, not a value.
- Two weapon slots (0x8FA54 `MOV R8, #0` to 0x8FFA4 `BLT loc_8FCBC`) reading LDRSB [Ship,#0x22] and
  LDRSB [Ship,#0x23]. Ids 25..30 append the name record 1350 + (id - 25) and take the count from
  Ship + 0x3D/0x3E/0x3F/none/0x40/0x41; id 28 has no byte and sets -1 at 0x8FDF8, which prints the
  aNA literal. Any other non-zero id appends no name and keeps the 0 stored at 0x8FCBC. A zero id
  skips BOTH rows of its slot (0x8FE50 `BEQ loc_8FF9C`). The rows are 30 apart: 75/90 and 105/120.
- The shared-pool halving (0x8FED8..0x8FF30) has three arms and not two. UNEQUAL mounts skip the
  halving ENTIRELY (`BNE loc_8FF34` jumps past both halves); equal mounts on slot 1 always floor;
  equal mounts on slot 0 round up only when ammo / 2 == 1, i.e. only for a pool of 2 or 3. The -1
  sentinel exits at 0x8FEBE before any of this is reached.
- 0x8FFB8 tests Ship.bContactMsg (+0x3C) and picks the four handlers. Set: all four take
  Smap_ResolveInterceptUI. Clear: Smap_DismissSelected on *0x186BA8, Smap_DismissSelected stored on
  *0x186B9C at 0x8FFE8 and then OVERWRITTEN by Smap_SelectMapTarget at 0x8FFEC, Smap_ConfirmSelected
  on *unk_186B98, and *pGeoscapeCtlB @ 0x186BB0 takes Smap_ResolveInterceptUI in both cases.
- bInterceptDone byte 0 @ 0x18709C gates two things at once: the cancel control's second pad blit at
  0x900B4 and the 'Îòìåíà' label at 0x90210. That label is TEXTS[1230], a second record carrying the
  same shipped text as 1144 -- the card never reads 1144.
- Four controls centred on 120 from their own pad widths at y 140/160/180/200, labels TEXTS[1227],
  [1228], [1229] at 140/160/180 and [1230] at 201.

Tests: 62 new checks (16,908 across 60 suites, 0 failures). Every value row is now pinned by pixels
rather than by row presence: the row's ink mask, taken against the panel body colour because the anim
paints a filled body, is compared with a reference draw of the string the test expects, centred with
the original's own formula (0x90204..0x90218). That is what makes 'b51' and 'b52' different answers.
The fixture points colour slot 0 at craft 1 while 0x187054 still holds 0, so the write at 0x8FA90 is
visible; the home base is site 3 so the base row shows the index is Ship.bHomeBase; ids 29 and 30 read
different ammo bytes (0x40, 0x41) and different name records, so a field mix-up shows up as a row.
27 more _Static_assert pins hold records 1222..1230 and 1350 plus the fourteen geometry values to the
ARM immediates.

Mutations: 23 patterns, 23 caught. The first sweep ran 21 patterns and two survived: reading ammo
0x41 for id 29 (the fixture had no ids 29/30 at all -- coverage added, then it was caught) and
changing the strip blit's key 0x96 to 0x95, which is provably EQUIVALENT: 16*149>>8, 30*149>>8 and
7*149>>8 give the same 9/17/4 fields as at 150, so the packed pixel is identical. It was replaced by
0x96 -> 0x60, which the pixel check catches (4454 against 8745). One run of the harness crashed
mid-sweep and left its first mutation (the weapon-mount swap) in the source, so every later pattern in
that run was measured against a mutated baseline and reported wrong rows; the swap was reverted, the
sweep re-run, and the harness now restores the source in a finally block.

IDB: 11 comments written (0x8F9E4 the pad reads and the body box, 0x8FA90 the only writer of 0x187054,
0x8FBC4 uFuelCap as the speed value, 0x8FC50 the multiply before the divide, 0x8FCBC the ammo bytes,
0x8FE50 the zero-id skip, 0x8FEBE the -1 exit, 0x8FEDC the three-arm halving rule, 0x8FFB8 the handler

bugs.tsv: 2 new rows (0x8FA90 unchecked apCraft index, 0x8FC50 divide by a possibly zero uRangeMax),

### Unit 107, part 6: the trace-lost panel (0x90220..0x904CC)
