### Unit 107, part 8: the intercept list (0x90728..0x9097C)

The eighth arm of the default chain, flag 0x1B. It is unlike every other arm in three ways: it is the
only one whose early exits leave the WHOLE default arm, the only one that draws the clock strip and the
root block's own thirteen controls, and the only one with a label at a non-120 centring anchor and
another with no centring at all.

The exits. 0x90798, 0x907A8, 0x907B8 and 0x90904 all branch to IDA's `def_8C1B0` -- the body of the
jumptable at 0x8C1B0's default case, which lives at **0x944B4** and is the shared tail of the whole
geoscape draw. They are not "skip this arm" jumps; they end the frame, and the flag tests after them
(0x14 at 0x909B8 and the rest) never run. The port says this with a bool return.

Shape:
- 0x90748 reads colour slot 0 and 0x90760 STORES it into 0x187054. It is a dword store, but the value
  cannot exceed 0xFF anyway: every write into a colour slot masks it (UiPanel_InsertLine @ 0x5A2F4 and
  UiPanel_SetLineColors @ 0x5A454 both `AND R3,R3,#0xFF`), which is also how Smap_HitTestStrategSelect's
  -1 arrives as 255 -- the same value the 0x0D panel uses as its "no target" sentinel.
- 0x9076C..0x90788 re-blits the strip pad rectangle with the same four reads and 0x3C / 0x78 / 0x82,
  nKey 0x96 built at 0x9074C.
- 0x9078C..0x907B8: the gates -- bSmapUfoCrashPanel @ 0x18708C, bSmapSitePanel @ 0x187090,
  bSmapAlienBasePanel @ 0x187098, the three bytes RadarScreen's click arms for an active type-4,
  type-3 and type-0 intercept. All three come AFTER the rectangle is already painted.
- 0x907C0 PadImage_Blit of the strip pad ITSELF, at its own origin, on top of that rectangle.
- 0x907C8 Geoscape_DrawClockPads with no GameTime_Decode in front of it. The decode belongs to
  LoadGame, SaveSlot_FormatList, GameTime_Reset, Geoscape_AdvanceTime, Geoscape_InitUI and
  Geoscape_PulseUpdate; the only draw-time call is 0x6C35C in Geoscape_DrawScreen.
- 0x907D0..0x907F4 blits the geoscape UI root's own thirteen widgets (0x1864F8 + 4*i, the loop test is
  CMP R0, #0xD), the counter kept in dword_186B08. The same thirteen-widget tail runs again at
  0x91D1C for every screen id except 2.
- 0x907F8..0x90828 the body anim (0xE, 0x104) size (0xD0, 0x28) from src (0x1E, 0x28), key 0xFF: box
  x 14..225, y 260..305 -- painted OVER the clock strip it just drew.
- 0x90858..0x9086C TEXTS[1235] "Âûáåðåòå öåëü" at x fixed 0x28, y 0x110|3 = 275. There is no
  Text_MeasureWidth call in front of this line at all.
- 0x90874..0x908A4 *pCtlB @ 0x186BB0 at x 0x8C = 140 fixed (the only control in the chain not centred

- 0x908D4..0x908F4 TEXTS[1144] centred on **173** (`RSB R1,R1,#0xAD`) at the same y 275.
- 0x908F8..0x90978 bFinalMissionCtlArmed @ 0x187068: clear ends the frame; set blits

### Unit 107, part 9: the map-target panel (0x909A8..0x90D60)

The ninth arm of the default chain, flag 0x14. Read with the ABI made explicit, because this arm is
where that ABI was finally nailed down: Ui_AnimExpandBlit takes FOUR register arguments (pObj, x, y,
nW) and SIX stack arguments (nH, nIdx, srcX, srcY, nKey, nMode) at SP+0..SP+0x14, which in
Geoscape_Draw's frame are the slots IDA names nKey@0, g2@4, b2@8, srcY@0xC, var_1B0@0x10,
nMode@0x14. SoftSurf_BlitSrcRect is the same shape (x, y, nRectW, nRectH in registers; nIdx,
nColorMid, nColorLow, nKey on the stack). Reading the stores through those slots is what confirms
every anim argument in this chain -- and it confirmed the 0x1B arm's arguments, which the compiler
loaded from registers rather than immediates.

The registers those immediates come from: the flag-0x10 TEST prologue (0x904DC..0x904F4) sets
R7 = 0x78, R11 = 0xB4, R8 = 0, R10 = 0x28 and R9 = 1144 * 205, and all five are callee-saved. That
prologue runs whenever the chain reaches it, whether or not flag 0x10 was taken -- so the 0x1B anim's
nH and srcY are R10, its nIdx and nMode are R8, the 0x14 anim's nKey is R11, and the 0x14 arm's
TEXTS[1144] label uses R9. The values are sticky, not reloaded.

bMapSelectionFlag @ 0x159E84 branches at 0x909DC, and the two blocks it selects -- 0x909E0..0x90A04
and 0x90BAC..0x90BD0 -- store the SAME six stack values: nH 0x5A, nIdx 0 (R8), srcX 0x28, srcY 0x32,
nKey 0xB4 (R11) and nMode 0 (R8), and reload nW 0xD0 into R3. The anim call is identical in both
arms; the flag only picks the text record. R0..R2 (the pad, x 0xE, y 0x3C) are set once at
0x909C4..0x909D4, before the branch.

Clear arm (0x90A08..0x90BA4):
- psz = TEXTS[1237] "Êðóøåíèå "; then strcat the status panel's OWN row buffer,
  `pStatusPanel->apLines[colour slot 0]` (0x90A30 reads slot 0, 0x90A48 `LDR R1,[R3,R10]` with
  R10 = 0xBE4 = the apLines offset); then strcat " " (asc_AADB8 at 0x90A58); then strcat the size
  word of `strategList[colour slot 1]` -- SLOT 1, not slot 0 (0x90A68) -- by its bCraftClass byte at
  +0x02 (0x90A84 LDRSB), jumptable at 0x90A8C: 0 -> 1359, 1/2 -> 1360, 3/4 -> 1361, 5/6 -> 1362,
  7 -> 1363. ADDLS only fires for 0..7 unsigned, so a negative class falls to the default at 0x90A90
  and appends nothing.
- the line centred at y 70; *pCtlA centred on 120 from its own uWidth at y 0x73 (115);
  Smap_ResolveInterceptUI installed at 0x90B60 BEFORE the 0x90B68 blit -- the reverse of the 0x0B,
  0x0D, 0x10 and 0x1B arms; TEXTS[1127] "ÎÊ" centred at y 0x74 (116).

Set arm (0x90BAC..0x90D40): psz = TEXTS[1238] "Ìèññèÿ: " (via R7, loaded in the test prologue at
0x909B0) + the same apLines row, with no space and no size word; the line at y 70; *pCtlB centred at
y 0x66 (102) with Smap_CancelTarget @ 0x84254 installed at 0x90C78 before the 0x90C80 blit; TEXTS[1127]
centred at y 0x67 (103); *pCtlA centred at y 0x7D (125) with Smap_ResolveInterceptUI; TEXTS[1144]
centred at y 0x7E (126). Both arms end in the same centring tail at 0x90D44..0x90D5C, with y already
in R2, and then B 0x90D7C -- the next flag test.

ORIGINAL BUG, in bugs.tsv: 0x90A48 indexes the status panel's apLines by the raw colour byte with no
bounds test and no null check. That panel is built with 20 rows (Geoscape_InitUI 0x86AC0,
UiPanel_ctor(pPanel, 20)) and UiPanel_ctor allocates exactly nLineCount buffers, so apLines[20..499]
is NULL and a slot value of 20..255 hands a NULL to the strcat at 0x90A54. The colour byte is a
strateg-list index in the arms before this one, so the two roles do not share a bound. The port skips
a row it cannot read.

Tests: 52 new checks (17,054 across 60 suites, 0 failures) and 13 new _Static_assert pins. Two new
fixture pieces carry the weight: (1) the panel gets 20 row buffers with text in rows 3 and 4, so the
apLines index is visible in the drawn line and rows 20 and 255 exercise the guard; (2) the blit
callback now also snapshots the control's pfnClick AT BLIT TIME (the pad identifies the control), so
the handler-before-blit order is observable -- on a single fresh run, because PnCapture runs the arm

order mutation survived its first version for the double-run reason above and was caught after the
test was fixed, not after the source was).

### Unit 107, part 10: the intercept-mission panel (0x90D78..0x9118C) and the travel panel (0x91190..0x91480)

Two more arms of the status-panel default chain, read after the argument ABI was known.

  0x90FB0). This is the only arm in the chain that reads the panel's own row instead of a colour slot.

  srcX 0x28, srcY 0x32, nMode 0 with nW 0xD0 and x 14. The key 0xB4 is a literal here (0x90DAC)
  because R11 is holding 0xBD8 and cannot carry it; the two zeros come from `MOV R0,#0` at 0x90DB0,
  before the 0x90DB4 branch.

  the mission-site name is strcat on -- index from the signed byte at +0x02 of `strategList[colour
  SLOT 1]` (0x90E94, 0x91038 `LDRSB`), times 0x18 (0x90E90 / 0x91034 `MOV R2,#0x18`, the MissionSiteRec
  stride), off 0x1864F8 + 0xC8 = 0x1865C0, plus 4 for the name. Drawn centred at y 86 (0x90ED8,

  0x838dc stored at 0x91578 BEFORE the `UiControl_BlitActivePad` at 0x91580. TEXTS[1127] (R8 = aTextOk,
  inline copy 0x91584..0x915A0) centred at y 103 (0x915D0).

  `Craft_CountSoldiersAboard`. The first argument is abFacilityGrid (0x915E8) and the callee never reads
  it -- 0x664A0 loads its own roster base at 0x1139B8 and 0x664B0 the count from nSoldierCount, so only
  the colour byte matters. The craft index here is a FULL byte, not the 0..7 size class the 0x14 arm reads
  from the same slot.

  that REPLACE CtlB's handler with Smap_ResolveInterceptUI -- after its pad has already been blitted. An
  empty craft therefore draws a "select craft" row whose click resolves the intercept.
- CtlA: centred (0x9160C), y 125 (0x91624), resolve handler stored at 0x91630 before the 0x91638 blit;
  TEXTS[1144] (R9, inline copy 0x9163C..0x9165C, tail `BNE loc_9164C`) centred at y 126 (0x91688). The
  arm ends there: 0x9168C is the flag-0x15 test.
- There is no `bMapSelectionFlag` read anywhere in 0x9148C..0x91688 -- one path only, which the test
  proves by running the arm with the flag clear and set and comparing the frames.
- The `AND R1,R0,#0xFF` is provably a formality: UiPanel_InsertLine writes a colour slot with `LDRB` of a
  byte argument into the record's dword slot (0x5A314 / 0x5A318), so a slot value is 0..255 before any
  reader masks it. That is why dropping the mask is not a behaviour change and why the first version of
  the byte test here was vacuous -- it was replaced by a real one (craft 255 counts, craft 4 does not).

### Unit 107, part 13: the flag-0x16 clone (0x91938..0x91B1C)

The status-panel chain has the descent panel TWICE. Flag 0x17 tests at 0x91498 and runs 0x914A4..0x91688;
flag 0x16 tests at 0x91930 (0x91920 `MOV R7,#0`, `BL UiPanel_GetLineFlag` at 0x9192C, `CMP R0,#0x16` at
0x91930, `BNE loc_91B20` at 0x91934) and runs a second copy of the same body at 0x91938..0x91B1C.

- The clone proof is instruction-by-instruction, not byte-by-byte: both bodies are 484 bytes and 121
  instructions, in the same order, writing the same frame slots and calling the same callees. 117 of the 121
  pairs disassemble identically. The 4 that do not are all equivalent: three copy-loop tails naming their own
  arm's loop head (0x91500 / 0x91994, 0x915A4 / 0x91A38, 0x9165C / 0x91AF0) and 0x91AE4 `STRB R2,[R0,R1]`
  against 0x91650 `STRB R2,[R1,R0]` -- additive [Rn,Rm] addressing over the same pair (R1 = psz - rec from
  0x91ADC, R0 = rec + i), so both store at psz + i. The compiler picked the other operand order.
- A first attempt at this comparison used raw bytes and was WRONG: the byte fetch came back short (395 of
  484 bytes), the chunks were concatenated anyway, and the misaligned windows produced a list of 24
  "differences" whose pairs disassembled identically. Check the returned length before comparing bytes;
  compare disassembly when the length is not exact.
- The clone reads six sticky registers set by other arms' prologues and sets none itself: R5 (TEXTS base),
  R6 = TEXTS[1239] (0x91490), R7 = 0 (0x9149C, the anim's two zero stack stores at 0x91964 / 0x9196C),
  R8 = TEXTS[1127], R9 = 1144 * 205, R10 = 0xBE4, R11 = 0xBD8 (0x90D88). Its rows are the 0x17 rows: text
  line 70, CtlB 102 (0x919F8 #0x66) with `Smap_BeginCraftSelect` at 0x91A0C before the 0x91A14 blit,
  TEXTS[1127] 103, the soldiers-aboard gate at 0x91A68..0x91A80 with the zero-count handler swap at
  0x91A8C..0x91A98, CtlA 125 with the resolve handler at 0x91AC4 before 0x91ACC, TEXTS[1144] 126.
- The clone carries the same two dead things as the first copy: `abFacilityGrid` as
  `Craft_CountSoldiersAboard`'s unread first argument (0x91A7C, against 0x664A0) and `AND R1,R0,#0xFF` at
  0x91A78 after `UiPanel_GetLineColor` (0x91A74).
- Port shape: one arm, `PUFO_STATUS_FLAG_DESCENT_ALT` (0x16) next to
  `PUFO_STATUS_FLAG_DESCENT_PANEL` (0x17), both through `StatusPanel_DrawDescentPanel`. The port does NOT
  duplicate the body.

Tests: 22 checks (17203 across 60 suites, 0 failures), one `_Static_assert` pin on 0x16, and 6/6 mutations
caught -- five at run time, and the sixth (the constant changed to 0x1B) caught by the pin at compile time.
The new whole-frame compare is paired with its control: 0x16 against the saved 0x17 frame must give 0
changed pixels, and 0x15 against the same frame must change some, so the match carries information.

bugs.tsv: 1 row for the duplicated body.

### Unit 107, part 14: the alien-base panel (0x91B34..0x91CE8, flag 0x3C)

The last arm of the status-panel chain that the flag tests reach. 0x3C is outside the 0x1F..0x31 range the
jumptable at 0x8C844 covers (0x8C798 `CMP #0x1E` BLE, 0x8C7AC `CMP #0x32` BGE), so it enters through the
default case, the same route 0x12..0x17 take. Test: 0x91B20 `MOV R7,#0`, `BL UiPanel_GetLineFlag` at 0x91B28,
`CMP R0,#0x3C` at 0x91B2C, `BNE loc_91CEC` at 0x91B30.

- Anim (0x91B34..0x91B70): x 2 (0x91B64) and nW 0xE8 (0x91B6C) -- the widest panel in the chain, against the
  0xE / 0xD0 every other arm passes. y 0x3C, nH 0x5A, srcX 0x28, srcY 0x32, nKey 0xB4 as usual, but nIdx and
  nMode are zeroed LOCALLY (0x91B48 `MOV R0,#0` stored at 0x91B54 and 0x91B58) instead of reusing R7.
- Three records, all by inline copy loops, none appended to: TEXTS[1445] (0x91B74 `=(unk_FBDF1 - 0xB38D0)`,
  loop 0x91B88..0x91B98) centred at y 70; TEXTS[1446] (0x91BF4 `=(unk_FBEBE - 0xB38D0)`, loop 0x91C08..0x91C18)
  centred at y 100; TEXTS[1144] (0x91C74 `MOV R1,#0x39418` = 1144 * 205, loop 0x91C8C..0x91C9C) centred at
  y 126. lang.dat gives them: "Âíèìàíèå! Îáíàðóæåíà áàçà ïðèøåëüöåâ", "Öåíòð íà áàçó", "Îòìåíà".
- Two controls: CtlConfirm centred from its own pad at y 100 (0x91BE0) and CtlA centred at y 125 (0x91C60),
  blitted at 0x91BF0 and 0x91C70. The 1446 label is drawn at y 100 AFTER that blit, so it lands on the
  control's own row.
- Handlers come LAST: `Smap_OnPointerUp` @ 0x84688 at CtlConfirm+0xC (0x91CD0/0x91CD8) and
  `Smap_ClearSelection` @ 0x84648 at CtlA+0xC (0x91CE0/0x91CE8) -- after both blits, which is the opposite of
  the 0x17 / 0x16 / 0x15 arms that install before blitting.
- Nothing else is read: no colour slot, no strateg entry, no panel row, no mission site, no gate, no
  bMapSelectionFlag. That is asserted by a whole-frame compare against a fixture with different colour slots,
  a different selected row, a different strateg entry and bMapSelectionFlag set -- 0 pixels differ.
- The arm FALLS THROUGH into the chain's shared tail at 0x91CEC (the other arms reach it by BNE). That tail is
  not ported: `*0x186BC4 == 2` test; otherwise blit `*0x186BBC`, `Geoscape_DrawClockPads` (0x91D0C) and blit the
  thirteen root widgets at 0x1864F8 + 4*i for i in 0..12 (0x91D1C..0x91D38); the == 2 branch at 0x91D78 reads
  the two signed cursor shorts, calls `Geoscape_DrawGlobeHover`, stores the result into bPendingRegionId and
  continues to 0x93058 only when byte_1870AC is zero.

Two things the port-side reading needed, both worth remembering:

- TEXTS records 1445 and 1446 read as 0xFF in the IDB: the whole 0xB38D0 TEXTS block is uninitialised in the
  shipped .data and only carries text after TEXTS.DAT loads (lang.dat holds 1650 records of 200 bytes each,
  main.dat 1721; the in-memory stride is 205). So record identity is checked against lang.dat, not the binary.
- The arm is only reachable because 0x3C is OUTSIDE the jumptable range. The port's equivalent test is
  `nFlag < PUFO_STATUS_FLAG_MIN || nFlag > PUFO_STATUS_FLAG_MAX` at the top of `Geoscape_DrawStatusPanel`,
  which routes such flags into `StatusPanel_DrawDefault` -- and the arm chain lives in that default arm's
  continuation.

A wrong citation was fixed on the way: `GeoscapeStatusPanelEnv.pfnSelectTarget` was commented "Smap_OnPointerUp
@ 0x89450", but 0x89450 is `Geoscape_OnPointerUp`; `Smap_OnPointerUp` is @ 0x84688, which is what 0x91CD0 and
0x90640 load. The IDB names were already right; the port comment had the wrong address.

### Unit 107, part 15: the chain's shared tail (0x91CEC..0x91DB0)

The block every arm of the flag chain lands on. Reached three ways: the flag tests reach it by `BNE`
(0x91B30 is the last one), the 0x3C body by falling through from 0x91CE8, and the jumptable case for flag 0x2B
by the `B 0x8E3E4`. Ported as `StatusPanel_DrawChainTail`, called at the end of `StatusPanel_DrawDefault` and
in `case '+'`.

- Branch test (0x91CF4 `CMP R0, #2` on *0x186BC4): an equality test, not a range test. Screen id 3 -- what
  `LoadGame_Slot*_InitOptions` leaves at 0x6B1B0 -- takes the ordinary branch too. The port writes it as
  `*pEnv->pnScreenId != PUFO_STATUS_SCREEN_ID_GLOBE_HOVER`.
- Not 2 (0x91CFC..0x91D3C): `PadImage_Blit` of the pad *pGeoscapeStripPad points at (its own glyph at its own
  origin, not a rectangle), `Geoscape_DrawClockPads` (0x91D0C, with the block at 0x159618 as its only
  argument), then a thirteen-iteration loop blitting the geoscape UI root's own widgets at 0x1864F8 + 4*i, with
  the loop counter spilled into dword_186B08 (reset at 0x91D18, compared against #0xD at 0x91D34). Ends with
  `B def_8C1B0`, i.e. the frame-end block at 0x944B4: BaseAtScreen_Draw, the MainMenu_nListMode 4/3 modal
  dialogs, GX_Present, the epilogue.
- == 2 (0x91D78..0x91DB0): the new-base globe hover. Three arguments are set -- R0 = abFacilityGrid,
  R1 = nSmapCursorX, R2 = nSmapCursorY -- but only R0 is read by the callee: it saves it (0x67280 PUSH {R0},
  0x6728C STR to var_s28) and reads it back once at 0x67860 as the base for the +0x62C / +0x630 pending-pick
  stores, while its first call at 0x67294 overwrites R1 / R2 first. The hovered tile comes back in R0 and is
  stored with `STRB` at 0x91D94 into bPendingRegionId @ 0x159DF4 (a byte store of a 32-bit value). Then
  `ANDS R3, R0, #0xFF` / `BNE` at 0x91D98..0x91DA4: while the byte at 0x1870AC is non-zero the close control
  is NOT blitted. Otherwise `LDR R0, =g_pUiCloseCtl; LDR R0,[R0]` and `B loc_93058` -- the blit itself is a
  site shared with the other screen arms, not code in this block.
- **0x1B is the one chain arm that never reaches the tail.** Every exit of it -- the three panel gates
  0x90798 / 0x907A8 / 0x907B8, the final-mission gate 0x90904 and its normal end 0x9097C -- jumps to
  def_8C1B0. That was a live port bug: `StatusPanel_DrawInterceptList` returned a bool and only the `false`
  paths stopped the chain, so a normal 0x1B frame continued through the remaining flag tests. It was harmless
  while the tail was unported and became visible the moment the tail was added (the 0x1B frame would have
  blitted 27 pads instead of 14). Now the arm returns void and the caller returns after it. The mutation
  sweep has this exact mutant: 14 -> 27 blits, caught.
- Among the jumptable cases only 0x2B '+' reaches the tail (0x8E3E4); the other twelve end at def_8C1B0.
  Test-wise that is the difference between 15 blits and 2 for the 13-arm table.

What the tail changed in the existing tests. It adds thirteen control blits and its own ink (the strip pad at
30,250 and the clock down to y 305) to every chain-path arm, so 40 checks needed fixing:

- Blit counts became `PUFO_GEOUI_ROOT_CTLS + n` with the message naming both parts.
- Whole-surface frame measurements became `PnDiffRect(0, 0, W-1, PN_TAIL_INK_Y - 1)` (row 250 is the tail's
  first ink row), and the two 100x24 strip-rectangle counts became rect-limited `PnDiffRect(30, 250, 129, 273)`
  -- the tail's clock rows fall partly outside that rect and would otherwise join the count, while its own pad
  blit falls INSIDE the rect and cannot change a count that is already full.
- The "draws NOTHING" checks for flag 0x1E are now two checks: nothing above row 250, and a positive check
  that the frame is NOT empty, because the tail is what is left.

Three of the new tail's own checks failed on the first run, all test-side: the pad glyph's far corner is
0x2F07 (eight indices 11..18 row-major over a 4x2 pad, not 11/12/13/14 in a column); on the hover branch
BdPix(30,250) is not 0 because the hover paints a full-surface wash first (0x672C8..0x672D8), so the honest
assertion is that the pad's glyph colour 0x2F00 is absent; and the hover's `nPickX` sentinel must be re-applied
per frame (as GhRun does) or the second run sees the first run's pick.

0x91D94, 0x91DA4, 0x91DA8, 0x9097C, 0x8E3E4) and one wrong comment corrected -- 0x91D88 said
"abFacilityGrid ... unused", but the callee keeps it in var_s28 and reads it at 0x67860 for the +0x62C /

`pGeoscapeStripPad` (allocated in Geoscape_InitUI, read by the globe hover, blitted whole at 0x907C0 and
0x91D04) and 0x1870AC `bPlacementPending` (set by Geoscape_OnMapClick 0x8B608, cleared by Game_StartNew

Part 16 -- the frame end 0x944B4..0x94550, ported as Geoscape_DrawFrameEnd (src/pufo/game/pufo_geoscape.c).

Who reaches it. Case 20 (0x944B0) falls through. The jumptable default (0x8C1B4: screens 13, 14 and any id
outside 0..20), the twelve screen arms that end in B def_8C1B0, the flag chain (0x91D3C after its thirteen root
blits, 0x91DA4 on the globe-hover branch) and the five exits of the 0x1B arm (0x90798, 0x907A8, 0x907B8,
0x90904, 0x9097C) branch to it. Case 19 is the only arm that does not: its funding block ends at 0x9449C with
B loc_92ACC, the centring/printing tail shared with the earlier arms. So BaseAtScreen_Draw, the two modal
dialogs and GX_Present are the tail of the WHOLE function and one port function covers every arm.

The registers the block relies on. R4 = the Map/context base 0x1139B8, loaded at 0x8C19C before the switch and
kept by every arm: it is the first argument of both modal calls (0x944F4, 0x94530 MOV R0,R4) and of GX_Present
(0x94538). R5 = 0 (0x944BC) is written into the two button-string slots (0x944D0 psz2, 0x944E8 psz): the dialog
has no buttons. R6 = &MainMenu_nListMode (0x944B8, 0x157188).

BaseAtScreen_Draw (0x58728) has no argument. It reads its state from globals: the gate byte bBaseAtActive
(0x158864, LDRB at 0x58734), the pad pointer pBaseAtPad (0x15884C, the +0xC field of the 0x158840 record,
LDR [R0,#0xC] at 0x58744) and the panel pBaseAtPanel (0x15885C, LDR R5,=0x15885C at 0x58754). The
LDR R0,=0x158840 that case 20 leaves in R0 at 0x944B0 is therefore dead -- a ledger row, and the reason the
port's env has no field for it.

The mode tests. 0x944C0 LDR R0,[R6] / 0x944C4 CMP #4 / 0x944C8 BNE 0x94500: mode 4 is the save-in-progress
dialog. 0x944FC re-reads the same global before the mode-3 test at 0x94500 -- the first dialog's callee is free
to change it -- so the port reads it twice (nModeA, nModeB). Both arms write 0x28 (40) into
Map.anActionPhaseSave0[112] @ 0x128AA0 (MOV R0,#0x28 at 0x944CC / 0x94508, R12 offset 0x944D8 / 0x94514, STR
0x944E0 / 0x9451C) and call UiModal_DrawDialog with nWidth 0x96 (150), nLines 1 and the record built in two
steps: 0x440 at 0x944D4 / 0x94510, then ORR #0xF (1103) at 0x944EC or ORR #0xE (1102) at 0x94528. Any other mode
value draws no dialog here (modes 1, 12 and 13 tested).

GX_Present at 0x9453C is the 0x27788 thunk for GX_PresentFrame (0x9ea7c): the frame is on screen before
Geoscape_Draw returns, which is why Render_Frame's geoscape branch (0x22328 / 0x22330) has no present of its
own. The port hands the thunk's value back like 0x9453C leaves it in R0.

0x94550 RET is padding behind the epilogue's LDM (0x94544) and the literal pool (0x94548 DCD
MainMenu_nListMode, 0x9454C DCD 0x158840), not a second return path.

Tests (TestGeoscapeFrameEnd, 32 checks; 17286 across 60 suites). Both dialogs are pinned by their box, not by a
count: nWidth 150 gives nX = (240-150)/2 = 45 and nLines 1 gives nHeight = 13+10 = 23 with nY = (320-23)/2 =
148, so the checks are "nothing above y 147", "nothing below row 171", "nothing left of x 45", the corner at
(45,148) drawn, the right border at x 195 -- one column outside the body, the 0x265D4 off-by-one the port keeps
-- and nothing at x 197. Record identity is checked both ways with a positive control per mode: mode 4 loses
its text when 1103 is blanked and keeps the same frame when 1102 is blanked, mode 3 the other way round, and a
mode-4 frame differs from a mode-3 frame. BaseAtScreen_Draw runs first: its confirm-shown byte is set and its
label at PUFO_BASEAT_CONFIRM_Y 290 is the only ink in a mode-0 frame (rows 286..305, nothing above 285), and
with its gate cleared the frame stays empty while GX_Present still runs once. The phase save is untouched for
modes 0, 12 and 13 and is 40 for both dialog arms. Same mode drawn twice gives a diff of 0. The present hook's
value is handed back (7) and a missing hook returns 0.

Mutations: 8 behaviour-bearing mutants, 8 caught, none survived -- each mode test flipped, the two records
swapped, the width 150 -> 120, nLines 1 -> 2, the 0x28 -> 41, dropping BaseAtScreen_Draw, dropping the present.
One candidate was left out on purpose: caching the mode instead of re-reading it at 0x944FC cannot be observed
here, because nothing between the two tests writes MainMenu_nListMode.

IDB: 12 line comments on the frame end (0x942F4, 0x94304, 0x94314, 0x9449C, 0x944B0, 0x944B8, 0x944C4, 0x944CC,
0x944D4, 0x944FC, 0x94510, 0x9453C) and the 21-case screen-switch map as the function comment of Geoscape_Draw.
Four globals named to match the port's BaseAtUpdateEnv: nBaseAtClass (0x158840), pBaseAtPad (0x15884C),
pBaseAtPanel (0x15885C), bBaseAtActive (0x158864), each with a data comment giving the record layout at

UiPanel * -- a pointer type on a byte -- while every access is 4-byte (LDR/STR [R5,#0xC] at 0x578E0..0x57900,
LDR [R4] at 0x57AEC..0x586D4); they are 4-byte items now. A scratch note on dword_186B08: no single owner, the
UI open/init paths use it as a temp (0x84B60, 0x84C54, 0x851FC, 0x85838..0x86CCD) and Geoscape_Draw spills its

Part 17 -- the thin screen arms 0x93DD4..0x93F04 and 0x94114..0x941A4, ported as Geoscape_DrawResearchArm,
Geoscape_DrawManufArm, Geoscape_DrawTransferArm and Geoscape_DrawBuySellArm.

Five arms are thin: a pad blit, a run of the screen's own control pads, the screen frame (every frame function
is ported already), then the frame end of part 16. The run is the same loop five times over -- the counter
spilled into the shared scratch dword_186B08 and re-read from it every iteration, the control pointer read out
of the screen's own block -- so the port writes it once (Geoscape_BlitCtlRun).

Case 8 (0x94114..0x94154): ResearchScreen_Draw FIRST (0x9411C, R0 = &aResearchTopics) and the callee blits the
pad itself at 0x73A40, so this arm has no pad blit at all. Two controls: aResearchTopics + 0x1D48 / + 0x1D4C
(0x160C50, 0x160C54), the offset built as 0x1D40|8 at 0x9412C / 0x94134, CMP #2 at 0x9414C. The next two words
(0x160C58 / 0x160C5C) are a different pair -- the quantity controls the frame blits.

Case 9 (0x9415C..0x941A4): [0x159E98] blitted first (0x94160 / 0x94164), then 0x159E98 + 0x4F84 / + 0x4F88
(0x15EE1C, 0x15EE20; offset built as 0x4F00|0x84 at 0x94174 / 0x9417C, CMP #2 at 0x94194), then
ManufScreen_DrawFrame with the block base in R0 (0x9419C / 0x941A0).

Case 10 (0x93E5C..0x93EB4): [0x1870D8] (the transfer root array's pad), then FOUR controls -- the array's own
slots 0x1870DC..0x1870E8 (LDR [R3,#4] at 0x93E78, CMP #4 at 0x93E8C) -- then TransferScreen_Draw(R0 = the
array, R1 = nSelectedBaseIdx read SIGNED at 0x93EA8, R2 = byte_1870F4 read SIGNED at 0x93E98: the base the psi
screen selected), value dropped.

Cases 11 and 12 (0x93DD4..0x93E14, 0x93E20..0x93E58): instruction-for-instruction identical prefixes --
*pBuySellScreenPad (0x161A08), then g_aBuySellCtl[0] and [1] (0x161A0C, 0x161A10) -- and ONE shared
BuySellScreen_Draw call at 0x93E10: case 11 falls into it, case 12 reaches it with the B at 0x93E58. The two
screens draw the same frame (a ledger row); only their Geoscape_CloseUI cases differ (0x8C0BC rebuilds the
controls, 0x8C108 rebuilds the panels and then calls Base_RemoveAllShips and Base_RemoveAllSoldiers).

The tail 0x93EB4..0x93F04, shared by cases 10, 11 and 12: LDRB R3,[R7,#0x35] -- R7 is Geoscape_Draw's argument
(0x8C190 MOV R7,R0) and Render_Frame passes 0x1864F8 (0x2232C), so the gate is the root block's byte at
0x18652D (bBaseFacPreviewOk, the base-facility preview flag: the transfer screen drives the buy/sell lists --
a ledger row). Then UiScrollList_TrackHold on *pBuySellPanelB (0x161A00, re-read at 0x93ED4) and on
*pBuySellPanelC (0x161A20, re-read at 0x93EE8), both with the SAME cursor position: R5 = nSmapCursorY and
R6 = nSmapCursorX, loaded at 0x93EC0 / 0x93EC4 and read LDRSH for both lists.

Cases 15 (0x94304) and 18 (0x942F4) are one call each -- FundingScreen_Draw(&pFundPad @ 0x1595DC) and
Geoscape_DrawScreen(aOptionsListCtl) -- so there is no arm code to port; the dispatcher will call them.

Tests (TestGeoscapeScreenArms, 27 checks; 17313 across 60 suites). Calibrated first: the transfer frame's first
separator really paints at (130,69) and BaseUi_DrawFrameRails really paints the left rail at x 5. Control blits
are counted by UiControl_BlitActivePad offering the control's pad to the recorder, so the run is checked by pad
IDENTITY and by ORDER, not by counts alone: two pads for 8, 9, 11/12 and four for 10, each in slot order. The
arm pad is a 2x2 glyph of a private colour (0x3A00, palette index 20, slot 20) placed exactly on the transfer
separator column, which is what makes the pad-before-frame order observable: after the transfer arm the colour
survives at (131,69) and is gone at (130,69), while the buy/sell arm keeps both -- that frame draws no
separator on the ungated path. The controls-before-frame order of 9 and 11/12 is pinned by the frame's own
control (ManufFrameEnv.pCtlReset at 0x70D84, BuySellDrawEnv.pCtlClose at 0x78028 -- unconditional, unlike the
research frame) being recorded LAST. Screen 8 has no pad of its own: the colour is absent at both columns. The
tail is checked through the row UiPanel_TrackHoldRow stores at panel+0xC: cursor Y 150 with panel B at nPosY
100 / nFont 10 gives 5 and panel C at 200 gives -5, and with 0x18652D clear neither panel is touched while the
four control blits still happen. Screens 8 and 10 have no arm/callee-order marker (neither frame blits a
control on this path), so those two orders rest on the citations -- stated rather than tested.

Mutations: 17 mutants, all caught (16 by a check, 1 by a crash: the control run with its null guard removed).
Counts 2->4 and 4->2 in each arm, the loop index shifted by one, each of the three pad blits dropped, the frame
moved before the pad and the controls in 9, 10 and 11/12, each tail call dropped, the 0x18652D gate removed,
nSmapCursorX fed instead of nSmapCursorY, and panel C fed twice. Two of them had to be re-authored: MSVC /W4
fails the build on an unreferenced formal parameter (C4100), so a dropped pad blit needs a (void)pPad.

IDB: 13 comments on the arm sites and the shared tail (0x94114, 0x94120, 0x9415C, 0x94168, 0x9419C, 0x93DD4,
0x93E0C, 0x93E20, 0x93E5C, 0x93E68, 0x93EB4, 0x93EC0, 0x93EDC). Seven wrong item sizes fixed: 0x1870D8
(PadImage *) and 0x1870DC..0x1870E8 (UiControl *) and the two manufacturing arm controls 0x15EE1C / 0x15EE20
were 1-byte items although every access is a 4-byte LDR. Comments (not retypes) at 0x160C50, which sits inside
the aResearchTopics record layout, and at 0x18652D for its second job as this gate. Saved.


Part 18 -- the ufopaedia and psi screen arms 0x941AC..0x94288 and 0x94288..0x942E8, ported as
Geoscape_DrawUfopaediaArm and Geoscape_DrawPsiArm.

Case 16 (0x941AC..0x94288). 0x941AC LDR R6,=g_pUfopaediaScreenPad and 0x941B0 MOV R0,R6 -- the callee receives
the BLOCK BASE (0x1872E0), not a pad, so Ui_DrawBaseInfo blits the screen pad itself (0x9B600) and the close
control (0x9B7C0) and this arm blits no pad. What follows is three copies of the control loop over the block's
six slots, the pointer being LDR [R6 + 4*i + 8] = 0x1872E8..0x1872FC:
  open && !dirty -> i 4..5 (0x941DC MOV R0,#4, CMP #6 at 0x941FC);
  dirty && wide  -> i 0..3 (0x94220 MOV R0,#0, CMP #4 at 0x94240);
  dirty && !wide -> i 2..3 (0x9425C MOV R0,#2, CMP #4 at 0x9427C).
0x941CC BEQ (not open) and 0x941D8 BNE (dirty) both land on the dirty test at 0x94204, so the open byte gates
only the first range: a closed screen with a dirty entry still blits the entry controls, and an open screen
with a dirty entry blits no category control (a ledger row).

Which control is which comes from aUiBaseInfoCtlDesc @ 0xAC548, the table Ui_InitBaseInfo hands to
UiControl_Setup(slot 2+i) at 0x9DE9C..0x9DEC0: [0] (142,210) and [1] (172,210) are the text-panel scroll pair,
[2] (10,210) and [3] (40,210) the entry prev/next pair, [4] (200,18) and [5] (200,38) the category selector
scroll pair. Each gate therefore picks the pair the view it draws needs: no entry drawn -> the category
scroll pair; the wide text panel -> the scroll pair plus the entry pair; a plain entry -> the entry pair only.
Geoscape_OnPointer (0x88E28..0x88E54 with MOV R0,#4 / CMP #6, then 0x88E94.. with the same wide test at
0x88E74) drives exactly 4..5, 0..3 and 2..3 on click -- the cross-check for the bounds. Geoscape_PulseButtons
case 16 (0x95748..0x957E0) pulses only 4..5 (ADD R5,R4,#0x10 then LDR [R5,#8]) and 0..1, and pulses nothing
when the wide byte is clear (0x957B4 BEQ): the entry pair is blitted but never auto-repeats.

The flag that selects the wide layout, 0x1871FC, was unk_1871FC. Ufopaedia_RefreshEntry clears it with the
other layout defaults (0x9A0B8) and sets it from the entry-number band (0x9A154, 0x9A19C, 0x9A1C0, 0x9A208,
0x9A21C, 0x9A230, 0x9A244). The IDB now names it g_bUfopaediaWidePanel; the port had two names for it
(pbWidePanel in UfopaediaEnv, pb16ListFull in GeoscapePointerEnv) and now has one.

Case 17 (0x94288..0x942E8). R0 = the block base 0x15EE78 (0x94294 MOV R0,R6) and R1 = byte_1870F4 read SIGNED
(LDRSB at 0x94290), which the port already carries as PsiScreenDrawEnv.nBaseIdx, so the arm needs no extra
argument. Two gates, both on bytes the callee reads itself: the scroll controls run only with byte_1870F8 CLEAR
(0x9429C..0x942A8 BNE) AND g_bPsiPanelOpen set (0x942AC..0x942B8 BEQ -- the same flag PsiScreen_Draw gates on
at 0x723B8). The controls are the block's own slots +4 / +8 (LDR [R6 + 4*i + 4] at 0x942CC): g_pPsiScrollPrevCtl
0x15EE7C then g_pPsiScrollNextCtl 0x15EE80, CMP #2 at 0x942E0.

Tests (TestGeoscapeUfoPsiArms, 29 checks; 17342 across 60 suites, 0 failures). Ui_DrawBaseInfo runs on the one
path that needs no panels -- bUfopaediaScreenBuilt clear gives screen pad, close control, return
(0x9B7CC..0x9B7D8) -- so the callee-first order is pinned by its close control being the FIRST recorded blit,
and the ranges by pad identity: slots 4,5 in the open-and-clean case, 0..3 with the entry dirty and wide, 2,3
with the entry dirty and not wide, and the category pair proven ABSENT in the dirty case (0x941D8 BNE). The
independence of the two halves is tested directly (open=0, dirty=1 still blits four). PsiScreen_Draw runs with
the four panels NULL and dwActionFail clear, so its rails, its pad and its two geoscape buttons run while the
shortfall panel does not (0x72A94..0x72AD4); the arm's controls are the third and fourth recorded blits. Both
arms are also run with apCtl NULL, which leaves only the callee's blits.

Part 19 -- the soldier arms 0x92DAC..0x92EE4 and 0x92EE4..0x9309C, ported as Geoscape_DrawSoldierArm and Geoscape_DrawSoldierEditArm (src/pufo/game/pufo_geoscape.c).

Case 4 (screen 4, the soldier list). It is the only pair of arms that POSITIONS a control: 0x92DB0 STRH #0xE0 and 0x92DC8 STRH #1 write x=224, y=1 through the g_pUiCloseCtl global (0x92DB8 / 0x92DC4), before the draw at 0x92DD0. R0 = the block base 0x159768 (0x92DCC MOV R0,R5), so the callee gets the whole soldier block: its pad 0x1598D4, the names panel 0x15975C, the craft panel 0x159DEC, the open byte 0x159DE0 and the cursor 0x159E08. Then the control run (0x92DE0..0x92DFC, CMP #2 at 0x92DF8) over the block's +0x148 pair 0x1598B0 / 0x1598B4, then the close control at 0x92E04, then three captions, then B def_8C1B0.

Case 5 (screen 5, the soldier name editor) is the ONLY arm whose draw/control ORDER depends on a gate. It blits the block's pad word first (0x92EE8 LDR / 0x92EEC), writes the same (224,1) position (0x92EF4 / 0x92F00), and branches on bTransferFlag @ 0x159E10 (LDRB at 0x92F10, BEQ at 0x92F18). Armed: the close control moves again to (198,77) (0x92F20 STRH #0xC6 / 0x92F28 STRH #0x4D), SoldierScreen_Draw runs FIRST (0x92F38), the three +0x150 controls run after it (0x92F48..0x92F64, CMP #3), and three centred captions follow. Unarmed: the three controls run first (0x93070..0x9308C, CMP #3 at 0x93088), SoldierScreen_Draw runs AFTER them (0x93094), and no text call exists on this path. Both paths land on 0x93054, the close-control blit.

The controls are Geoscape_BuildNavControls' own installs (0x67C70, 0x67C8C for the pair; 0x67D00, 0x67D14, 0x67D24 for the triple): SoldierScreen_PanelPrev / PanelNext and SoldierScreen_FindNextAtBase / FindPrevAtBase / Ui_SetTransferFlag. The third is what arms bTransferFlag, so the flag that reorders this arm is set by a control this arm blits.

The centring. 0x92E48..0x92E58, 0x92FB0..0x92FC0 and the shared tail 0x92ACC..0x92ADC all spell MOVS R1,R0 / ADDMI R1,R1,#1 / MOV R1,R1,ASR#1 / RSB R1,R1,#centre. ADDMI fires only on a NEGATIVE width, so the half-width is floor(w/2) -- the +1 is a negative-number correction, not a round-up. x = centre - (w >> 1). The port has Geoscape_CentredX for it. Rounding down is not visible: an odd w centres exactly, an even w is half a pixel left.

Centres and records, from the RSB immediates and the ADD offsets over the 205-byte TEXTS stride: case 4 TEXTS[71] (0xB71AB) on 120 at y 26, TEXTS[88] (0xB7F48) at (38,50), TEXTS[89] (0xB38D0+0x4745 = 0xB8015) at (170,50); case 5 TEXTS[90] (0xB80E2) on 104 at y 38 -- the same "Armour" caption SoldierScreen_DrawDetail uses -- TEXTS[91] (0xB81AF) on 90 at y 80 and TEXTS[92] (0xB827C) on 170 at y 80. Each caption follows a Gfx_PackRgb565Pair, and case 4 ends with a third pair (255,200,20 / 10,10,10) that no text in the arm draws with: the arm leaves that colour for the next drawing user. Ported as it is.

Tests (TestGeoscapeSoldierArms, 33 checks). SoldierScreen_Draw is observed through its seam: with nGeoscapeScreen at 5 the callee IS the caller's pfnTextInput (0x652A4..0x652B0), and the hook records g_nPnBlits at the moment it runs -- 0 in case 4 and in armed case 5, 3 in unarmed case 5. That is the only way the ARM's own order becomes visible, because the soldier callee blits no control of its own; the seam also pins the argument (nSoldierCursor). With the screen id at 4 and the open byte set the real callee runs instead and its rails and pad are checked on the surface; with the open byte clear it draws nothing (0x652CC), which is what makes the caption comparison clean. Caption claims are pixel-VALUE comparisons against a reference the test builds: pack the claimed pair, draw the record at the claimed centred x and y, and compare every surface pixel. A wrong centre, y, record or colour pair differs; the mutant that rounds the half-width up was caught by 694 differing pixels, so the floor rounding is pinned by the odd-width records. Close-control positions are asserted as fields (224,1 vs 198,77), the blit lists as pad identities.
